title: Night Nine
adaptation_status: Complete playable English adaptation: a storybook backstory and playable prologue, ten chapters with two interludes and two flashbacks, a storybook epilogue and the final signal.

greeting.title: Why did I hear the same greeting twice?

theories.text: Dad’s old recorder is printing one tape onto the other.
I was tired and heard a match that was never there.
Since the boat, I may be reading too much into ordinary things.
Someone else has been using Nora’s name.

aquarium.title: What happened in the north wing?

theories.text: The work order was an ordinary repair with the wrong date on it.
The woman on that tape might still be alive somewhere.

town.title: How can June and I test a suspicion?

theories.text: A change in someone’s habits could identify a copy.
A fresh private fact, or a dated record that puts someone in two places, could tell us more.

meridian.title: What is really at Sentinel Point?

theories.text: Meridian runs a world-changing engine on very little power.
Meridian’s engine may not be what the press releases say.

rook.title: What does Rook know about June?

theories.text: Only June’s old friend could know the right words.
Someone else could be playing the performance on her voicemail.

boat.title: Why did Mom and Dad go out that night?

theories.text: They only wanted company on the water.
They went out to find the signal Dad was tracking.

iris.title: Why did she let me leave?

theories.text: She can only repeat what Nora would have done.
She can make a choice Nora never made.
She is exactly who she seems: a retired teacher who gets around.
Someone else has been selling bait on the pier.

signing.title: Where could a substitution take place?

theories.text: We only need to watch the podium.
The swap would happen between the hatch and the podium, out of sight.

choir.title: What is making the tune inside the ship?

theories.text: I am hearing a familiar tune in ordinary ship noise.
Something on the ship holds people’s memories, and sings them.

broadcast.title: How can the fleet test our performance?

theories.text: We could replay the old Meridian test over the tower.
We could answer every cue live, through the ship’s own equipment.

scenes.title: The bay is singing
scenes.objective: Help Frank find the hum hiding under his radio static.

tasks.title: Frank’s radio
tasks.prompt: Drag the dial until both stations fade, switch on Narrow bandwidth, then record what is left.
options: Tune between the stations and narrow the band
tasks.note: K7BLW log, eleven-oh-four. Eight-fifteen, narrow band. Not one tone. Several, holding the same note.
hints: Drag the dial toward the middle, away from both stations.
The hum sits in a quiet gap between the two stations. Narrow bandwidth shuts out their edges.
Stop where both stations are at their faintest, in the low 800s. Switch on Narrow bandwidth before you record.
tasks.goal: Find the hum between the two stations.
tasks.background: Frank has tracked a hum under his radio static for months. It comes every ninth night, and out on the water it is louder. Two stations crowd the band: a time signal on one side, a chime on the other.

tasks.title: Helen’s phone
tasks.prompt: Where should Helen hold the phone while she leaves Steve a message?
options: Up in the wind, away from the radio
Inside her coat, out of the spray
tasks.note: Eleven-twenty. Helen called the boy. Held the phone to my speaker, so he gets the hum along with her.
hints: The phone has to hear the radio, not just Helen.
Which spot is closest to the sound she wants Steve to hear?
The phone should sit as close as it can to the sound Helen wants Steve to hear, not to Helen.
tasks.goal: Get the hum onto Steve’s voicemail.
tasks.background: Steve stayed ashore for his shift at KBWR. Helen wants him to hear this for himself, but her phone’s little microphone won’t pick up the radio from across the boat.

wrong.1: The wind would swallow everything but her voice.
wrong.2: Warm and dry, but all he’d hear is wool.

shots.direction: Drift beside the rowboat as turquoise light grows beneath black water.
Move toward the active interaction.

chapter.title: The Bay Is Singing
chapter.goal: Frank and Helen Mercer row out to listen to the bay.

scenes.coach: Click the glowing radio to begin. Press I for a list of things to look at.
scenes.when: Eighteen months ago, a little after eleven at night
scenes.next: Black. The storybook “Eighteen months” plays, then Chapter 1.
notes: Mix a faint low hum (the ship) under the voicemail recording.voicemail. Chapter 1 depends on hearing it there.

scenes.title: Good Morning, Sleepyhead
scenes.objective: Test Dad’s old recorder before you move Mom’s voicemail to a fresh tape.

tasks.title: The red cassette
tasks.prompt: Saturday morning. What should the red cassette catch at a quarter past seven?
options: The KBWR station ident on the kitchen radio
Steve reading the same sentence aloud
tasks.note: Red cassette, Saturday, 7:15. My ident, AutoRick, Nora saying good morning on her way out, and me.
hints: Steve needs a sound that is identical every time it plays.
A person never does anything exactly the same way twice. A recording does.
Only one of the three sounds comes off a station cart, exactly the same every morning.
tasks.goal: Catch something on tape that never changes.
tasks.background: To time Dad’s recorder, Steve needs a sound that is exactly the same every time it plays. The kitchen radio is tuned to KBWR, where AutoRick plays Steve’s twelve-second station ident at 7:15 every morning.

wrong.1: My voice changes every time I open my mouth. A reference can’t change.
wrong.2: Nora grinds the beans differently every day. That’s sort of the point of Nora.

tasks.title: The blue cassette
tasks.prompt: Sunday, 7:14. How should Steve set up the blue cassette?
options: Same spot on the table, same level, record at 7:15
Next to the radio, so the ident comes out louder
Wait and record the noon news instead
tasks.note: Blue cassette, Sunday, 7:15. The ident, the radio, Nora and me, all over again. Now I can time the machine.
hints: Repeat Saturday’s test exactly.
Anything that changes besides the day spoils the comparison.
Two of the setups move something besides the day: the distance, or the sound itself.
tasks.goal: Record the second reference exactly like the first.
tasks.background: A fair test changes one thing only: the day. If anything else moves, the recorder, the volume or the time, a difference on the tape could come from that instead.

wrong.1: Then a difference could just be the distance. Change one thing, and only one.
wrong.2: The news is new every day. Only the ident repeats.

tasks.title: Two mornings, side by side
tasks.prompt: Slide Sunday until the two idents line up. Then play both tapes and compare every voice on them.
options: Similar delivery with a new breath
tasks.note: The ident matches, so the recorder is fine. AutoRick and I change from day to day, like anyone would. Nora’s good morning matches perfectly. People don’t do that. Recordings do.

puzzle.instruction: First line up the ident. Then listen to each voice on both tapes and say how the two days compare.

rows.label: The ident
options: Same words, said a new way

rows.label: AutoRick
options: Same words, said a new way

rows.label: Steve: Morning, Nor.
options: Same words, said a new way

rows.label: Nora: Good morning, sleepyhead.
options: Same words, said a new way

hints: Line up the end of the ident first. Then play both tapes together.
AutoRick reads a new script every day. A person says the same words a little differently each time.
Only a recording repeats every breath and click. Compare each voice with the ident.

tasks.goal: Line the two cassettes up on the ident and time Dad’s recorder.
tasks.background: Steve puts the red cassette in one ear and the blue in the other. If the recorder runs true, the two idents will line up. The tapes also caught the rest of the kitchen: AutoRick on the radio, Nora on her way out, and Steve himself.
hints: Line up the end of the ident first. Then play both tapes together.
AutoRick reads a new script every day. A person says the same words a little differently each time.

tasks.title: Dad’s recorder
tasks.prompt: Steve says “one, two” twice onto the blue cassette, and a chair squeaks only during the second pass. On playback the squeak is there once, and nothing of Saturday plays underneath. Which explanation can he cross out?
options: The blue tape carried Saturday’s sound over
I was tired and heard a match that was never there
Since the boat, I’ve been reading too much into ordinary things
tasks.note: Crossed out: the tape. It holds only what happened in the room. That leaves my ears, my grief, or Nora.
hints: Which explanation is about the machine?
A tape carrying old sound would play Saturday underneath, or repeat the first pass. It did neither.
A ghost of Saturday would sound like Saturday. Did anything from Saturday play under the test?
tasks.goal: Rule out the most boring explanation first.
tasks.background: Steve’s notebook rule: list every explanation, then cross them out, starting with the dull ones. Dad reused his cassettes for years. An old tape can carry a ghost of an earlier recording.

wrong.1: The squeak tests the tape, not my ears. Tiredness stays on the list for now.
wrong.2: The squeak says nothing about grief. It’s about the tape. That one stays on the list too.

shots.direction: Move from a dark reel-to-reel recorder toward amber kitchen light.
Move toward the active interaction.

chapter.title: Good Morning, Sleepyhead
chapter.when: Saturday the 20th, three in the morning
chapter.goal: Steve wants to save his mother’s last voicemail before the tape wears out.

scenes.title: Sunday on the pier
scenes.objective: Spend the afternoon on the pier with Nora.

tasks.title: Admiral’s whistle
tasks.prompt: Steve is worried Admiral might be sick. How can he give Admiral a fair chance to answer her?
options: Wait until the winch stops and Admiral surfaces, then ask Nora to whistle again
Toss Admiral the rest of the sandwich
tasks.note: Admiral hears fine. He came to my clumsy whistle and turned away from Nora’s. Her second note went down. It always used to go up.
hints: What else could keep Admiral from hearing her?
Take away the winch and the water before you trust the result.
A fair test removes every excuse: the noise, and the water between them. Then Nora gets another try.
tasks.goal: Give Admiral a fair chance to hear Nora’s whistle.
tasks.background: Admiral has come to Nora’s two-note whistle since the day she bottle-fed him. He steals food from everybody else. Right now he is underwater, and the harbor winch is roaring.

wrong.1: That only tests whether he likes rye. He doesn’t, and he’d eat it anyway.
wrong.2: Then he’d be answering me. I want to know if he hears her.

tasks.title: Deputy Lyle
tasks.prompt: Lyle Boone has never apologized for anything. What does Steve ask him?
options: “Since when do you make their games?”
“Who are you, and what have you done with Lyle?”
tasks.note: Lyle Boone has gone to every game since June. Before that he missed them all. And he apologized to me.
hints: A change only matters once you know when it happened.
Lyle will happily tell Steve about his new habit. Ask how long he’s had it.
Lyle loves talking about his boys. A question about when the new habit started gets a date, not a fight.
tasks.goal: Put a date on Lyle’s change of heart.
tasks.background: Deputy Lyle Boone took the missing-persons report on Steve’s parents and never called him back. Since his divorce he has missed most of his sons’ games. Dad’s rule: put a date on everything.

wrong.1: That’s an accusation. He’d close up, and I’d learn nothing.
wrong.2: He’d laugh, I’d laugh, and I’d learn nothing. Put a date on it.

tasks.title: Agnes’s bait stall
tasks.prompt: Every sound has a source. Is the low note Agnes, or something else?
options: Ask which part of the bay she hears it from
Ask when she learned the melody
Ask whether she hums it in the shop
tasks.note: The low note comes from the water, under the floating dock. Agnes only hums along. June heard it without her. And it is the note under Mom’s voicemail.
hints: Start with June. What did she hear, and where was she?
A sound that stops early can’t be making a note that keeps going.
June never heard Agnes, but she heard the note by the water. Where does that put the note?

puzzle.instruction: Agnes keeps a tide book in her bait tin. Help her answer four questions about the low note.
evidence: June was in the fish-shed line. She heard the low note before Agnes started humming.
June could not hear Agnes from the fish shed.
June heard the note best by the water, under the floating dock.
The winch stopped halfway through the note. The note kept going.

stages.prompt: Put one card on each question.
slots: Where does the low note come from?
What stopped before the note did?
Who heard the note without Agnes?

rows.label: Where does the low note come from?
What stopped before the note did?
Who heard the note without Agnes?

tasks.goal: Work out where the low note is coming from.
tasks.background: Mrs. Agnes Penhallow taught Steve in third grade. She is ninety-one and sells bait that nobody buys. Today a low note is drifting in off the water, and she is humming along. Steve knows that note. It is under Mom’s voicemail.

scenes.title: A plate kept warm
scenes.objective: Have dinner with Nora’s family, and listen to the people who know her best.

tasks.title: Carmen’s photo strip
tasks.prompt: Steve puts a date on everything. What can he write down for certain?
options: Nora was at La Marea at 20:04, 20:15 and 20:29; Mateo drove her in at noon, and Rafa drove her home at midnight
Nora never left the restaurant all day
tasks.note: Carmen’s birthday: Nora at La Marea at 20:04, 20:15 and 20:29. Mateo drove her in at noon. Rafa drove her home at midnight.
hints: Separate what the photos show from what anyone assumes.
Each photo fixes one moment. The two rides fix the start and the end.
Keep only what has a time stamp or a witness behind it.
tasks.goal: Write down where Nora was on Carmen’s birthday, and who saw her.
tasks.background: Carmen photographs everything, mostly food, and her camera stamps the time on every picture. Nora is in three of last month’s birthday photos: 20:04, 20:15 with the kitchen check in her hand, and 20:29.

wrong.1: The photos cover twenty-five minutes. Mateo and Rafa cover the ends. Nobody watched her every minute.
wrong.2: She’s smiling in every picture. Smiles don’t come with timestamps.

tasks.title: When did she change?
tasks.prompt: Nora changed after her last argument and before the first time she simply agreed. Bracket it.
options: Nora has forgotten how the dish used to taste
Two witnesses noticed a change worth following
They know when and why Nora changed her mind
tasks.note: Nora stopped arguing with her family between the end of May and the first Sunday in June. Lyle changed in June too. I was on nights. I never noticed.
hints: Look for the latest argument and the earliest agreement.
Tomás’s call came before Mateo’s fight. Carmen’s birthday came long after Rafa’s mole.
Put the dates in order: May 17, Memorial Day weekend, the first Sunday in June, Carmen’s birthday in September. The change sits in one gap.
tasks.goal: Narrow down when Nora changed.
tasks.background: Steve worked nights all spring and summer. He can’t say when Nora changed, because he had stopped looking. Her brothers can. Each of them remembers a last argument or a first surprise.

puzzle.instruction: Pick the last argument anyone remembers. Then pick the first time she just agreed.

rows.label: Last argument anyone remembers
options: Mateo’s driving fight, Memorial Day weekend

tasks.title: Tomás’s field reels
tasks.prompt: Tomás will lend Steve his field reels if Steve can file them back by date. If the hum keeps a schedule, the dates will show it.
options: The episodes arranged by broadcast date
The field reels with their original labels
An undated compilation of the clearest hums
tasks.note: Tomás’s loud nights come every nine nights: September 24, October 3, October 12. The next one is tonight.
hints: Where was the buoy on October 3? Could it ring that night?
Count the nights from one date to the next. September has thirty days.
September 24 to October 3 is the same count as October 3 to October 12. Add that count once more.

puzzle.instruction: Match each reel to its date. Then count the nights between dates to find the next loud night.
evidence: September 24: the bell buoy was in the water, ringing at low tide.
October 3: the buoy was ashore for repair, with a cracked clapper. It could not ring.
October 12: the repair crew tapped the buoy twice, then put it back in the water.
Each reel starts with whatever was making noise when Tomás pressed record.
Tomás only goes out on the nights the hum is loudest. September has thirty days.

stages.prompt: Match each date to the first sound on its reel.
Count the nights between the dates. When is the next loud night?

tasks.goal: Find out whether the hum in the bay keeps a schedule.
tasks.background: Nora’s brother Tomás, twenty-nine, has said for three years that something is hiding in the bay. Nobody listens, Steve included. His podcast is cut up for drama, but his field reels are dated in pencil, and he only goes out on the nights the hum is loudest.

Queue the release and restart the motor with the stair lit
Try the thumb pad with the motor running

tasks.title: Nora’s irises
tasks.prompt: There is one way out.
options: Climb along the rail toward the stair
tasks.note: Nora watched Steve go and did nothing to stop him.
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Climb along the rail toward the stair.
tasks.goal: Get to the communal stair.
tasks.background: The shared rail runs past Nora’s pots of irises to Mr. Bell’s open gate and the lit stair. The crash brings Nora to the balcony door.

scenes.title: The Aquarium Is Closed
scenes.objective: Get into the sealed north wing. The work order says Nora signed something there.

tasks.title: The old exhibit plan
tasks.prompt: The old plan and the newer notice disagree. Which route still reaches the north wing?
options: Reach the outgoing pump route from the service entrance
Trace an incoming pipe back toward the pump
tasks.note: The way in runs from the service door through the pump room, along the only pipe that carries water away.

puzzle.instruction: Trust the newer notice. Door 1 is bricked up, so the visitor hall goes nowhere. The service door opens into the pump room. Pump arrows: pipe N flows in, pipe E flows out, pipe S flows in.
hints: Where the old plan and the new notice disagree, trust the notice.
Door 1 is bricked up, so the visitor hall is a dead end. Which entrance skips the visitor hall?
In the pump room, look for the one arrow that points away from the pump.
Where the old plan and the new notice disagree, trust the notice.
Door 1 is bricked up, so the visitor hall is a dead end. Which entrance skips the visitor hall?
In the pump room, look for the one arrow that points away from the pump.
tasks.goal: Find a way into the sealed north wing.
tasks.background: The north wing has been closed to the public for two years. On the old plan, the café and the public tank lead to the visitor hall, and door 1 goes from there to the north wing. A newer notice taped over the plan says door 1 is bricked up. The service door opens into the pump room, which has three pipes.

tasks.title: Two service doors
tasks.prompt: Steve records six seconds at each door. Which corridor can he cross without meeting anyone?
options: Wait for both doors to go silent
tasks.note: The filter corridor plays a loop: the same bell and the same cough on the same beat. Nobody’s there. The pump corridor has real footsteps.
hints: Look for a sound that repeats on the same beat.
Compare the spacing and shape of the peaks in each six-second strip.
Watch the bell and the cough. In one strip they come back on exactly the same beat. Nobody coughs on a schedule.
tasks.goal: Pick the corridor with nobody in it.
tasks.background: Steve hears a voice and footsteps behind each door. On Sunday morning, Nora’s good morning played twice, exactly the same. Since then he knows how to tell a person from a recording: a recording repeats exactly, and a person never does.

wrong.0: Those footsteps change their spacing. Somebody real is walking that corridor.
wrong.2: Neither door goes quiet. One of them never will, because it’s on a loop.

tasks.title: Nora’s coat and the intercom tape
tasks.prompt: Nora’s voice, Nora’s whistle, and a date on the spool. What does the tape tell Steve?
options: File the intact spool and its marked leader
Keep the two notes alone with a new date label
Copy the name only and discard the leader
tasks.note: The real Nora recorded this here on May 29. Someone else has been living her life with me for five months. Her whistle rises. The one Admiral ignored falls.
hints: Start with the date on the spool. Then count the months to tonight.
Count the months from late May to late October, one at a time.
Admiral comes to Nora’s real whistle. On the pier he turned away from a whistle whose second note fell.

tasks.goal: Work out what Nora’s tape means.

tasks.title: The open channel
tasks.prompt: The Archivist wants a witness who has lived on shore with these people. Who can speak for life in Bellwether?
options: The Archivist, reading her departure register
Her shore echo, with last winter’s credit ledger
Mrs. Penhallow, still waking up in row three
tasks.note: My echo stood behind the bait counter last winter and let the boats pay in spring. I remember the wind. She remembers the people. I will let her win.
hints: Who has actually lived on shore?
The register is nine hundred years old, and the real Agnes has been asleep for three years.
A witness to life on shore has to have lived it, last winter, behind the bait counter.
tasks.goal: Find a witness to life on shore.
tasks.background: A report to the fleet needs the word of the Prefect or the Archivist. Saren refuses. To confirm it, the Archivist must break every law she has kept for nine hundred years, and she wants a witness first. Her shore echo has sold bait on the pier for three years. Last winter, when the boats came in empty, she let the fishermen pay in spring. The real Agnes slept in row three the whole time.

wrong.0: The register is nine hundred years old. It knows nothing about Bellwether.

Keep it sealed to protect Saren’s reputation
Claim Earth is the only possible home
tasks.note: Reach 2: water, air and three separate surveys of empty ground. The Prefect found a home for the fleet and sealed it, because a home would have ended his mission.
hints: The fleet needs water, air and room to settle.
A beacon that answers every call means somebody already lives there. A world with no water can’t take the fleet.

The survey is about a place. The ledger is about people.

tasks.title: The new signal
tasks.prompt: Three in the morning. A real signal from deep space: two joined tones, the second climbing, a gap, then one long tone lower than both. Helen has three pages open.
options: Page 12: two joined strokes rising, a gap, one long low stroke
Page 4: one long stroke, a gap, two joined strokes falling
tasks.note: Translated the first reply from deep space.
hints: Follow the shape: joined, climbing, a gap, then low.
You heard Wick sing this shape in Row Zero.
It is the same shape Helen copied onto her last page from Frank’s Reel 11.
tasks.goal: Recognize the shape of the reply.
tasks.background: Helen copied Wick’s phrase onto the last page of her notebook from Frank’s tapes, and followed it in Row Zero. Wick sent a message home to Tirel.

wrong.0: Three separate strokes. Nothing is joined, and nothing climbs.

p_bay.in.01.speaker: frank
p_bay.in.01.text: Nine nights since the last one, Helen. Same interval. Louder out here. Whatever it is, it keeps better time than I do.

p_bay.in.02.speaker: helen
p_bay.in.02.text: Steve would hear more in this than both of us put together. I’ll leave him a message.

p_bay.tune.01.speaker: frank
p_bay.tune.01.text: There you are. Hear that, Helen? More than one voice, all holding the same note.

p_bay.tune.find.speaker: frank
p_bay.tune.find.text: K7BLW log, eleven-oh-four. Eight-fifteen, narrow band. Not one tone. Several, holding the same note.

p_bay.message.01.speaker: helen
p_bay.message.01.text: He should hear this for himself. There. Now he’ll tell us we recorded it wrong.

p_bay.message.find.speaker: frank
p_bay.message.find.text: Eleven-twenty. Helen called the boy. Held the phone to my speaker, so he gets the hum along with her.

p_bay.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: frank
p_bay.talk.helen.1.01.text: Think the boy will come out with us next time?

p_bay.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: helen
p_bay.talk.helen.1.02.text: He’ll say he has a shift. Then he’ll call tomorrow and ask what we heard.

p_bay.talk.helen.1.04.speaker: helen
p_bay.talk.helen.1.04.text: He’s your son, Frank. He can’t leave a sound alone.

p_bay.talk.helen.2.02.speaker: frank
p_bay.talk.helen.2.02.text: Gloves are in the tackle box. Under the logbook.

p_bay.talk.helen.2.03.speaker: helen
p_bay.talk.helen.2.03.text: Of course they are. Everything in this boat is under the logbook.

p_bay.talk.helen.3.01.speaker: helen
p_bay.talk.helen.3.01.text: Listen. It goes up at the end, like a question.

p_bay.talk.helen.3.02.speaker: frank
p_bay.talk.helen.3.02.text: Then write it down. Time, place, what it does.

p_bay.talk.helen.3.03.speaker: helen
p_bay.talk.helen.3.03.text: Eleven-oh-five. Rowboat. It sounds like it’s waiting for someone.

p_bay.recap.01.speaker: frank
p_bay.recap.01.text: Eleven-forty. The note is climbing. Helen says it has a shape, like speech. We’re going to follow it out.

p_bay.out.01.speaker: helen
p_bay.out.01.text: Come out with us, kiddo. The bay is singing tonight.

c1_flat.in.01.speaker: helen
c1_flat.in.01.text: Come out with us, kiddo. The bay is singing tonight.

c1_flat.in.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.02.text: Three in the morning. Again. Well, Mom, it’s a fine night for it.

c1_flat.in.05.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.05.text: Your tape’s wearing thin, Mom. I’ll move you to a fresh one. Just as soon as Dad’s recorder runs true.

c1_flat.in.06.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.06.text: Dad’s recorder runs slow. Old belts. Everyone on it sounds a little sleepy.

c1_flat.in.07.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.07.text: There’s an easy test. KBWR still plays my old station ident at a quarter past seven every morning. I made that ident. It runs exactly twelve seconds.

c1_flat.in.08.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.08.text: Record it two mornings running. If it lasts twelve seconds both times, the machine runs true.

c1_flat.in.03.speaker: autorick
c1_flat.in.03.text: Good morning, Bellwether! Yesterday will be sunny.

c1_flat.saturday.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.saturday.01.text: Saturday, kitchen, quarter past seven. Dad always said to put the date on everything.

c1_flat.saturday.03.speaker: iris
c1_flat.saturday.03.text: Coffee’s on the stove. I made it strong, the way you like it.

c1_flat.saturday.05.speaker: iris
c1_flat.saturday.05.text: Strong is fine. Whatever you like.

c1_flat.saturday.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.saturday.find.text: Red cassette, Saturday, 7:15. My ident, AutoRick, Nora saying good morning on her way out, and me.

c1_flat.sunday.03.speaker: autorick
c1_flat.sunday.03.text: The voice of the coast, now with zero humans!

c1_flat.sunday.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.sunday.02.text: Morning, Nor. Blue tape, Sunday. Date on everything, Dad.

c1_flat.sunday.04.speaker: iris
c1_flat.sunday.04.text: I’m off to feed Admiral and the otters. Back by noon.

c1_flat.sunday.05.speaker: steve
c1_flat.sunday.05.text: On a Sunday? You used to fight for every Sunday off.

c1_flat.sunday.06.speaker: iris
c1_flat.sunday.06.text: The animals don’t know it’s Sunday, sleepyhead.

c1_flat.sunday.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.sunday.find.text: Blue cassette, Sunday, 7:15. The ident, the radio, Nora and me, all over again. Now I can time the machine.

c1_flat.compare.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.01.text: Twelve seconds, both days. Dad’s recorder runs true.

c1_flat.compare.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.02.text: And Nora... lines up too. The breath. The little click before “morning.”

c1_flat.compare.03.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.03.text: Nobody says a sentence the same way twice. I spent twelve years listening for exactly that.

c1_flat.compare.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.compare.find.text: The ident matches, so the recorder is fine. AutoRick and I change from day to day, like anyone would. Nora’s good morning matches perfectly. People don’t do that. Recordings do.

c1_flat.out.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.out.02.text: I need evidence. Being afraid of something doesn’t make it true.

c1_flat.control.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.lead.01.text: Let’s not panic yet. Let’s make a list.

c1_flat.control.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.01.text: Testing. One, two. Testing... one, two.

c1_flat.control.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.02.text: The squeak made the second pass only. Nothing of Saturday underneath. So the tape is clean. Cross that one out.

c1_flat.control.find.speaker: steve
c1_flat.control.find.text: Crossed out: the tape. It holds only what happened in the room. That leaves my ears, my grief, or Nora.

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.01.text: Want some toast before you go?

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.02.text: I ate already. There’s fruit in the blue bowl.

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.03.text: Since when do you eat breakfast?

c1_flat.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris
c1_flat.talk.iris.1.04.text: For a while now. It’s good for you.

c1_flat.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: iris
c1_flat.talk.iris.2.02.text: Growing. One of them bit a volunteer again. Only a little.

c1_flat.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: steve
c1_flat.talk.iris.2.03.text: You used to say that was her best quality.

c1_flat.talk.iris.2.04.speaker: iris
c1_flat.talk.iris.2.04.text: She’s a good otter. They’re all good otters.

c1_flat.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: iris
c1_flat.talk.iris.3.01.text: I heard the new radio host this morning. He sounds cheerful.

c1_flat.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.talk.iris.3.02.text: He read yesterday’s weather again. Twelve years at that desk, and they replaced me with him.

c1_flat.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: iris
c1_flat.talk.iris.3.03.text: Then you have more time at home. That’s nice, isn’t it?

c1_flat.talk.iris.4.03.speaker: steve
c1_flat.talk.iris.4.03.text: You used to kick the blankets off every night. Every single night.

c1_flat.talk.iris.4.04.speaker: iris
c1_flat.talk.iris.4.04.text: Did I? I don’t remember that.

c1_flat.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_flat.recap.01.text: Dad’s recorder runs true, and the tape is clean. And the woman I love said good morning twice, the way a cassette would.

c1_flat.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_flat.recap.02.text: I tried to remember our last real conversation. I couldn’t. Before the boat, she never said anything the same way twice.

c1_flat.out.03.speaker: steve
c1_flat.out.03.text: Nor? Walk the pier with me this afternoon? Like we used to. We could say hi to Admiral.

c1_flat.out.05.speaker: iris
c1_flat.out.05.text: And Mamá kept your plate warm again. Dinner at six, if you want.

c1_pier.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.01.text: Sunday on the harbor. The crab boats were in, the winch was hauling pots onto the dock, and the fish shed had a line out the door.

c1_pier.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.02.text: Every Sunday, Nora visits Admiral, the sea lion she raised from a rescued pup. I used to come along.

c1_pier.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.03.text: I hadn’t, in a long time.

c1_pier.ctx.04.speaker: steve
c1_pier.ctx.04.text: Sheriff June Calder was in that fish-shed line, the way she is every Sunday. Mrs. Penhallow sat at her bait stall, where nobody ever buys anything.

c1_pier.in.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.in.01.text: Admiral! That was my lunch. You’re six hundred pounds of sea lion, and you don’t even like rye.

c1_pier.whistle.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.lead.01.text: Your whistle, Nor. He always comes for that.

c1_pier.whistle.lead.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.lead.03.text: He didn’t even come up. The winch is going. He probably didn’t hear you.

c1_pier.whistle.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.02.text: Nothing. He’s looking right at you.

c1_pier.whistle.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.03.text: ...He came for me. I can’t even whistle.

c1_pier.whistle.04.speaker: iris
c1_pier.whistle.04.text: He wants the rest of your sandwich.

c1_pier.whistle.find.speaker: steve
c1_pier.whistle.find.text: Admiral hears fine. He came to my clumsy whistle and turned away from Nora’s. Her second note went down. It always used to go up.

c1_pier.door.lead.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.door.lead.01.text: Steve. I owe you an apology. When your folks went missing, I never called you back. That wasn’t right.

c1_pier.door.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.door.01.text: They’re both pitching today. I promised I’d watch every inning.

c1_pier.door.03.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.door.03.text: Every one since June. Haven’t missed one. Ask the boys.

c1_pier.door.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.door.02.text: Deputy Lyle, keeping a promise. I should write that down before the world ends.

c1_pier.door.find.speaker: steve
c1_pier.door.find.text: Lyle Boone has gone to every game since June. Before that he missed them all. And he apologized to me.

c1_pier.in.02.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.in.02.text: Fish don’t sing, Steven. Something under them does.

c1_pier.bait.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.bait.lead.01.text: That note. It’s under Mom’s voicemail. I always thought it was the phone line.

c1_pier.bait.lead.02.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.bait.lead.02.text: It’s loud today, Steven. It always is, on certain nights.

c1_pier.bait.lead.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.bait.lead.03.text: June! Did you hear that hum just now?

c1_pier.bait.lead.04.speaker: calder
c1_pier.bait.lead.04.text: From the fish-shed line. It started before Agnes did.

c1_pier.bait.lead.05.speaker: calder
c1_pier.bait.lead.05.text: It was loudest down by the water, under the floating dock.

c1_pier.bait.lead.06.speaker: steve
c1_pier.bait.lead.06.text: Could you hear Agnes humming from there?

c1_pier.bait.lead.07.speaker: calder
c1_pier.bait.lead.07.text: Nobody can hear Agnes hum. She’s quieter than the fog.

c1_pier.bait.lead.08.speaker: steve
c1_pier.bait.lead.08.text: And the winch stopped halfway through. The note just kept going.

c1_pier.bait.01.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.bait.01.text: Count the nights, Steven. And when you record them, leave room for the loud parts.

c1_pier.bait.find.speaker: steve
c1_pier.bait.find.text: The low note comes from the water, under the floating dock. Agnes only hums along. June heard it without her. And it is the note under Mom’s voicemail.

c1_pier.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris
c1_pier.talk.iris.1.02.text: Nine. He weighs more than your car.

c1_pier.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.talk.iris.1.03.text: You bottle-fed him in our bathtub. For three weeks.

c1_pier.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris
c1_pier.talk.iris.1.04.text: I remember. It was a good bathtub.

c1_pier.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris
c1_pier.talk.iris.2.01.text: The line is long today. The crab boats came in early.

c1_pier.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.talk.iris.2.02.text: You used to talk your way to the front of that line.

c1_pier.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris
c1_pier.talk.iris.2.03.text: Waiting is fine. Everyone gets a turn.

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.01.text: You still whistle for him every Sunday?

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: iris
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.02.text: Every Sunday. Two notes. He always comes.

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.03.text: You used to say he’d come to that whistle through a hurricane.

c1_pier.talk.iris.3.04.speaker: iris
c1_pier.talk.iris.3.04.text: Then you should visit him more often, sleepyhead.

c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.02.text: Splendid. Nobody has bought a thing since Tuesday.

c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.04.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.talk.agnes.1.04.text: It means the fish are safe, Steven. Somebody has to be on their side.

c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.01.text: You still remember me from third grade?

c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.02.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.02.text: You took my classroom clock apart to find the tick.

c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.04.speaker: agnes
c1_pier.talk.agnes.2.04.text: With two pieces left over. It ran fast ever after.

c1_pier.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder
c1_pier.talk.calder.1.02.text: Every Sunday for twenty years. My mother bought it in this same line.

c1_pier.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c1_pier.talk.calder.1.03.text: Some things in this town don’t change. I like that about it.

c1_pier.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.talk.calder.2.01.text: Is that Lyle by the shed? In a clean shirt?

c1_pier.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: calder
c1_pier.talk.calder.2.02.text: He asked for every Sunday off this summer. For his boys’ games.

c1_pier.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder
c1_pier.talk.calder.2.03.text: Since early summer he’s been my best deputy. Never late once. I keep waiting for the catch.

c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.text: My oldest, then his brother. I’ll be in the stands for every inning.

c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.speaker: lyle_copy
c1_pier.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.text: I made them a promise. I keep my promises now.

c1_pier.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell
c1_pier.talk.pell.1.02.text: Every route runs on schedule, Mr. Mercer.

c1_pier.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_pier.recap.01.text: Admiral turned away from Nora’s whistle. Lyle Boone apologized to me. And the bay is humming the note that has been under Mom’s voice for eighteen months.

c1_pier.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.recap.02.text: One odd thing is an accident. Three is a list.

c1_pier.recap.03.speaker: steve
c1_pier.recap.03.text: Dinner at La Marea was at six. Carmen has kept my plate warm every Sunday since the boat. She throws it out every Monday.

c1_pier.out.01.speaker: pell
c1_pier.out.01.text: Your parents’ mail, Mr. Mercer. Delivered precisely on schedule.

c1_pier.out.02.speaker: steve
c1_pier.out.02.text: They haven’t been home in eighteen months, Dale. You know that.

c1_dinner.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.ctx.01.text: La Marea. The Reyes family restaurant, and for four years my Sunday table.

c1_dinner.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.ctx.02.text: Luis still keeps Dad’s old chair at the bar. Nobody sits in it.

c1_dinner.in.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.in.01.text: Your plate is warm, Steve. Sit. I’m her mother, so you can apologize to me while you eat.

c1_dinner.in.02.speaker: rafa
c1_dinner.in.02.text: I kept the sauce separate. You used to like it that way.

c1_dinner.in.03.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.in.03.text: Nora, the mole. More chilies this time, or less?

c1_dinner.family.01.speaker: iris
c1_dinner.family.01.text: Whatever you think is best, Mamá.

c1_dinner.in.04.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.in.04.text: She used to call it a crime against chilies.

c1_dinner.in.05.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.in.05.text: She texts like a ransom note, too. No capitals. No apostrophes.

c1_dinner.birthday.lead.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.birthday.lead.01.text: Look at this. My birthday, last month.

c1_dinner.birthday.lead.02.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.birthday.lead.02.text: Your girl agreed with me all night. Eleven times. I counted.

c1_dinner.birthday.01.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.birthday.01.text: I drove her here at noon. Rafa drove her home. Midnight, give or take ten minutes.

c1_dinner.out.01.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.out.01.text: She stopped arguing with me. My daughter has argued with me since she could talk.

c1_dinner.birthday.find.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.birthday.find.text: Carmen’s birthday: Nora at La Marea at 20:04, 20:15 and 20:29. Mateo drove her in at noon. Rafa drove her home at midnight.

c1_dinner.family.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.family.lead.01.text: When did she stop arguing? With any of you?

c1_dinner.family.lead.02.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.family.lead.02.text: With me? She fought me about her driving every week. The last real fight was Memorial Day weekend.

c1_dinner.family.lead.03.speaker: rafa
c1_dinner.family.lead.03.text: She sent my mole back every Sunday for ten years. Too sweet. The first Sunday in June, she ate the whole plate.

c1_dinner.family.lead.04.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.family.lead.04.text: She called my show every episode to fix my tide tables. The last call was May seventeenth.

c1_dinner.family.lead.05.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.family.lead.05.text: Funny. Lyle Boone hasn’t missed one of the Little League games I coach since June either.

c1_dinner.family.02.speaker: luis
c1_dinner.family.02.text: Eat before it gets cold, Steve. Then tell us what is troubling you.

c1_dinner.family.03.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.family.03.text: I’m not sure yet, Luis. I’m working on it.

c1_dinner.family.find.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.family.find.text: Nora stopped arguing with her family between the end of May and the first Sunday in June. Lyle changed in June too. I was on nights. I never noticed.

c1_dinner.podcast.lead.01.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.podcast.lead.01.text: Steve. You’re the sound guy. Settle something. There’s a hum in the bay. Three years of tape, and nobody listens.

c1_dinner.podcast.lead.02.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.podcast.lead.02.text: I heard it today. On the pier.

c1_dinner.podcast.01.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.podcast.01.text: You can borrow them. You could also have listened any time in the last three years.

c1_dinner.podcast.find.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.podcast.find.text: Tomás’s loud nights come every nine nights: September 24, October 3, October 12. The next one is tonight.

c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.02.text: It is too sweet. Rafa is in love, so everything he cooks is sweet now.

c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.04.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.talk.carmen.1.04.text: With the girl from the bakery counter. He thinks I don’t know. Mothers know.

c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.01.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.01.text: You still keep Dad’s chair, Luis.

c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.02.speaker: luis
c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.02.text: Frank sat there every Friday for twenty years. Nobody else fits it.

c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.03.speaker: luis
c1_dinner.talk.luis.1.03.text: When he comes home, it will be waiting for him.

c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.02.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.02.text: Four wins, nine losses. But we lead the league in effort.

c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.03.speaker: mateo
c1_dinner.talk.mateo.1.03.text: And my outfield can finally catch. Mostly with their faces, but it counts.

c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.02.speaker: rafa
c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.02.text: Forty tables, one birthday, and Mamá tasting everything twice.

c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.03.speaker: rafa
c1_dinner.talk.rafa.1.03.text: Come to Sunday dinner for real, Steve. She sets your plate either way.

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.02.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.02.text: Eleven listeners. Twelve, if Mamá ever figures out the app.

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.03.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.1.03.text: Laugh now. One day the bay is going to make me famous.

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.01.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.01.text: Come on my show sometime, Steve. A real sound engineer would double my ratings.

c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.03.speaker: tomas
c1_dinner.talk.tomas.2.03.text: Nora used to call in every week just to correct my tide tables. I miss that, honestly.

c1_dinner.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.talk.iris.1.03.text: You used to argue with your mother about the chilies all night.

c1_dinner.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.recap.01.text: Nora changed between the end of May and the first Sunday in June. Lyle changed in June. Carmen noticed. Admiral noticed. I didn’t.

c1_dinner.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.recap.02.text: And Tomás has three years of tape that says the bay hums every nine nights. Tonight is the ninth.

c1_dinner.out.02.speaker: iris
c1_dinner.out.02.text: I’m tired. Let’s go home, sleepyhead.

c1_dinner.out.03.speaker: carmen
c1_dinner.out.03.text: Next Sunday, Steve. The plate will be warm.

c1_escape.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.ctx.01.text: Home. Nora took a phone call in the bedroom and closed the door. She never closes the door.

c1_escape.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.ctx.02.text: Her raincoat was dripping on the floor. I carried it out to hang on the balcony hooks.

c1_escape.order.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.lead.01.text: Something in the lining. Soaked. Aquarium letterhead... north wing?

c1_escape.order.lead.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.lead.02.text: Signed at 20:30. Nora always said that north-wing clock runs fifteen minutes fast.

c1_escape.order.lead.03.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.lead.03.text: And the aquarium is across the bay. Eighteen minutes each way, even with every light green.

c1_escape.order.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.01.text: Noon to midnight at La Marea. Mateo and Rafa both saw her. She couldn’t have been in the north wing.

c1_escape.in.01.speaker: iris
c1_escape.in.01.text: No. He does not know where the notebook is. Tonight? Understood.

c1_escape.in.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.in.02.text: Nora? The balcony door’s locked. From inside.

c1_escape.order.find.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.find.text: Someone signed Nora’s name in the north wing while she was at her mother’s birthday, across the bay. And now Nora has locked me out on the balcony.

c1_escape.power.lead.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.power.lead.01.text: Mr. Bell’s gate. It’s the only way down from here.

c1_escape.power.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.power.01.text: I fixed this latch for Mr. Bell last winter. He paid me in fruitcake. Tonight it’s worth every slice.

c1_escape.power.find.speaker: steve
c1_escape.power.find.text: Mr. Bell’s gate opened, and his stair light never flickered. He never knew I was there.

c1_escape.cross.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.cross.01.text: Sorry. Sorry. Those were your irises.

c1_escape.cross.04.speaker: steve
c1_escape.cross.04.text: Don’t. Please. I don’t know who you are tonight.

c1_escape.cross.find.speaker: steve
c1_escape.cross.find.text: She was close enough to stop me. She didn’t move.

c1_escape.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.recap.01.text: My list: one good morning, played twice. A whistle Admiral won’t answer. A signature Nora couldn’t have made. A phone call about a notebook. A locked door.

c1_escape.recap.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.recap.02.text: And Tomás’s tapes say the bay sings tonight.

c1_escape.recap.03.speaker: steve
c1_escape.recap.03.text: So I went down to the beach. In Bellwether, that’s where you go when you can’t sleep.

c1_escape.out.03.speaker: steve
c1_escape.out.03.text: Midnight. That’s Lyle, in his church shoes. Gus from the bakery. They’re walking into the water.

c2_aquarium.in.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.01.text: Emergency. Bellwether beach. People are walking into the water, and they’re not coming back out. Hello? Hello?
c2_aquarium.in.01.direction: on his flip phone, static rising

c2_aquarium.in.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.02.text: The line died. I didn’t know if anyone had heard.

c2_aquarium.in.03.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.03.text: There was one place in town with Nora’s name on it that night. The north wing of her aquarium.

c2_aquarium.in.04.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.in.04.text: I knew the back way in. Four years of visiting her at work.

c2_aquarium.plan.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.01.text: Nora showed me this plan the week I fixed the underwater speakers. She said the pumps were the heartbeat of the place.

c2_aquarium.plan.lead.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.lead.01.text: On the old plan, the café and the public tank lead to the visitor hall. Door one leads to the north wing.

c2_aquarium.plan.lead.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.lead.02.text: But this newer notice says door one is bricked up. The service door still opens into the pump room.

c2_aquarium.plan.lead.03.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.lead.03.text: And the notice says to follow the one pipe that carries water away from the pump.

c2_aquarium.plan.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.02.text: Service door, pump room, the outgoing pipe. Into the north wing.

c2_aquarium.plan.find.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.plan.find.text: The way in runs from the service door through the pump room, along the only pipe that carries water away.

c2_aquarium.guard.lead.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.lead.01.text: Someone’s behind both doors. Maybe only one of them is real.

c2_aquarium.guard.lead.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.lead.02.text: A real person never steps or coughs the same way twice. A recording does it every time.

c2_aquarium.guard.lead.03.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.lead.03.text: Six seconds at each door. Then I compare the two.

c2_aquarium.guard.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.01.text: The cough was in exactly the same place. That corridor has a recording.

c2_aquarium.guard.find.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.guard.find.text: The filter corridor plays a loop: the same bell and the same cough on the same beat. Nobody’s there. The pump corridor has real footsteps.

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.01.text: Her fleece. Her real fleece, with the fish pins. And an intercom spool.

c2_aquarium.out.01.speaker: nora
c2_aquarium.out.01.text: My name is Nora Reyes, and somebody just walked out of here wearing my face.

c2_aquarium.intercom.01.speaker: nora
c2_aquarium.intercom.01.text: Two short notes. If Admiral can hear me, perhaps somebody else can.

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.02.text: The paper on the spool is dated in her handwriting. May 29th.

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.03.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.03.text: Her second note goes up. Like it always did, before this summer.

c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.04.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.intercom.lead.04.text: And there’s a loose copy of the whistle in the drawer. On that one, the second note falls.

c2_aquarium.out.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.out.02.text: Five months. I didn’t notice for five months.

c2_aquarium.intercom.find.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.intercom.find.text: The real Nora recorded this here on May 29. Someone else has been living her life with me for five months. Her whistle rises. The one Admiral ignored falls.

c2_aquarium.recap.01.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.recap.01.text: The north wing is no repair job. It’s a holding station, with cots, Nora’s real coat, and her voice on a tape from May.

c2_aquarium.recap.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.recap.02.text: The woman who said good morning to me yesterday was not Nora. Nora was here, frightened, whistling for help. And I didn’t hear it for five months.

c2_aquarium.recap.03.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.recap.03.text: If she was alive in May, she might be alive now.

c2_aquarium.out.04.speaker: lyle_copy
c2_aquarium.out.04.text: Easy now, Steve. Nobody wants this to be hard.

c2_ship.in.04.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.04.text: They walked me down the old intake tunnel, under the bay. At the end of it there was a ship.

c2_ship.in.05.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.05.text: Glass corridors. Slow light. And a hum that was almost a tune.

c2_ship.in.01.speaker: iris
c2_ship.in.01.text: Please come with us. They want to know where your mother put her notebook.

c2_ship.in.02.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.02.text: Would peaceful human hold music assist your experience?

c2_ship.in.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.03.text: I’d prefer the exit. Does that come with music too?

c2_ship.in.06.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.06.text: “You are the author of your own story.” This is from a human book. Is it helping?

c2_ship.in.07.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.07.text: The scan proceeds from the oldest memories. You are now nineteen. Congratulations on your driving test.

c2_ship.command.lead.01.speaker: guard
c2_ship.command.lead.01.text: This restraint is sticking. Release, please.

c2_ship.command.lead.02.speaker: guard
c2_ship.command.lead.02.text: Thank you, Prefect. And fastened again.

c2_ship.command.lead.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.command.lead.03.text: Dad’s recorder was running in my pocket the whole time.

c2_ship.command.lead.04.speaker: steve
c2_ship.command.lead.04.text: The chair’s little lamp stayed dark when the attendant asked. It lit up for the voice on the intercom.

c2_ship.command.lead.05.speaker: steve
c2_ship.command.lead.05.text: Dad’s counter ticks once a second. The lamp lit at tick three. The buckle clicked at tick seven.

c2_ship.command.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.command.find.text: The Prefect’s release command is on Dad’s tape: four seconds, from “Release” to the click.

c2_ship.escape.lead.01.speaker: guard
c2_ship.escape.lead.01.text: Fifty-eight percent. Fifty-nine. You are doing very well.

c2_ship.escape.lead.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.lead.02.text: Dad’s recorder caught three voices tonight. Nora’s spool, the attendant, and the Prefect.

c2_ship.escape.lead.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.lead.03.text: Two speaker covers by my hand. The attendant tested the hall speakers on the cracked one.

c2_ship.escape.lead.04.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.lead.04.text: When my sleeve brushed the other grille, the chair’s lamp blinked.

c2_ship.escape.lead.05.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.lead.05.text: The lamp stays lit for one second each beat. At the notch marked sixty-one, it stays lit for six.

c2_ship.escape.01.speaker: saren
c2_ship.escape.01.direction: Dad’s recorder, held to the grille

c2_ship.escape.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.02.text: It worked. Sixty-one percent of me, and all of me is getting out of this chair.

c2_ship.escape.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.find.text: The Prefect’s own voice opened the chair, at the notch marked sixty-one. The scan stopped at sixty-one percent.

c2_ship.nora.lead.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.lead.02.text: That hum. It’s almost a song. I know it from somewhere.

c2_ship.nora.lead.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.lead.03.text: The corridor light flashes at two, six and ten seconds. Every four seconds, like a clock.

c2_ship.nora.lead.04.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.lead.04.text: The pickup on the rail repeats each flash, one second late.

c2_ship.nora.lead.05.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.lead.05.text: And there’s fog on the glass above her mouth. Three seconds, seven, then twelve.

c2_ship.nora.lead.06.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.lead.06.text: I made a rubbing of each rhythm. Now the labels have come off.

c2_ship.nora.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.02.text: I can’t move you without stopping whatever keeps you breathing. I’m coming back for you.

c2_ship.nora.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.01.text: I kept waiting until I knew what to say. I’m here now. I should have been here sooner.

c2_ship.nora.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.nora.find.text: Nora is alive. Her breath keeps its own time, a little behind the ship’s. She’s asleep, not gone.

c2_ship.out.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.out.01.text: The tunnel’s flooding. The underwater speakers still work... I fixed them, the day I met her.

c2_ship.intake.lead.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.intake.lead.01.text: Admiral swims the whole bay at night. If he hears the right whistle, he’ll come.

c2_ship.intake.lead.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.intake.lead.02.text: Nora’s spool, the loose copy, or the Prefect. One chance.

c2_ship.intake.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.intake.01.text: Come on, Admiral. You never missed this one.

c2_ship.intake.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.intake.find.text: Nora’s real whistle, through the speakers I fixed the day we met. Admiral came down through the dark and dragged me to the surface.

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.01.text: Where are we, Nor? What is this place?

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.02.text: Somewhere safe, under the bay. Please don’t be frightened.

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.03.text: You walked me down that tunnel yourself.

c2_ship.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris
c2_ship.talk.iris.1.04.text: They asked me to. I always do what I am asked.

c2_ship.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.iris.2.01.text: Do you remember the day we met?

c2_ship.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: iris
c2_ship.talk.iris.2.02.text: At the aquarium. You fixed the underwater speakers. You had a coffee stain on your green shirt.

c2_ship.talk.iris.2.04.speaker: iris
c2_ship.talk.iris.2.04.text: I remember everything she saw. Everything I saw.

c2_ship.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.iris.3.01.text: Carmen keeps my plate warm every Sunday. Does she know her daughter is down here?

c2_ship.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: iris
c2_ship.talk.iris.3.02.text: Carmen is happy. Everyone at that table is happy.

c2_ship.talk.iris.3.04.speaker: iris
c2_ship.talk.iris.3.04.text: It is the only one I am allowed to give you.

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.text: Lyle, do your boys know where you are tonight?

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.speaker: lyle_copy
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.text: They’re asleep. I’ll be at their game on Sunday. I always am now.

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.text: You used to miss every single one.

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.speaker: lyle_copy
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.1.04.text: People change, Steve. Mostly for the better.

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.01.text: You’re a deputy, Lyle. You swore an oath to this town.

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.02.speaker: lyle_copy
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.02.text: I did. I remember every word of it.

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.03.text: Then get me out of this chair.

c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.04.speaker: lyle_copy
c2_ship.talk.lyle_copy.2.04.text: I am helping you, Steve. This is the easy way.

c2_ship.recap.01.speaker: steve
c2_ship.recap.01.text: There is a ship under the bay. Nora is asleep on it, alive, with hundreds of others. At the far end of the hall, one bed lay under frost, and something too tall to be human slept in it. The guards never looked at it.

c2_ship.recap.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.recap.02.text: They tried to make another me. They got sixty-one percent.

c2_ship.recap.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.recap.03.text: And the woman with Nora’s face, who let me go on the balcony, had walked me to that chair herself.

c2_ship.out.03.speaker: steve
c2_ship.out.03.text: Sheriff... there’s a ship. Under the bay.
c2_ship.out.03.direction: coughing up seawater on the beach at dawn

c3_house.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.ctx.01.text: June Calder pulled me off the beach at dawn on Monday and drove me to her house, not the station. She called it protective custody. Her beagle, Biscuit, slept through the whole thing.

c3_house.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.ctx.02.text: By Friday, the whole town had heard I broke into the aquarium. The casseroles started arriving.

c3_house.in.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.in.01.text: Forty-seven casseroles. Your town is either very worried or very hungry.

c3_house.in.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.in.02.text: Nora is asleep on a ship under the bay. I know exactly how that sounds.

c3_house.in.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.in.03.text: Then we start with what you can prove.

c3_house.in.04.speaker: carmen
c3_house.in.04.text: Forty-eight. Mine is the good one.
c3_house.in.04.direction: at the front door, holding a covered dish

c3_house.in.05.speaker: carmen
c3_house.in.05.text: Nora told me you’re not well, mijo. But I saw you at the market this morning, smiling at the tomatoes. I was so glad.

c3_house.in.06.speaker: steve
c3_house.in.06.text: Carmen... I haven’t left this house since Monday.

c3_house.crossword.lead.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.text: You told me that chair copies the oldest memories first. And you got out at sixty-one percent.
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.direction: after Carmen has gone, closing the door

c3_house.crossword.lead.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.02.text: I was at the station all morning, and Biscuit isn’t a witness. So you tell me. What could I ask you that the man at the market couldn’t answer?

c3_house.crossword.lead.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.03.text: Don’t tell me something sweet. Copies can be sweet. Don’t act strange. Grieving people act strange.

c3_house.crossword.lead.04.speaker: steve
c3_house.crossword.lead.04.text: I called 911 on Sunday night, when people walked into the water. That was before the chair.

c3_house.crossword.lead.05.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.05.text: After midnight, the 911 line rings in my kitchen. My machine keeps every call. I haven’t played Sunday’s yet.

c3_house.crossword.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.03.direction: after playing back the call on her kitchen machine

c3_house.crossword.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.crossword.01.direction: relieved, leaning over her crossword, his elbow near her mug

c3_house.crossword.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.02.text: No copy is that bad at this. And you’ve put coffee in my lap.

c3_house.crossword.04.speaker: steve
c3_house.crossword.04.text: How do I know you’re you?

c3_house.crossword.05.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.05.text: You don’t. Nobody scanned me halfway. So you check my paperwork, same as everyone else.

c3_house.crossword.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.crossword.find.text: The chair never got as far as Sunday night. My 911 call was on June’s machine, word for word. Whoever Carmen saw at the market, it wasn’t me.

c3_house.out.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.out.01.text: For a year I’ve kept a list. People who got better overnight. Thirty-one names.

c3_house.rules.lead.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.lead.01.text: Lyle’s on it. My own deputy. Fourteen years, and this summer he started filing his reports on time.

c3_house.rules.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.01.text: We do this fairly. Otherwise we’re just frightened people making a list.

c3_house.rules.lead.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.lead.02.text: Gus Albano. Thirty years of his grandmother’s recipes, and on Monday a new pastry in his window.

c3_house.rules.lead.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.lead.03.text: Mateo’s coaching book. Lyle missed every game last spring. From June eleventh, he signed in at every one.

c3_house.rules.lead.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.lead.04.text: Walt moved to Washington in April. His signature is on a permit here, dated a day he was testifying in Washington.

c3_house.rules.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.02.text: Two I could take to a judge. And if I do, what do I tell Lyle’s boys? Mateo says they’ve never been happier.

c3_house.rules.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.rules.03.text: Is Mrs. Penhallow on it? She was on the beach at midnight on Sunday.

c3_house.rules.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.04.text: Agnes? She hasn’t changed in forty years. She still corrects my grammar.

c3_house.rules.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.rules.find.text: June’s list has thirty-one names, and most of them are feelings. Two are records: Lyle’s sign-in book and Walt Prior’s permit. Mrs. Penhallow isn’t on it.

c3_house.mail.lead.01.speaker: pell
c3_house.mail.lead.01.direction: at the front door with the mail, saluting the sleeping beagle

c3_house.mail.01.speaker: pell
c3_house.mail.01.text: A most diligent animal. I will return at the scheduled interval.

c3_house.mail.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.02.text: She’s asleep, Dale. That is her schedule.

c3_house.mail.lead.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.lead.02.text: On Monday the post office told me Dale had already brought your letters here. Before I’d called them. So I asked for the paperwork.

c3_house.mail.lead.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.lead.03.text: At ten past six on Monday, I radioed the station to say you were here. Lyle was starting his shift. He answered.

c3_house.mail.lead.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.lead.04.text: Dale’s bag left the post office at four minutes past eight, with your letters already bundled for my house.

c3_house.mail.lead.05.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.lead.05.text: I didn’t phone the post office until twelve past eight. And Carmen only heard from Nora at lunch.

c3_house.mail.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.mail.03.text: He had my mail sorted for your house before anyone told the post office I was here.

c3_house.mail.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.04.text: Lyle took my call at ten past six.

c3_house.mail.05.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.05.text: Then nobody tells Lyle where we go next. Or Dale.

c3_house.mail.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.mail.find.text: Dale had my letters bundled for June’s house at 08:04. The post office didn’t know until 08:12. The only other person who knew was Lyle, who took June’s call at ten past six. They talk to each other.

c3_house.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.calder.1.01.text: Does Biscuit ever wake up, June?

c3_house.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.1.02.text: For cheese. And once for a thunderstorm, back in two thousand nineteen.

c3_house.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.calder.1.03.text: Some guard dog you have there.

c3_house.talk.calder.1.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.1.04.text: Ruth picked her out. She said a sheriff needs one partner who never argues.

c3_house.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.calder.2.01.text: You really do the crossword in ink, every single morning?

c3_house.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.2.02.text: Ruth started it. She said pencils are for people who expect to be wrong.

c3_house.talk.calder.2.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.2.04.text: Every day, Mercer. I just commit to it.

c3_house.talk.calder.3.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.calder.3.01.text: What are we going to do with forty-eight casseroles?

c3_house.talk.calder.3.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.3.02.text: Eat Carmen’s tonight. The deputies get the rest, except the tuna one.

c3_house.talk.calder.3.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.calder.3.03.text: What’s wrong with the tuna one?

c3_house.talk.calder.3.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.3.04.text: Potato chips on top. I have standards, even in a crisis.

c3_house.talk.calder.4.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.calder.4.01.text: How long have you kept that list, June?

c3_house.talk.calder.4.02.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.4.02.text: Since last fall. The town got nicer, and nobody could tell me why.

c3_house.talk.calder.4.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.talk.calder.4.03.text: In my job, when everybody suddenly behaves, you start counting.

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.01.text: How is Nora doing, Carmen? Really?

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: carmen
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.02.text: Calm. So calm. She agrees with me about everything now.

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.03.speaker: carmen
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.03.text: I should be happy, mijo. But I miss the fights. Is that terrible?

c3_house.talk.carmen.1.04.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.carmen.1.04.text: No, it isn’t. I miss them too.

c3_house.talk.carmen.2.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.carmen.2.01.text: The man at the market, Carmen. What did he say to you?

c3_house.talk.carmen.2.02.speaker: carmen
c3_house.talk.carmen.2.02.text: That the tomatoes looked lovely. You never say lovely, Steve. Not once in four years.

c3_house.talk.carmen.2.03.speaker: carmen
c3_house.talk.carmen.2.03.text: I thought you were finally getting better.

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.01.text: What did you bring us, Carmen?

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.02.speaker: carmen
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.02.text: Chicken tinga. Rafa made it, so it is too sweet. He is still in love.

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.03.text: With the girl from the bakery counter?

c3_house.talk.carmen.3.04.speaker: carmen
c3_house.talk.carmen.3.04.text: Now he brings home day-old bread every night. We are drowning in bread.

c3_house.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.pell.1.01.text: Cold out there this morning, Dale?

c3_house.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell
c3_house.talk.pell.1.02.text: Eleven degrees at eight o’clock. Wind from the west at nine knots.

c3_house.talk.pell.1.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.pell.1.03.text: I only meant, is it cold.

c3_house.talk.pell.1.04.speaker: pell
c3_house.talk.pell.1.04.text: It is within the normal range for October.

c3_house.talk.pell.2.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.pell.2.01.text: You still bring letters for my parents, Dale.

c3_house.talk.pell.2.02.speaker: pell
c3_house.talk.pell.2.02.text: Every item goes to its address. That is the procedure.

c3_house.talk.pell.2.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.talk.pell.2.03.text: They’ve been gone for eighteen months.

c3_house.talk.pell.2.04.speaker: pell
c3_house.talk.pell.2.04.text: The address has not changed, Mr. Mercer.

c3_house.recap.01.speaker: steve
c3_house.recap.01.text: June believes me. That makes one person.

c3_house.recap.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.recap.02.text: Somebody with my face was at the market this morning. Lyle passes things to Dale. And two names on June’s list have paper behind them.

c3_house.recap.03.speaker: steve
c3_house.recap.03.text: Paper is harder to replace than people. And June has keys to the Town Hall archive.

c3_house.out.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.out.03.text: Town Hall closes at five. I have keys.

c3_house.out.02.speaker: steve
c3_house.out.02.text: Then let’s find out which of them got better, and which of them got replaced.

c3_archive.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.ctx.01.text: Town Hall, after five. June had the keys, and I had a phone call to make.

c3_archive.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.ctx.02.text: I asked Tomás for help. It was the first time in a year I’d asked anybody for anything.

c3_archive.in.01.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.in.01.text: Three years of recordings. Original timestamps. You can stop calling it a hobby now.

c3_archive.in.03.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.in.03.text: Nora says you broke into her aquarium.

c3_archive.in.06.speaker: steve
c3_archive.in.06.text: When I can prove it, you’re the first person I tell.

c3_archive.paper.lead.01.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.lead.01.text: Walt Prior. County planner. I went to his going-away party in April. He cried into the punch.

c3_archive.paper.lead.02.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.lead.02.text: The county computer says he signed this permit by fax from Washington. The clerk’s ledger says he signed it at her counter.

c3_archive.paper.lead.03.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.lead.03.text: The ledger was signed in ink, right here at the counter. May third, ten past two, with the clerk’s stamp.

c3_archive.paper.lead.04.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.lead.04.text: The computer entry was typed in from the ledger the next day. Somebody has changed it since.

c3_archive.paper.lead.05.speaker: steve
c3_archive.paper.lead.05.text: This hearing transcript has Walt in Washington that afternoon, answering questions from half past one until four.

c3_archive.paper.lead.06.speaker: steve
c3_archive.paper.lead.06.text: And the newspaper column only says he looked tired.

c3_archive.paper.lead.07.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.lead.07.text: The permit reopens the aquarium’s old seawater intake. The same tunnel they walked you down.

c3_archive.paper.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.paper.01.text: Two places. Same time. Witnesses on both documents.

c3_archive.paper.02.speaker: calder
c3_archive.paper.02.text: And somebody went back and fixed the computer. Nobody bothered with the ink.

c3_archive.paper.find.speaker: steve
c3_archive.paper.find.text: On May 3, Walt Prior was answering questions in Washington while someone signed his name at our counter to reopen the aquarium’s old seawater intake. Later, somebody changed the computer. Nobody changed the ink.

c3_archive.power.lead.01.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.power.lead.01.direction: at the archive door, a bait bucket on her arm

c3_archive.power.lead.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.lead.02.text: Mrs. Penhallow? You’re miles from your pier.

c3_archive.power.lead.03.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.power.lead.03.text: I take the bus. Two dollars, please. Herring.

c3_archive.power.lead.04.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.lead.04.text: She’s wrapped it in the business page. Something’s circled. ‘Meridian Labs: the engine that will change the world.’

c3_archive.power.lead.05.speaker: calder
c3_archive.power.lead.05.text: Sentinel Point. It was a radio array when I was a girl. Now it’s Meridian’s. Federal money, an armed gate, and on November seventh the President flies in to sign something there.

c3_archive.power.lead.06.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.power.lead.06.text: Electricity is very honest, Steven. It can’t be charming.

c3_archive.power.lead.07.speaker: calder
c3_archive.power.lead.07.text: Here are last month’s meter rolls. Sentinel Point, and Pearl Laundry next door.

c3_archive.power.lead.08.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.lead.08.text: They’re running totals, like the miles on a car. What counts is how far each one moved.

c3_archive.power.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.01.text: A world-changing machine with a very modest dryer cycle.

c3_archive.power.find.speaker: steve
c3_archive.power.find.text: Last month Sentinel Point used 640 units. The laundromat next door used 882. Whatever Meridian is building out there, it runs on less power than a row of dryers.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.01.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.lead.01.text: Every ninth night for three years, I was out there with a recorder. I wrote down everything, from wherever I was standing.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.cycle.lead.02.text: Then help me pick a night, and a place to stand.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.03.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.lead.03.text: Each box has two dates. The night I recorded, and the day the episode aired.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.04.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.lead.04.text: The pier lamp always dims first, at 23:42. Footsteps pass the boathouse at 23:53.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.05.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.lead.05.text: And at four minutes past midnight, the water starts to glow.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.06.speaker: calder
c3_archive.cycle.lead.06.text: I want to see faces on that path before they reach the water. Without anyone seeing us.

c3_archive.cycle.lead.07.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.lead.07.text: From the sea wall, the path is behind you. The pier is wide open. The boathouse window faces the path.

c3_archive.cycle.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.cycle.01.text: Nine nights apart, for three years. It never missed one.

c3_archive.cycle.04.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.cycle.04.text: Then I want it on tape.

c3_archive.cycle.find.speaker: steve
c3_archive.cycle.find.text: Three years of tape, and the bay never missed a ninth night. The next one is Tuesday the 30th. June and I will be at the boathouse window by 23:40, before the pier lamp dims.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.01.text: How many listeners does the podcast have now?

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.02.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.02.text: Fourteen. Mamá found the app, and now she leaves comments.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.03.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.03.text: Every episode, the same comment. Eat something, mijo.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.04.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.tomas.1.04.text: She’s not wrong, you know, Tomás.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.02.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.02.text: Last night. No capitals, no apostrophes, same as always.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.03.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.talk.tomas.2.03.text: She just wrote, eat something. She sounds like Mamá now. That’s new.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.01.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.01.text: Do you know how many boxes are down here?

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.02.text: No, but I bet you counted them.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.03.speaker: tomas
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.03.text: Four hundred and twelve. I counted while June looked for the light switch.

c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.04.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.tomas.3.04.text: You’d get along with Mrs. Penhallow.

c3_archive.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.calder.1.01.text: Why does the sheriff have keys to the archive?

c3_archive.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder
c3_archive.talk.calder.1.02.text: The sheriff’s office has had a key since nineteen fifty. Nobody ever asked for it back.

c3_archive.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c3_archive.talk.calder.1.03.text: Ruth used to say I’d rather read old permits than novels. She was right.

c3_archive.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.calder.2.01.text: The President is coming here? To Bellwether?

c3_archive.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: calder
c3_archive.talk.calder.2.02.text: November seventh. The Rotary Club is already fighting about the bunting.

c3_archive.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder
c3_archive.talk.calder.2.03.text: I’ve been asked to close Harbor Road and smile. I can manage one of those.

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.01.text: You came all the way here on the bus?

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.02.text: The number four. The driver and I have an arrangement.

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.03.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.03.text: What kind of arrangement is that?

c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.04.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.talk.agnes.1.04.text: He drives, and I correct his grammar. We both arrive improved.

c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.01.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.01.text: I like archives, Steven. Somebody should keep what everyone else forgets.

c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.02.text: Is that why you came all this way?

c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.03.speaker: agnes
c3_archive.talk.agnes.2.03.text: I came to sell you a herring. Two dollars, please. Exact change.

c3_archive.recap.01.speaker: steve
c3_archive.recap.01.text: Three things nobody thought to change. Walt Prior’s name in ink, in two places at once. A lab that will change the world, running on less power than a laundromat. And three years of tape that never missed a ninth night.

c3_archive.recap.02.speaker: steve
c3_archive.recap.02.text: June wanted to see it with her own eyes. So on Tuesday the 30th, at 23:40, we were at the boathouse window.

c3_archive.out.04.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.04.text: At 23:42 the pier lamp went out. Eleven minutes later, the footsteps started.

c3_archive.out.05.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.05.text: That’s Lyle. Gus again. Half the Rotary Club. Nobody’s talking.
c3_archive.out.05.direction: a whisper at the boathouse window

c3_archive.out.06.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.06.text: Nobody’s swimming. They’re walking until they’re gone.

c3_archive.out.08.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.08.text: She’s stopped at the waterline. She’s... going back up the beach.

c3_archive.out.01.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.01.text: Two hundred and seventy-four. My list had thirty-one.
