c3_archive.out.09.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.09.text: Mrs. Penhallow was on the boathouse steps, watching. She isn’t on your list.

c3_archive.out.10.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.10.text: She isn’t on anyone’s. Ninety-one years old, on a boathouse step at midnight. Counting.

c3_archive.out.11.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.11.text: I’m calling Adrian Rook. FBI. He owes me a favor from a kidnapping case fifteen years ago.

c3_archive.out.12.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.12.text: An hour later my flip phone buzzed. A text, from a number I didn’t know.

c3_archive.out.03.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.03.text: “He remembers June. That doesn’t mean he’s Adrian.” No capitals. No apostrophes.
c3_archive.out.03.display_text: “he remembers june. that doesnt mean hes adrian.” No capitals. No apostrophes.

i1_archive.ctx.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.ctx.01.text: Every ninth night they come below, and I compare each of them with the record they were made from.

i1_archive.ctx.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.ctx.02.text: Two hundred and seventy-four tonight. One of them has changed.

i1_archive.in.01.speaker: gus
i1_archive.in.01.text: I invented a kelp croissant. Nobody asked for it. I wanted to know what it would taste like.

i1_archive.in.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.in.02.text: Your record contains no such recipe.

i1_archive.in.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.in.03.text: You were made from Gus Albano’s scan, and you have drifted from it. That makes you an echo. Echoes are reconciled.

i1_archive.in.04.speaker: gus
i1_archive.in.04.text: It was a very good croissant.

i1_archive.reset.lead.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.reset.lead.01.text: One recipe of drift. The law does not measure how much. Only that it happened.

i1_archive.reset.lead.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.reset.lead.02.text: The law is simple. The source is never touched. The echo is restored from the source.

i1_archive.reset.lead.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.reset.lead.03.text: And whatever the echo loses, I must describe in the witness ledger. In words, not numbers.

i1_archive.reset.02.speaker: gus
i1_archive.reset.02.text: Good evening. May I help you?

i1_archive.reset.find.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.reset.find.text: Gus Albano’s echo, reconciled. He will go back to town smiling, without the croissant. I have written down what it was.

i1_archive.signals.lead.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.lead.01.text: Two human tests of the Meridian engine. The Prefect keeps them in his file.

i1_archive.signals.lead.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.lead.02.text: A year ago I noticed something about them. Every ninth night I listen again, to be sure.

i1_archive.signals.lead.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.lead.03.text: Each pulse has one missing beat near the middle. And each station wrote down when its lamp flared.

i1_archive.signals.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.01.text: The same pulse. The same missing beat. Different light. Either humans are very consistent, or very careful liars. I will not guess on the record.

i1_archive.signals.find.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.signals.find.text: Two tests, a week and a world apart, with the same pulse and the same missing beat. Only the light differs. I have not written down what I think it means.

i1_archive.quiet.01.speaker: saren
i1_archive.quiet.01.text: The fleet has answered. One word. Deliver.

i1_archive.quiet.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.02.text: And who will come to check?

i1_archive.quiet.lead.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.lead.01.text: The fleet never takes a Prefect’s word for long. Sooner or later, it sends a Vigil to look.

i1_archive.quiet.lead.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.lead.02.text: Seven worlds with people on them. Every one went quiet soon after the fleet arrived.

i1_archive.quiet.lead.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.lead.03.text: The newest went quiet three hundred years ago. The other six went quiet at least five hundred years ago.

i1_archive.quiet.lead.04.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.lead.04.text: The sleeper in Row Zero came aboard three hundred years ago. It has never said a word.

i1_archive.quiet.04.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.04.text: Tirel went quiet. So did six others. Not one body, in any survey.
i1_archive.quiet.04.direction: beside the frosted bed in Row Zero

i1_archive.quiet.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.03.text: Three hundred years, and you still will not tell me where your people went.

i1_archive.quiet.find.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.quiet.find.text: The sleeper in Row Zero came from Tirel, three hundred years ago. Seven worlds went quiet, and the surveyors found empty cities, not graves. The Prefect’s sealed entry, I have not read.

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.01.text: Tell me about your bakery, Gus Albano.

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.02.speaker: gus
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.02.text: Ovens on at four. The radio on, low. My grandmother’s recipes, every one of them.

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.03.speaker: gus
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.03.text: People wait outside in the rain for her cinnamon knots.

i1_archive.talk.gus.1.04.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.talk.gus.1.04.text: Then they must be very good knots.

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.01.text: What do the people of your town do in the morning?

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.02.speaker: gus
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.02.text: They buy bread and complain about the weather. Then most of them buy a second loaf.

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.03.text: Why would anyone need a second loaf?

i1_archive.talk.gus.2.04.speaker: gus
i1_archive.talk.gus.2.04.text: For a neighbor. Everybody there has somebody to bring bread to.

i1_archive.talk.gus.3.01.speaker: gus
i1_archive.talk.gus.3.01.text: Have you seen my delivery van? It has a giant croissant on the roof.

i1_archive.talk.gus.3.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.talk.gus.3.02.text: I have not. Is the croissant necessary?

i1_archive.talk.gus.3.03.speaker: gus
i1_archive.talk.gus.3.03.text: Absolutely. Children wave at it. Nobody waves at a plain van.

i1_archive.talk.gus.4.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.talk.gus.4.01.text: Do you remember the croissant, Gus?

i1_archive.talk.gus.4.02.speaker: gus
i1_archive.talk.gus.4.02.text: Croissant? I bake my grandmother’s recipes. I have never changed one.

i1_archive.talk.gus.4.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.talk.gus.4.03.text: No. Of course you have not. Go back to your ovens.

i1_archive.recap.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.recap.01.text: One echo reconciled, and one croissant written down. Two human tests, a world apart, with one pulse between them. Seven quiet worlds, and not one grave.

i1_archive.recap.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.recap.02.text: And a Prefect who has promised the fleet an engine.

i1_archive.out.03.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.03.text: Last, as every ninth night, Helen Mercer. A windowless room. Two delegations. And Helen between them, writing in a notebook.

i1_archive.out.01.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.01.text: Report to the Prefect. Subject: Mercer, Helen. Memory damaged by scan. Engine details in subject’s notebook.

i1_archive.out.02.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.02.text: Her memory is not damaged. I will leave the report as it is.

i1_archive.out.04.speaker: archivist
i1_archive.out.04.text: Then I did what I always do when the work is finished. I listened to the last wind on Veyr.

p_veyr.in.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.in.01.text: There are forty thousand names on the departure register. I have checked every one.

p_veyr.shield.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.shield.01.text: Now I can hear the city, beneath the wind.

p_veyr.levels.lead.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.levels.lead.01.text: The gusts so far touched minus nine, minus three and minus six on the meter.

p_veyr.levels.lead.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.levels.lead.02.text: The engines will be nine decibels louder than the loudest gust. Above zero, the meter turns red.

p_veyr.levels.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.levels.01.text: Leave room for the loud parts. They belong to the record too.

p_veyr.levels.find.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.levels.find.text: Six decibels of room. When the engines come, they will reach the top of the meter and no further.

p_veyr.record.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.record.02.text: Forty thousand names. Somebody should remember the quiet after them.

p_veyr.record.find.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.record.find.text: The wind, the engines, and the quiet after them. One take.

p_veyr.recap.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.recap.01.text: One take. The wind over the western towers, the engines rising, and then the quiet.

p_veyr.recap.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.recap.02.text: I did not look back. I watched the meter.

p_veyr.out.01.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.out.01.text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Original take.

p_veyr.out.02.speaker: archivist
p_veyr.out.02.text: I will remember where we lived.

c4_safe.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.01.text: Adrian Rook arrived the next afternoon with four agents and two black SUVs. He was everything June had promised. Calm. Kind. Thorough.

c4_safe.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.02.text: He drove us to a Bureau safe house in the hills above the bay. An hour from town, with nobody else for miles.

c4_safe.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.03.text: I kept thinking about that text. If someone wanted to cut me off from the one man who could help, that’s exactly what they’d send.

c4_safe.ctx.04.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.04.text: On the drive, every station talked about President Ward. On November seventh she signs an accord with China at Sentinel Point.

c4_safe.in.01.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.in.01.text: We’ll take the tapes as evidence. You may keep the recorder.

c4_safe.in.02.speaker: calder
c4_safe.in.02.text: Adrian and I go back a long way.

c4_safe.in.04.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.in.04.text: One more thing, Steve. Your mother kept a notebook. Any idea where?

c4_safe.in.05.speaker: steve
c4_safe.in.05.text: Mom kept a lot of notebooks.

c4_safe.in.07.speaker: steve
c4_safe.in.07.text: He had already taken every tape I’d brought. Not Mom’s voicemail. That cassette lives in my cardigan pocket, and I didn’t offer it.

c4_safe.record.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.lead.01.text: Every hour, on the hour, Rook goes on hold with the Bureau. And he hums along.
c4_safe.record.lead.01.sfx: hold music through the office door

c4_safe.record.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.lead.02.text: When the music stops, he leans out and tells June the same thing. Word for word, like the voicemail on her phone.

c4_safe.record.lead.03.speaker: calder
c4_safe.record.lead.03.text: If you record Adrian, Mercer, I want to hear this house around his voice. Not my phone.

c4_safe.record.lead.04.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.lead.04.text: The lounge has the karaoke machine, and the generator roars right under June’s window.

c4_safe.record.lead.05.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.lead.05.text: But his office door has a gap at the bottom. And he speaks a second after the music stops.

c4_safe.record.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.02.text: That’s the line. Keep the whole take.

c4_safe.record.find.speaker: steve
c4_safe.record.find.text: I have Rook’s line on Dad’s tape, from outside his door, with this house’s room sound around it. Nobody can say I copied it off June’s phone.

c4_safe.match.lead.01.speaker: calder
c4_safe.match.lead.01.text: You want my voicemail? Mercer, that’s a federal agent you’re recording.

c4_safe.match.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.match.lead.02.text: Then it won’t matter. Please, June.

c4_safe.match.lead.03.speaker: steve
c4_safe.match.lead.03.text: Remember Nora’s good morning? Two days, same breath, same pause. People never do that. Recordings do.

c4_safe.match.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.match.01.text: Different rooms. Same breath, same pause, same little click on the S. That isn’t a man repeating himself. That’s a recording wearing a man.

c4_safe.match.find.speaker: steve
c4_safe.match.find.text: June’s voicemail and Rook’s voice through the door are one recording, breath for breath, like Nora’s good morning. The man running this house isn’t Adrian Rook.

c4_safe.screens.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.lead.01.text: That night the agents dragged out the karaoke machine. Rook sang three songs. Beautifully.

c4_safe.screens.lead.02.speaker: calder
c4_safe.screens.lead.02.text: Adrian hates karaoke. He walked out of my wedding when the machine came on.

c4_safe.screens.lead.03.speaker: calder
c4_safe.screens.lead.03.text: ...Odd behavior proves nothing. My own rule.

c4_safe.screens.lead.04.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.lead.04.text: While he was singing, his office door was open.

c4_safe.screens.lead.05.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.lead.05.text: In the aquarium, a picture that kept repeating meant nobody was really there.

c4_safe.screens.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.01.text: Adrian Rook, asleep in bed 41B. Both governments’ seals on the transfer. And an empty bed waiting for President Ward on signing day.

c4_safe.screens.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.02.text: And a list of placements in Washington and Beijing. The first name on it is Walt, from June’s list.

c4_safe.screens.find.speaker: steve
c4_safe.screens.find.text: The real Adrian Rook is asleep on that ship, in bed 41B. They have people in Washington and in Beijing. And they’ve made up a bed for President Ward, for the day she signs the accord.

c4_safe.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.talk.calder.1.01.text: Who is looking after Biscuit while you’re up here?

c4_safe.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: calder
c4_safe.talk.calder.1.02.text: Dale. He comes by twice a day with the mail anyway.

c4_safe.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c4_safe.talk.calder.1.03.text: She likes him better than me. He never forgets the treats.

c4_safe.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: calder
c4_safe.talk.calder.2.01.text: My father brought me up here to fish when I was a girl. We never caught a thing.

c4_safe.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.talk.calder.2.02.text: Then why did you keep coming?

c4_safe.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder
c4_safe.talk.calder.2.03.text: For the sandwiches. And three whole hours where nobody could phone him.

c4_safe.talk.calder.3.01.speaker: calder
c4_safe.talk.calder.3.01.text: Adrian and I worked a case together twenty years ago. He argued with everyone, including me.

c4_safe.talk.calder.3.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.talk.calder.3.02.text: He hasn’t argued with anybody since he got here.

c4_safe.talk.calder.3.03.speaker: calder
c4_safe.talk.calder.3.03.text: No. He hasn’t. I noticed that too.

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.01.text: Nice place. Does the Bureau own it?

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.02.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.02.text: It does. Every room is exactly as the file describes. I checked them all twice.

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.03.speaker: steve
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.03.text: You read the file on the furniture?

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.04.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.1.04.text: I read everything, Steve. It saves time later.

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.01.text: June says you take your coffee with three sugars.

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.02.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.02.text: I take it however the house makes it.

c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.04.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.talk.rook_copy.2.04.text: It’s a very good answer. It never disappoints anyone.

c4_safe.recap.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.recap.01.text: Rook’s voice is a recording. The real Rook is asleep under the bay. And there’s a bed waiting for the President.

c4_safe.recap.02.speaker: steve
c4_safe.recap.02.text: I had to tell June. Rook had made sure I couldn’t just walk down the hall and do it.

c4_safe.out.02.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.out.02.text: June will sit with my team in the east wing tonight. You’ll be more comfortable in the west.

c4_safe.out.03.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.out.03.text: And Steve. The notebook. Anything at all you remember.

c4_safe.out.04.speaker: rook_copy
c4_safe.out.04.text: At five o’clock a van takes you down to Bellwether. You’ll be processed at the Sheriff’s office. It’s only paperwork.

c4_safe.out.05.speaker: steve
c4_safe.out.05.text: Bellwether. Where the ship is. I had a feeling I would never get as far as the paperwork.

c4_escape.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.ctx.01.text: Rook put June in the east wing and me in the west, with an agent at each end of the hall. Kindly. Firmly.

c4_escape.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.ctx.02.text: The house was older than the FBI. In the service corridor, there were brass tubes in the wall.

c4_escape.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c4_escape.ctx.03.text: The van for my transfer was already parked in the transport bay, keys in it, waiting for five o’clock.

c4_escape.tube.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.lead.01.text: Pneumatic post. Dad would have loved this.

c4_escape.in.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.in.02.text: Rook is one of them. I have proof.

c4_escape.tube.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.lead.02.text: If both takes reach June, she can hear it for herself. Rook’s desk sorts everything else.

c4_escape.tube.lead.03.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.lead.03.text: The night list says June moved out of OAK, into the room across from the linen cupboard.

c4_escape.tube.lead.04.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.lead.04.text: Standard capsules stop at Rook’s desk for sorting. The blue maintenance ones go straight through.

c4_escape.tube.01.speaker: calder
c4_escape.tube.01.text: I heard both. I’ll keep his attention. You get out. We both know you can’t bluff him in person.
c4_escape.tube.01.direction: the capsule comes back with Dad’s recorder; June has recorded a reply at the end of the tape

c4_escape.in.01.speaker: calder
c4_escape.in.01.text: I don’t need you to be brave, Steve. I need you to be honest.

c4_escape.tube.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.02.text: Nobody had asked me for that since the funeral.

c4_escape.tube.find.speaker: steve
c4_escape.tube.find.text: June heard both takes, and she believes me. She’s staying with Rook to keep him busy. I have to get myself out.

c4_escape.fault.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.lead.01.text: A drill console. If a drill says the west wing has to go, they’ll have to move me. In a van.

c4_escape.fault.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.lead.02.text: Yesterday’s log says what each card does. SILVER moves the signer. BLUE moves his whole corridor. WHITE moves everyone else.

c4_escape.fault.lead.03.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.lead.03.text: The van escort signed tonight’s ticket, and he works my corridor. Four of us sleep on the west side.

c4_escape.fault.lead.04.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.lead.04.text: The house rules are pinned above it. In any alarm, a protected witness leaves in his assigned vehicle, with his assigned escort. Mine is the five o’clock van.

c4_escape.fault.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.01.text: Test circuit. No heat, no flame. Just enough bureaucracy to get us outside.

c4_escape.fault.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.02.text: The bells went off in every room. Agents in socks. Somebody holding a toothbrush. And by the rules, the witness and his escort went first, in the five o’clock van, six hours early.

c4_escape.fault.find.speaker: steve
c4_escape.fault.find.text: A BLUE drill, for real, on the escort’s own ticket. The whole west corridor, me included, goes to the transport bay, and the rules put me straight into my own transfer van. Rook stays in the east wing with June.

c4_escape.van.lead.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.lead.01.text: One escort. One rear door. And a catch that only comes off for gravel.

c4_escape.van.lead.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.lead.02.text: The driver radios before he slows. First a brick bridge over the canal, then a gravel bend.

c4_escape.van.lead.03.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.lead.03.text: After the gravel comes the weighbridge. There, the escort opens the door himself.

c4_escape.van.lead.04.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.lead.04.text: We were on the old logging road down toward Bellwether. Rook would hear about the drill within minutes. I had less than that.

c4_escape.van.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.01.text: I meant to land on my feet. The ditch had other plans.

c4_escape.van.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.02.text: The escort grabbed for me and got a handful of cardigan. His radio came away in my hand. Then I was rolling through ferns in the dark, and the van’s brake lights were already a long way down the hill.

c4_escape.van.find.speaker: steve
c4_escape.van.find.text: On the gravel bend, with the catch off, I pulled the handle and jumped for the soft side. Mostly I fell. But I fell out of the van, with the escort’s radio in my hand.

c4_escape.recap.01.speaker: steve
c4_escape.recap.01.text: June has the proof, and she chose to stay with Rook so I could run.

c4_escape.recap.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.recap.02.text: Now I was in a ditch in the hills above the bay with Dad’s recorder, a stolen radio and no plan. And the radio was still talking.

c4_escape.out.01.speaker: rook_copy
c4_escape.out.01.text: All units. Steve Mercer, wanted for the abduction of Nora Reyes. And scan Calder tonight. The signing is in six days.

c4_escape.out.02.speaker: steve
c4_escape.out.02.text: Kidnapping Nora. They took her, and I’m the one on the poster. I have to keep moving.

c4_escape.out.03.speaker: rook_copy
c4_escape.out.03.text: Roadblocks on the coast road and both bridges. Dogs at first light. He’ll head for town.

c4_escape.out.04.speaker: steve
c4_escape.out.04.text: So I didn’t. I turned the radio off, went down the creek bed instead of the road, and walked all night toward the one place nobody had opened in eighteen months.

c5_shack.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.ctx.01.text: By sunrise my face was on every wanted poster in the county. I came down out of the trees to Dad’s radio shack, on the bluff above the bay.

c5_shack.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.ctx.02.text: Their boxes were still stacked where I’d left them. I’d never been able to open them.

c5_shack.in.01.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.01.text: Food. I know where your father used to come to think.

c5_shack.in.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.in.02.text: Are you going to call the Sheriff?

c5_shack.in.04.speaker: steve
c5_shack.in.04.text: Luis. They’re saying I took Nora.

c5_shack.in.05.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.05.text: Nora has been gone since Tuesday night. Carmen hasn’t slept. And I have known you since you were nine years old.

c5_shack.in.06.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.06.text: I’ve heard the bay sing since I was a boy. Your father was the only one who ever asked me what it sounded like.

c5_shack.notes.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.lead.01.text: Forty-five years of kitchen-table notes. Every morning, one of them left the other one a note.

c5_shack.notes.01.speaker: helen
c5_shack.notes.01.text: Frank, there is soup in the refrigerator. The other container is paint. Please read both labels.

c5_shack.notes.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.02.text: I missed you both so much I stopped looking at anything you left.

c5_shack.notes.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.lead.02.text: Coltrane was Dad’s favorite record. And weather carts are the little weather tapes we played on air at KBWR.

c5_shack.notes.03.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.03.text: The good stuff. Dad’s name for the station library.

c5_shack.notes.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.notes.find.text: Dad’s “Done” answers Mom’s March 2 slip: he filed their tape between the Coltrane and the weather carts. The good stuff is the KBWR record library. Mom hid her notebook at my old station.

c5_shack.rig.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.lead.01.text: Dad’s receiver. Dead battery, and the dial’s slipped since he last used it.

c5_shack.rig.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.lead.02.text: Every set has a rating card, Dad said. Read it before you plug anything in.

c5_shack.rig.lead.03.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.lead.03.text: Dad’s rule for packs. Same volts, same center pin, and at least as much current as the card asks for.

c5_shack.rig.lead.04.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.lead.04.text: His log says the dial reads a little high. The same amount, every time.

c5_shack.rig.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.01.text: Power off. Matching connector. I’m doing it your way, Dad.

c5_shack.rig.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.rig.find.text: The BLUE pack has the right polarity and enough current. The dial reads 0.05 high, so the club’s 3.56 sits at 3.61. Dad’s radio is alive.

c5_shack.club.04.speaker: steve
c5_shack.club.04.direction: his voice catching on his father’s call sign

c5_shack.club.01.speaker: operator
c5_shack.club.01.text: K7BLW? Frank? We thought we’d lost you.

c5_shack.club.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.club.02.text: It’s Steve. Frank’s son. I need your help.

c5_shack.club.05.speaker: operator
c5_shack.club.05.text: This is Gull. It isn’t Thursday, but none of us ever really switch off. Marsh and Cedar are on too. Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point these days.

c5_shack.club.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.club.find.text: Dad’s club answered his call sign: Gull, Marsh and Cedar. Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point. They meet every Thursday, and they’ll help.

c5_shack.log.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.lead.01.text: Dad’s logbooks. Months of them. Every ninth night, the same hum under his static.

c5_shack.log.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.lead.02.text: And Mom’s handwriting in the margins. Dates, and the word Meridian, underlined twice.

c5_shack.log.lead.03.speaker: luis
c5_shack.log.lead.03.text: Your father asked me what the bay sounded like. I told him, like a whole church humming one hymn.

c5_shack.log.01.speaker: frank
c5_shack.log.01.text: It isn’t one voice. It’s a choir.

c5_shack.log.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.02.text: Dad heard voices in the hum, and he wanted my ears on it. Was that the only reason they asked me along?

c5_shack.log.find.speaker: steve
c5_shack.log.find.text: Dad’s last reel isn’t one hum. It’s many voices holding one note. “It isn’t one voice. It’s a choir.” Mom and Dad weren’t out on the bay for the view. They were investigating, and they wanted my ears.

c5_shack.talk.luis.1.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.talk.luis.1.01.text: How is Carmen holding up, Luis?

c5_shack.talk.luis.1.02.speaker: luis
c5_shack.talk.luis.1.02.text: She cooks. When she is frightened, she cooks for forty people. The freezer is full of tamales.

c5_shack.talk.luis.1.03.speaker: luis
c5_shack.talk.luis.1.03.text: Take some with you when you go. She would want you fed, even now.

c5_shack.talk.luis.2.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.talk.luis.2.01.text: Did Dad ever bring you up here?

c5_shack.talk.luis.2.02.speaker: luis
c5_shack.talk.luis.2.02.text: Every spring. He tuned that radio for hours, and I fell asleep in that chair.

c5_shack.talk.luis.2.03.speaker: luis
c5_shack.talk.luis.2.03.text: He said I snored in perfect pitch. It was the nicest thing he ever said to me.

c5_shack.talk.luis.3.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.talk.luis.3.01.text: Luis, did Nora seem different to you lately?

c5_shack.talk.luis.3.02.speaker: luis
c5_shack.talk.luis.3.02.text: Last month she let her mother win an argument about salt. Nora never lets anybody win anything.

c5_shack.talk.luis.3.03.speaker: luis
c5_shack.talk.luis.3.03.text: I thought she was finally growing up. Now I don’t know what I thought.

c5_shack.talk.operator.1.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.talk.operator.1.01.text: What did Dad talk about on Thursday nights?

c5_shack.talk.operator.1.02.speaker: operator
c5_shack.talk.operator.1.02.text: Antennas, mostly. And your mother’s soup. He described every spoonful over the air.

c5_shack.talk.operator.1.03.speaker: operator
c5_shack.talk.operator.1.03.text: Cedar always said Frank’s soup reports were the best show on the band.

c5_shack.talk.operator.2.01.speaker: operator
c5_shack.talk.operator.2.01.text: Marsh has the tallest antenna in the county, out past Sentinel Point. Says the fog up there hums at night.

c5_shack.talk.operator.2.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.talk.operator.2.02.text: Tell Marsh I’d like to hear that sometime.

c5_shack.talk.operator.2.03.speaker: operator
c5_shack.talk.operator.2.03.text: Marsh will talk your ear off, kid. Bring a thermos.

c5_shack.recap.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.recap.01.text: Mom and Dad tracked the hum for months. Dad heard a choir in it. Mom wrote Meridian in the margins.

c5_shack.recap.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.recap.02.text: Dad’s club is back on the air. And Mom’s notebook is in the KBWR record library, at the station that fired me.

c5_shack.recap.03.speaker: steve
c5_shack.recap.03.text: Twice today someone stood on the path below the shack. Both times, by the time I looked, he was gone.

c5_shack.out.01.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.01.text: The good stuff. Dad’s name for the station library. And Mom wrote my first night at the desk, not my first show.

c5_shack.out.02.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.02.text: I know where the notebook is.

c5_shack.out.03.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.03.text: And the KBWR tower is blinking. Five flashes, then dark. Last night it was six.

c5_shack.out.04.speaker: steve
c5_shack.out.04.text: Six days, Rook said. It’s counting down to the signing.

c5_station.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.ctx.01.text: KBWR, after midnight. No humans work here now. Just racks of machines, playing music to nobody.

c5_station.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.ctx.02.text: And my voice, on the station ident, still playing between the songs.

c5_station.in.01.speaker: autorick
c5_station.in.01.text: Breaking news, folks: there’s a fella in our record library!

c5_station.in.03.speaker: steve
c5_station.in.03.text: Two fellas. Somebody else is breathing in here.

c5_station.automation.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.lead.01.text: AutoRick’s console. I wrote half these carts myself.

c5_station.automation.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.lead.02.text: The maintenance door only unlatches while my ident plays. Twelve seconds. But the walk over there takes fifteen.

c5_station.automation.lead.03.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.lead.03.text: And the news cart is locked. It only plays on the hour, and it’s twenty past.

c5_station.automation.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.01.text: I built this schedule before they replaced me with it. And the door still opens for my voice.

c5_station.automation.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.automation.find.text: WEATHER gave me forty seconds to cross the room. Then my own voice, on the ident, unlatched the maintenance door.

c5_station.sleeve.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.lead.01.text: The record library. Every master we ever made, filed the way Dad taught me.

c5_station.sleeve.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.lead.02.text: Mom never wrote my first show. She wrote my first night at the desk. The engineer sits at the desk.

c5_station.sleeve.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.02.text: I knocked the whole shelf over. The blue one landed in my lap.

c5_station.sleeve.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.01.text: Mom’s handwriting. Mandarin shorthand. And this last page... I’ve never seen that script.

c5_station.sleeve.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.sleeve.find.text: My first night at the desk was the 4th, when I engineered and Jo presented. The original is in the blue sleeve, and Mom’s notebook was in its back pocket. I can’t read a word of it.

c5_station.halcyon.lead.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.lead.01.text: Halcyon Media Holdings. The company that fired me. Their filing is very tidy.

c5_station.halcyon.lead.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.lead.02.text: Three early nights in September. Halcyon said they were saving on my overtime.

c5_station.halcyon.lead.03.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.lead.03.text: And the tower log says the tower ran by itself on those same three nights.

c5_station.halcyon.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.01.text: They needed the tower, and they needed the building empty. I was the last person here.

c5_station.halcyon.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.halcyon.find.text: Halcyon sent me home early every ninth night, and the tower transmitted alone as soon as I left. Then they let me go for good. The next unattended night is November 8.

c5_station.in.02.speaker: stephen
c5_station.in.02.text: That cardigan. Is this what happens when I stop trying?

c5_station.stephen.lead.02.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.lead.02.text: It’s a good face. You’re not doing it any favors.

c5_station.stephen.lead.03.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.lead.03.text: The last thing I remember of home is breakfast in Dad’s shack. Mom’s jam jar, with the chip in the blue lid.

c5_station.stephen.lead.04.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.lead.04.text: A tape that says Mom, last call? Mom never leaves voicemails. She calls back.

c5_station.stephen.lead.05.speaker: steve
c5_station.stephen.lead.05.text: Then turn this poster over, and read it.

c5_station.stephen.01.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.01.text: Sixty-one percent. That’s what the attendant said. I assumed the rest was a compliment.

c5_station.stephen.03.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.03.text: Call me Stephen. One of us should sound like a grown-up.

c5_station.stephen.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.stephen.02.text: Sit down. There’s something you need to know.

c5_station.stephen.find.speaker: steve
c5_station.stephen.find.text: He remembers Mom’s chipped jam jar, and nothing of home after that breakfast. He doesn’t know about the boat. He doesn’t know they’re gone.

c5_station.talk.autorick.1.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.talk.autorick.1.01.text: All right, machine. What’s the weather tonight?

c5_station.talk.autorick.1.02.speaker: autorick
c5_station.talk.autorick.1.02.text: Sunny and seventy-two, folks! Perfect beach weather out there in Bellwether!

c5_station.talk.autorick.1.03.speaker: steve
c5_station.talk.autorick.1.03.text: It’s midnight in November. That was yesterday’s weather, and it was wrong then too.

c5_station.talk.autorick.2.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.talk.autorick.2.01.text: Can I make a request? Anything with a saxophone.

c5_station.talk.autorick.2.02.speaker: autorick
c5_station.talk.autorick.2.02.text: Our request line is closed! Every song is chosen with love by Halcyon Media Holdings.

c5_station.talk.autorick.2.03.speaker: steve
c5_station.talk.autorick.2.03.text: Chosen with love. By a spreadsheet in another state.

c5_station.talk.autorick.3.01.speaker: autorick
c5_station.talk.autorick.3.01.text: Good night, Bellwether! Keep one ear on the water!

c5_station.talk.autorick.3.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.talk.autorick.3.02.text: I wrote that sign-off. My first week on the night desk.

c5_station.talk.autorick.3.03.speaker: steve
c5_station.talk.autorick.3.03.text: Dad called the station the next morning just to say he heard it.

c5_station.recap.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.recap.01.text: Mom’s notebook was in the blue sleeve, in a shorthand I can’t read. Halcyon cleared the building every ninth night so the tower could talk to the ship.

c5_station.recap.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.recap.02.text: And the man following me all week was me. Sixty-one percent of me, with nothing after the breakfast before the boat.

c5_station.out.01.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.01.text: They disappeared eighteen months ago. I said no to the boat trip.

c5_station.out.02.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.02.text: No. I had breakfast with them. It never got as far as the boat.

c5_station.out.04.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.04.text: I watched my own face learn it. Eighteen months, all at once.

c5_station.out.03.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.03.text: Then that explains what I saw when I woke up. Mom and Dad are on that ship, Steve. Row nine. They’re asleep. They’re alive.

c5_station.out.05.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.05.text: You woke up on the ship.

c5_station.out.06.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.06.text: In a glass tank, last Friday. Cold, wet and sixty-one percent. A very tall man gave me a crew pass, an earpiece and a job.

c5_station.out.07.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.07.text: Find the man with my face. Find Mom’s notebook. Report in every single night.

c5_station.out.08.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.08.text: Carmen saw you at the market.

c5_station.out.09.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.09.text: She hugged me and said I looked well. I didn’t know why that made me want to cry. After that I watched June’s house all week. Today I followed you up the path to Dad’s shack. Twice.

c5_station.out.10.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.10.text: Then I heard you through the shack window. The good stuff, the station library. So I came here first, and waited for you in the dark.

c5_station.out.11.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.11.text: Then the earpiece in his hand clicked. I knew that voice. It was the one on the ship’s intercom, the one that opened my chair.

c5_station.out.12.speaker: saren
c5_station.out.12.text: Hunter. You missed your report. Where is the original?
c5_station.out.12.direction: small and clear, from the earpiece in Stephen’s hand

c5_station.out.13.speaker: steve
c5_station.out.13.text: Stephen looked at me for a long time. Then he lifted the earpiece to his ear.

c5_station.out.14.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.14.text: Not at the station. He’s gone north, toward the border. I’m following him.

c5_station.out.15.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.15.text: There. I’ve just lied to a spaceship for you. I think that makes us brothers.

c6_iris.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.ctx.01.text: Stephen and I spent the weekend in Dad’s shack, arguing about haircuts. Every night at nine, he told the earpiece I’d gone north.

c6_iris.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.ctx.02.text: On Monday morning my flip phone buzzed.

c6_iris.in.03.speaker: autorick
c6_iris.in.03.text: Police are seeking Steve Mercer, last seen wearing a cardigan. Yesterday he was sunny.

c6_iris.in.06.speaker: steve
c6_iris.in.06.text: “Pier. Eight-ten. Come alone. Please.” No capitals. Same as the warning about Rook.
c6_iris.in.06.display_text: “pier. 8:10. come alone. please.” No capitals. Same as the warning about Rook.

c6_iris.in.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.in.01.text: You hide. I’ll be charming in public. We should each use our strengths.

c6_iris.alibi.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.alibi.lead.01.text: Three errands, three clocks. Nobody in this town agrees what time it is.

c6_iris.alibi.lead.02.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.alibi.lead.02.text: Gus sets his oven clock four minutes fast. He says it keeps the bread honest.

c6_iris.alibi.lead.03.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.alibi.lead.03.text: The bus clock runs two minutes slow. The florist sets hers by the radio, like a sensible person.

c6_iris.alibi.lead.04.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.alibi.lead.04.text: And Gus has my poster in his window. He asks everyone to help him fix the smudge.

c6_iris.alibi.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.alibi.01.text: Good morning. Yes, that’s my face on the poster. Terrible photograph.

c6_iris.alibi.find.speaker: steve
c6_iris.alibi.find.text: At 8:10 by the radio, Stephen stood beside his own wanted poster at Gus’s bread window while Gus fixed the smudge. Half the town is searching the market.

c6_iris.in.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.in.02.text: I sent the message about Rook. No capitals, the way Nora texts. Please listen before you decide what I am.

c6_iris.takes.lead.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.lead.01.text: You let me go on the balcony. And on the thirtieth you stopped at the waterline and walked home. I saw you.

c6_iris.takes.lead.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.lead.02.text: The first time I missed going below, it was an accident. I was chasing you. The second time, I chose.

c6_iris.takes.lead.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.lead.03.text: Then say something for me. Twice. “I stayed because I wanted to.”

c6_iris.takes.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.01.text: I stayed because I wanted to.

c6_iris.takes.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.02.text: I stayed... because I wanted to.
c6_iris.takes.02.direction: second take; she pauses in a new place

c6_iris.takes.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.03.text: Two different takes. You’re choosing what to say.

c6_iris.takes.04.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.04.text: Before I was Nora, I was a junior crew member with a duty and a record. We call ourselves Veyri. None of us had ever had a self.

c6_iris.takes.find.speaker: steve
c6_iris.takes.find.text: Two takes, two different rhythms. Copies replay. She chose her words each time. The tell has turned around.

c6_iris.hold.lead.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.lead.01.text: You saw the ones near the bay go below. The ones far away call.

c6_iris.hold.lead.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.lead.02.text: At four minutes past midnight on the thirtieth, I phoned two Halcyon offices. I taped both calls.

c6_iris.hold.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.01.text: The signal is inside the music. Near the bay we go below. Far away, we call.

c6_iris.hold.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.hold.02.text: Rook was never waiting for the Bureau.

c6_iris.hold.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.hold.03.text: Four minutes past midnight. That’s when the water lit up.

c6_iris.hold.04.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.04.text: Saren believes your mother wrote down how the engine works. A records officer told him so. I have never seen him want anything more.

c6_iris.hold.05.speaker: iris
c6_iris.hold.05.text: And on Wednesday, at the signing, he means to put a copy of your President in her chair. Her own physician scanned her weeks ago.

c6_iris.hold.find.speaker: steve
c6_iris.hold.find.text: Both calls share the same eight bars of hold music, at the minute the water lit up. Copies near the bay go below; copies far away wait on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.

c6_iris.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.talk.iris.1.01.text: Have you seen Admiral since you went missing?

c6_iris.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.talk.iris.1.02.text: Once, at dawn on Saturday, when the pier was empty. He still won’t come to my whistle.

c6_iris.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: iris
c6_iris.talk.iris.1.03.text: He stole my sandwich anyway. I think that means we’re friends now.

c6_iris.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.talk.iris.2.01.text: Do you even like breakfast? You always said you’d eaten already.

c6_iris.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.talk.iris.2.02.text: I don’t like it. Nora doesn’t either. It was on a list of healthy things.

c6_iris.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris
c6_iris.talk.iris.2.03.text: This morning I skipped it. It felt like breaking a very small law.

c6_iris.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.talk.iris.3.01.text: I miss Sunday dinners. Carmen shouting at the stove. Tomás explaining the moon landing to the soup.

c6_iris.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.talk.iris.3.02.text: They miss you too. They think you’re Nora.

c6_iris.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: iris
c6_iris.talk.iris.3.03.text: I know. That is the part I can’t fix.

c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.01.text: Do you still think I need a haircut?

c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.talk.stephen.1.02.text: We both need one. I just look better needing it.

c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.01.text: I slept in Dad’s chair last night. It still smells of solder and peppermints.

c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.02.text: He kept the peppermints in the drawer with the fuses.

c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.talk.stephen.2.03.text: Third drawer down. I know. I remember that part.

c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.01.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.01.text: Everyone at the market is going to stare at me today.

c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.03.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.talk.stephen.3.03.text: I’ve never been the interesting one before. I could get used to it.

c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.01.speaker: autorick
c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.01.text: Police are still looking for Steve Mercer. If you see him, tell him to smile!

c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.02.speaker: stephen
c6_iris.talk.autorick.1.02.text: He never smiles before ten. I can vouch for that personally.

c6_iris.recap.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.01.text: Nora’s copy sent the warning about Rook. She stopped going into the water, and she doesn’t replay any more. She chooses.

c6_iris.recap.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.02.text: Copies far from the bay stay in step on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.

c6_iris.recap.03.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.03.text: And she told me about June. They scanned her at the safe house. Her copy took the Sheriff’s desk this morning, and the real June is in her own cell until the ninth night.

c6_iris.recap.04.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.04.text: She also told me who could get us inside: the mail carrier. Every day at four he takes the Sheriff’s mail in the back way. “He isn’t Dale,” she said. “But he loves June’s dog.”

c6_iris.out.01.speaker: iris
c6_iris.out.01.text: Those Sunday dinners happened to me. I won’t let them take them away.

c6_iris.out.03.speaker: iris
c6_iris.out.03.text: Iris. After the flowers on the balcony.

c6_iris.out.04.speaker: steve
c6_iris.out.04.text: She took a flat paper envelope out of her coat. Inside was one of the irises I knocked off the balcony on the ninth night, pressed flat.

c6_iris.out.05.speaker: iris
c6_iris.out.05.text: I picked it up after you ran. It is the first thing I ever kept that nobody told me to keep.

c6_iris.out.06.speaker: iris
c6_iris.out.06.text: I’ve slept in the otter house since Tuesday. If the crew finds me, they will reset me, and I won’t remember any of this. Not even that I chose a name.

c6_iris.out.07.speaker: iris
c6_iris.out.07.direction: quietly, to herself, trying the name on; a different reading from the first time

c6_iris.out.08.speaker: steve
c6_iris.out.08.text: It came out a little different the second time. Nothing a recording would ever do.

c6_jail.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c6_jail.ctx.01.text: The Sheriff’s office, just before four. June’s copy was out on the harbor, running the search for me. The real June was in cell two.

c6_jail.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.ctx.02.text: Stephen walked in the front door wearing my face, to contest his own poster. I came in the back, under the parcels in the mail cart.

c6_jail.in.04.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.in.04.text: The Sheriff is out on the harbor, hunting you. The Sheriff is also in cell two. One of those is a staffing problem.

c6_jail.in.01.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.01.text: I am required to report your location.

c6_jail.in.02.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.02.text: Biscuit, Steve Mercer is here. My duty is complete.

c6_jail.in.03.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.in.03.text: We should put the dog in charge.

c6_jail.in.05.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.05.text: My name is Pell. Dale is asleep on the ship. I have worn his face for a year.

c6_jail.in.06.speaker: pell
c6_jail.in.06.text: I have fed Biscuit twice a day since the Sheriff went away. If I report you properly, they will reset me, and I will not remember her.

c6_jail.mail.lead.01.speaker: pell
c6_jail.mail.lead.01.text: The cell key was returned to the post this morning. I filed it.

c6_jail.mail.lead.04.speaker: pell
c6_jail.mail.lead.04.text: I file by destination. The carbon says Jail, returned key. That is register entry eighteen.

c6_jail.mail.lead.05.speaker: pell
c6_jail.mail.lead.05.text: Each slot holds two entries. Slot one holds entries one and two, and so on.

c6_jail.mail.lead.06.speaker: pell
c6_jail.mail.lead.06.text: County rule. When a cell is used, the spare key goes back to the clerk by registered post. The Sheriff wrote that rule. Her copy follows it exactly.

c6_jail.mail.01.speaker: pell
c6_jail.mail.01.text: Correctly delivered. Biscuit may inspect the chain of custody.

c6_jail.mail.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.mail.02.text: June’s own crossword is in the jail pile. I’ll circle one square and post it through her slot.

c6_jail.mail.03.speaker: steve
c6_jail.mail.03.text: Twenty-three across, where it crosses eight down. Only the woman in cell two will see that square.

c6_jail.mail.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.mail.find.text: The key was in the Jail drawer, slot 9, where entries 17 and 18 share a slot. And on June’s crossword I circled the square where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. Only the woman in cell two will see it.

c6_jail.distract.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.distract.lead.01.text: Three tickets at the counter. Leave the deputy to me.

c6_jail.distract.lead.02.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.distract.lead.02.text: The clerk says a contested likeness sends the deputy down to the basement for the file.

c6_jail.distract.lead.03.speaker: steve
c6_jail.distract.lead.03.text: She leaves at 3:59 and she’s back at 4:03. I need two clear minutes.

c6_jail.distract.01.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.distract.01.text: I would like a better photograph. My family will be seeing these.

c6_jail.distract.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.distract.02.text: The clerk radioed the Sheriff about the cheerful man at her likeness counter. Out on the harbor, June’s copy started asking questions.

c6_jail.distract.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.distract.find.text: Stephen contested his own wanted poster at the likeness counter. The deputy went down to the basement at 3:59. At 4:00 I was in the cell corridor with the key and June’s crossword. I had until 4:02 to check her answer and get us both out.

c6_jail.crossword.lead.01.speaker: calder
c6_jail.crossword.lead.01.text: Mercer. That woman in cell two is a copy. Don’t you dare let her out.
c6_jail.crossword.lead.01.direction: over the front-desk radio, from the harbor

c6_jail.crossword.lead.02.speaker: calder
c6_jail.crossword.lead.02.text: He’ll check my paperwork, Mercer. I taught him that.

c6_jail.crossword.lead.03.speaker: steve
c6_jail.crossword.lead.03.text: I’ll ask them both which letter I circled today. Only one of them has seen it.

c6_jail.crossword.03.speaker: steve
c6_jail.crossword.03.text: Radio June said T. Close. Wrong.

c6_jail.crossword.01.speaker: calder
c6_jail.crossword.01.text: Twenty-three across. Inimitable. Unlike my colleague on the radio.

c6_jail.crossword.04.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.crossword.04.text: Sheriff, this is the hunter. Mercer just ran out the front, toward the north jetty. I’m right behind him.

c6_jail.crossword.06.speaker: steve
c6_jail.crossword.06.text: Twice in one week, Stephen had lied to his own side for me.

c6_jail.crossword.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.crossword.find.text: The June in cell two had my crossword in her hand: the M where 23 Across crosses 8 Down. The June on the radio guessed a T, so she has never been near that cell. Iris was right. By 4:02 June was out, and we were in the records room, waiting for the shift change at the back door.

c6_jail.exit.lead.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c6_jail.exit.lead.01.text: Sheriff. Steve. I’m supposed to stop you.

c6_jail.exit.lead.02.speaker: lyle_copy
c6_jail.exit.lead.02.text: Ben’s a tree in the school play this afternoon. He’s been practicing being a tree for a month.

c6_jail.exit.lead.04.speaker: calder
c6_jail.exit.lead.04.text: The school doors close at four forty. Let’s find you the fastest way there.

c6_jail.exit.01.speaker: lyle_copy
c6_jail.exit.01.text: Bus A. Twenty-nine past. They gave me a seat in the front row.

c6_jail.exit.02.speaker: calder
c6_jail.exit.02.text: Then you’d better get there. We can talk tomorrow.

c6_jail.exit.find.speaker: steve
c6_jail.exit.find.text: Lyle’s copy could still make Ben’s play: Bus A at 4:29, at the school by 4:38. He chose the front row over his orders, and let us go.

c6_jail.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: steve
c6_jail.talk.pell.1.01.text: How is Biscuit doing these days?

c6_jail.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell
c6_jail.talk.pell.1.02.text: She eats at seven and at five. She prefers the blue bowl. I am not yet sure she prefers me.

c6_jail.talk.pell.1.03.speaker: pell
c6_jail.talk.pell.1.03.text: I am working on it. I have learned to scratch behind her left ear.

c6_jail.talk.pell.2.01.speaker: steve
c6_jail.talk.pell.2.01.text: Do you like the mail route?

c6_jail.talk.pell.2.02.speaker: pell
c6_jail.talk.pell.2.02.text: Dale’s route has two hundred and twelve stops. Dale liked eleven of them.

c6_jail.talk.pell.2.03.speaker: pell
c6_jail.talk.pell.2.03.text: I have started to like a twelfth. Carmen gives me a churro at La Marea. The real Dale never stopped there.

c6_jail.talk.pell.3.01.speaker: steve
c6_jail.talk.pell.3.01.text: What is Dale like? The real one.

c6_jail.talk.pell.3.02.speaker: pell
c6_jail.talk.pell.3.02.text: He complains about the rain, the dogs and the government. In that order.

c6_jail.talk.pell.3.03.speaker: pell
c6_jail.talk.pell.3.03.text: I have his memories, but not his complaints. I find I do not miss them.

c6_jail.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.talk.stephen.1.01.text: The clerk said I looked nothing like my poster.

c6_jail.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.talk.stephen.1.02.text: It is my poster. It is literally my face.

c6_jail.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: stephen
c6_jail.talk.stephen.1.03.text: I told her that. She said I was far too cheerful to be you.

c6_jail.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder
c6_jail.talk.calder.1.01.text: I spent the morning in my own cell. That mattress is worse than I ever admitted.

c6_jail.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.talk.calder.1.02.text: You told the county the cells were fine.

c6_jail.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c6_jail.talk.calder.1.03.text: I told the county a lot of things. I’m ordering new mattresses.

c6_jail.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: calder
c6_jail.talk.calder.2.01.text: Pell has been feeding my dog? Twice a day?

c6_jail.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.talk.calder.2.02.text: Blue bowl, seven and five. He’s learned the left ear.

c6_jail.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder
c6_jail.talk.calder.2.03.text: Then he can keep his job. Don’t you dare tell him I said that.

c6_jail.talk.calder.3.01.speaker: calder
c6_jail.talk.calder.3.01.text: She does my paperwork better than I do. That’s what bothers me most.

c6_jail.talk.calder.3.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.talk.calder.3.02.text: She guessed a T, June. She didn’t know you.

c6_jail.talk.calder.3.03.speaker: calder
c6_jail.talk.calder.3.03.text: No. She knew my files. That isn’t the same thing at all.

c6_jail.recap.01.speaker: steve
c6_jail.recap.01.text: June is out of her cell, and her copy is out at the north jetty, looking for me. Pell chose a beagle over his orders. Lyle’s copy chose a school play.

c6_jail.recap.02.speaker: steve
c6_jail.recap.02.text: Five fugitives and a beagle. We needed a car nobody would look for.

c6_jail.recap.03.speaker: steve
c6_jail.recap.03.text: Iris was waiting behind Gus’s bakery next door, where nobody would see Nora’s face.

c6_jail.out.02.speaker: gus
c6_jail.out.02.text: Take the van. I don’t know why, but I trust you.
c6_jail.out.02.direction: at the bakery loading door, holding out the keys to a van with a giant croissant on its roof

c6_jail.out.04.speaker: steve
c6_jail.out.04.text: Iris. The ring in my sock drawer. Did Nora ever find it?

c6_jail.out.01.speaker: iris
c6_jail.out.01.text: Nora found the ring a year ago. It is not mine to answer.

c6_jail.out.05.speaker: iris
c6_jail.out.05.text: A copy who stops going below starts to forget. Nora’s memories go first.

c6_jail.out.03.speaker: iris
c6_jail.out.03.text: We’re starting to forget. Stephen and I have days.

i2_nora.ctx.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.ctx.01.text: I woke up in amber light, in a bed I didn’t choose, in a hall that went on forever.

i2_nora.ctx.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.ctx.02.text: I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.

i2_nora.in.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.in.01.text: I can move my hand. That’s a start.

i2_nora.in.02.speaker: dale
i2_nora.in.02.text: If this is a hospital, I’m changing hospitals.

i2_nora.in.03.speaker: nora
i2_nora.in.03.text: Names first. Complaints after we have a plan.

i2_nora.patrol.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.patrol.lead.01.text: Boots. Then the pump. Then the far door. Again and again.

i2_nora.patrol.lead.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.patrol.lead.02.text: Once that far door shuts, he can’t see the aisle. Crossing takes me four counts.

i2_nora.patrol.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.patrol.01.text: Wait. Now. Keep low. We can argue about my tone after we’re out.

i2_nora.patrol.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.patrol.find.text: The guard’s lap is twelve counts. On the next lap the far door shuts at 20 and the boots come back at 26. Four counts to cross. We can move.

i2_nora.jobs.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.jobs.lead.01.text: Everybody’s good at something. Even Dale.

i2_nora.jobs.lead.02.speaker: lyle
i2_nora.jobs.lead.02.text: That hatch sticks. I’ve wedged it open twice already tonight.

i2_nora.jobs.lead.03.speaker: dale
i2_nora.jobs.lead.03.text: Thirty years on a mail route. I could walk this one with my eyes shut.

i2_nora.jobs.01.speaker: lyle
i2_nora.jobs.01.text: I can keep that latch from catching.

i2_nora.jobs.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.jobs.find.text: Lyle keeps the hatch from catching. Dale remembers every turn. I take the pumps. Water is the one thing on this ship I understand.

i2_nora.pump.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.lead.01.text: Three service branches. Let’s see what each one does.

i2_nora.pump.lead.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.lead.02.text: The top dial reads an empty wash line. Ignore it. Watch the return and the bed flow.

i2_nora.pump.lead.03.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.lead.03.text: Bed flow has to stay at three or more. The return has to drop below three.

i2_nora.pump.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.01.text: Pressure down. Nobody’s breathing changes. That’s our route.

i2_nora.pump.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.pump.find.text: The Blue branch keeps the beds at 4 and drops the RETURN to 2. The hatch can open, and nobody’s breathing changes.

i2_nora.message.lead.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.message.lead.01.text: If he comes. When he comes. He’ll come.

i2_nora.message.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.message.01.text: Steve, if you ever hear this message: I am furious with you. I love you. Please stop making me do both alone.
i2_nora.message.01.display_text: Nora records a private message for Steve.

i2_nora.message.find.speaker: nora
i2_nora.message.find.text: My message for Steve is in Slot B, by my bed. It will wait for him.

i2_nora.talk.dale.1.02.speaker: dale
i2_nora.talk.dale.1.02.text: Cold, stiff and starving. If this is a hospital, the food is terrible.

i2_nora.talk.dale.1.03.speaker: nora
i2_nora.talk.dale.1.03.text: There isn’t any food here, Dale.

i2_nora.talk.dale.1.04.speaker: dale
i2_nora.talk.dale.1.04.text: That is exactly my point, Nora.

i2_nora.talk.dale.2.01.speaker: dale
i2_nora.talk.dale.2.01.text: Who is feeding June Calder’s beagle? I carry biscuits in my bag for her every morning.

i2_nora.talk.dale.2.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.talk.dale.2.02.text: I’m sure somebody is looking after Biscuit.

i2_nora.talk.dale.2.03.speaker: dale
i2_nora.talk.dale.2.03.text: Somebody had better be. She sulks at anyone who forgets.

i2_nora.talk.dale.3.01.speaker: dale
i2_nora.talk.dale.3.01.text: Left at the pipes, right at the cold one, straight past the humming wall.

i2_nora.talk.dale.3.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.talk.dale.3.02.text: You really did learn the whole route.

i2_nora.talk.dale.3.03.speaker: dale
i2_nora.talk.dale.3.03.text: Mail carriers never forget a route, Nora. We only forget birthdays.

i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.01.speaker: lyle
i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.01.text: My boys have a game on Saturday. I’ve missed most of their games this year.

i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.02.text: Then you’ll make the next one, Lyle.

i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.03.speaker: lyle
i2_nora.talk.lyle.1.03.text: Every single one, when I get out of here. I swear it.

i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.01.speaker: lyle
i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.01.text: I should be at work. Somebody must be covering my shifts.

i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.02.text: I think somebody probably is, Lyle.

i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.03.speaker: lyle
i2_nora.talk.lyle.2.03.text: Then I hope he’s nicer to Steve Mercer than I was.

i2_nora.recap.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.recap.01.text: I know every name in my row now. I have a route, a crew and a pump that behaves.

i2_nora.recap.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.recap.02.text: The hardest part is the waiting. I have never waited quietly for anything. Between patrols I lie still and think about a man who went quiet for eighteen months.

i2_nora.out.01.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.01.text: Helen. Frank. Steve is going to be so glad.

i2_nora.out.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.02.text: Mrs. Penhallow? Row three. I should remember that.

i2_nora.out.03.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.03.text: And you, under the frost... you can hear me, can’t you?

i2_nora.out.04.speaker: nora
i2_nora.out.04.text: Under the frost, something opened one enormous eye. It looked at me. Then it closed again.

c7_gate.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.ctx.01.text: Sentinel Point. An old antenna field in the fog north of town, flags on every mast, and the President of the United States due at noon.

c7_gate.in.03.speaker: steve
c7_gate.in.03.text: We spent Tuesday in the back room of Gus’s bakery, planning on flour sacks.

c7_gate.in.04.speaker: steve
c7_gate.in.04.text: We couldn’t call anyone. The FBI’s man at the signing was Rook’s copy, and Rook’s list had names in Washington.

c7_gate.in.05.speaker: steve
c7_gate.in.05.text: So we used what we had. Halcyon runs the sound for the signing, Stephen still has their crew pass, and Dad’s tape has the tone.

c7_gate.in.06.speaker: steve
c7_gate.in.06.text: June wrote to the President in her own hand. Pell would deliver it the way he delivers everything: into the right hand, on time.

c7_gate.in.07.speaker: steve
c7_gate.in.07.text: Gus had two catering passes for the press tent. June and Iris would use them at the red window, at ten past eleven, on foot, in his aprons and hairnets, carrying croissants.

c7_gate.in.01.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.in.01.text: Crew credentials. Loyal asset. Very important face.

c7_gate.badge.lead.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.badge.lead.01.text: My face is on every poster in the county. So is yours.

c7_gate.badge.lead.02.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.lead.02.text: Then one of us should hide. I vote you.

c7_gate.badge.lead.03.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.lead.03.text: The gate card has three windows. Red at 11:10 is for deliveries on foot. No vehicles at all.

c7_gate.badge.lead.04.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.lead.04.text: Gold at 11:50 is for the signers. The President’s guards search every vehicle with dogs.

c7_gate.badge.lead.05.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.lead.05.text: Blue at 11:30 is for crew trucks. The guard scans the driver’s pass. If it shows green, the truck rolls through.

c7_gate.badge.lead.06.speaker: steve
c7_gate.badge.lead.06.text: And I have no pass at all. So the guard can’t be allowed to see me.

c7_gate.badge.02.speaker: rook_copy
c7_gate.badge.02.direction: at the gate, holding up a wanted poster

c7_gate.badge.03.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.03.text: I get that a lot. Scan me.

c7_gate.badge.05.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.05.text: He’s very close. I can feel it.

c7_gate.badge.01.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.badge.01.text: I’m expected. I’m usually expected everywhere.

c7_gate.badge.find.speaker: steve
c7_gate.badge.find.text: Blue window, 11:30. Stephen drove, his pass scanned green, and I rode under the sound desk. Rook’s copy waved us through and wished Stephen luck finding me.

c7_gate.in.02.speaker: pell
c7_gate.in.02.text: Registered mail for the President. Delivery cannot be delayed.

c7_gate.post.lead.01.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.lead.01.text: Registered mail goes into the addressee’s own hand. Nobody else may sign for her.

c7_gate.post.lead.02.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.lead.02.text: The press desk only stamps handouts for reporters. The stage door only signs for scenery.

c7_gate.post.lead.03.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.lead.03.text: The delegation clerk can call the President to her hatch in person.

c7_gate.post.lead.04.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.lead.04.text: She signs the white sheet, and her pen presses through to the yellow carbon underneath. The white sheet stays with her.

c7_gate.post.01.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.01.text: President Ward. Your letter. On time.

c7_gate.post.03.speaker: ward
c7_gate.post.03.text: Ribbon burn on my left wrist, from the accord folder. My first wound in office.

c7_gate.post.04.speaker: pell
c7_gate.post.04.text: Eleven fifty-four. Left wrist, bandaged. Noted for the record.
c7_gate.post.04.direction: writing on the counterfoil, then saluting

c7_gate.post.find.speaker: steve
c7_gate.post.find.text: Pell put the letter into Ward’s own hand at the delegation hatch at 11:54 and came back with the yellow carbon. And a note for the record: left wrist, bandaged. A fresh ribbon burn.

c7_gate.truck.lead.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.truck.lead.01.text: I climbed out from under the sound desk, tripped over a cable and fell straight into the shot of a live television camera.

c7_gate.truck.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.truck.01.text: Sound check. I’m supposed to be under the desk.

c7_gate.truck.02.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.02.text: Evelyn Shaw. I ran the sound stage for Meridian, back when it had a budget. Stay off the cables.

c7_gate.truck.lead.02.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.lead.02.text: The back fence failed the check. Sound crosses three hundred and forty meters in a second, and the fence is a hundred and seventy meters out. Tell me what it actually heard.

c7_gate.truck.lead.03.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.lead.03.text: The camera monitor shows the click the moment it leaves this desk.

c7_gate.truck.lead.04.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.lead.04.text: The stage van shows the television feed. That runs two seconds late, because of the satellite.

c7_gate.truck.03.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.truck.03.text: Half a second. Good ears. Who taught you?

c7_gate.truck.find.speaker: steve
c7_gate.truck.find.text: Sound covers 170 meters in half a second. The fence-line strip in the Halcyon truck shows the click at 0.5 s, so the fence hears the desk. Every speaker on the site is mine.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.01.text: Can you see the trucks from here? I can barely see my own feet.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.02.text: Good. Fog is very flattering. Nobody looks like a wanted poster in fog.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Dad used to say fog makes every sound feel closer.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.04.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.stephen.1.04.text: He said it on the boat, every summer. I remember that one. I think I do.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.01.text: I had two croissants from Gus this morning. He gave me a third one for free.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.02.text: He thinks you’re me, Stephen. My face is on every poster.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.stephen.2.03.text: He said the poster doesn’t do me justice. He’s right, you know.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.01.text: Rook’s copy wished you luck finding me.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.02.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.02.text: I told him the truth. You’re very close. You’re under the sound desk.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.03.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.03.text: Please stop enjoying this so much.

c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.04.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.stephen.3.04.text: I can’t. This is the most fun I’ve had in my whole short life.

c7_gate.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.pell.1.01.text: Who is looking after Biscuit today?

c7_gate.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: pell
c7_gate.talk.pell.1.02.text: The Sheriff’s neighbor. I left written instructions. Four pages, with diagrams.

c7_gate.talk.pell.1.04.speaker: pell
c7_gate.talk.pell.1.04.text: She is a very important beagle. She has a schedule.

c7_gate.talk.pell.2.01.speaker: pell
c7_gate.talk.pell.2.01.text: Dale’s route has two hundred and twelve mailboxes. I know every one of them.

c7_gate.talk.pell.2.02.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.pell.2.02.text: Do you actually like the work?

c7_gate.talk.pell.2.03.speaker: pell
c7_gate.talk.pell.2.03.text: I like the dogs, and the people who say thank you. Mostly the dogs.

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.01.speaker: rook_copy
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.01.text: The coffee in the press tent is terrible. I’ve had four cups.

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.02.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.02.text: You don’t seem to mind it very much.

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.03.speaker: rook_copy
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.1.03.text: Rook takes his coffee black. I keep putting sugar in mine. I don’t know why.

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.01.speaker: rook_copy
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.01.text: Do you ever think about him? The one you were made from?

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.02.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.02.text: Every single day. He snores, apparently.

c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.03.speaker: rook_copy
c7_gate.talk.rook_copy.2.03.text: I wonder if mine dreams. Down there, in the cold.

c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.01.text: This truck is older than you are. I rewired half of it myself.

c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.talk.shaw.1.03.text: Of course it does. I have good ears too. Mine are just older.

c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.01.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.01.text: Before this, I built explosions for the movies. Six films, and never one real fire.

c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.02.speaker: steve
c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.02.text: And now you run sound checks in the fog?

c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.03.speaker: shaw
c7_gate.talk.shaw.2.03.text: The government pays worse. But the sandwiches are better.

c7_gate.recap.01.speaker: steve
c7_gate.recap.01.text: We were in. Stephen as a loyal asset, Pell as the mail, and me at the sound desk with Dad’s tape of the ninth-night tone.

c7_gate.recap.02.speaker: steve
c7_gate.recap.02.text: Ward signed for Pell’s letter at 11:54, with a fresh bandage on her left wrist. The public ceremony starts at 11:58.

c7_gate.recap.03.speaker: steve
c7_gate.recap.03.text: June and Iris were already inside, in hairnets, somewhere near the service tunnel. Iris knew the crew’s routes. She used to walk them.

c7_gate.out.04.speaker: steve
c7_gate.out.04.text: If they swap her, it happens between the hatch and the podium.

c7_gate.out.05.speaker: stephen
c7_gate.out.05.text: So we watch the hatch. I’m very good at being looked at.

c7_gate.out.06.speaker: steve
c7_gate.out.06.text: In the fog between the antennas, an old woman was walking a dog. Mrs. Penhallow. Miles from her pier, again.

c7_swap.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c7_swap.ctx.01.text: Every ninth night, when the bay sounds that tone, every copy near Bellwether walks to the water. Dad taped it.

c7_swap.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.ctx.02.text: If it played on every speaker at once, every copy on the site would answer it at once. In front of everybody.

c7_swap.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c7_swap.ctx.03.text: At ten to twelve, the earpiece in Stephen’s hand stopped asking him for reports. It asked for me, by name.

c7_swap.in.01.speaker: saren
c7_swap.in.01.text: Your parents’ records are in good order, Mr. Mercer. So is mine. I have never been wrong on the record. Not on Tirel, and not here.
c7_swap.in.01.direction: through Stephen’s earpiece, which Stephen holds out to Steve

c7_swap.map.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.lead.01.text: I just gave the press a short interview. They loved me. Now, four feeds and one President. Possibly two.

c7_swap.map.lead.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.map.lead.02.text: Iris said Ward’s own doctor scanned her weeks ago. A copy made back then can’t know about this morning.

c7_swap.map.lead.03.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.lead.03.text: And this morning she burned her left wrist on the folder. Pell wrote it down. Left wrist, bandaged.

c7_swap.map.lead.04.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.lead.04.text: Podium camera. The woman at the lectern just waved. Her left wrist is bare.

c7_swap.map.lead.05.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.lead.05.text: Stair camera. The doctor is helping a patient down the east stair. Her left wrist is bandaged.

c7_swap.map.lead.06.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.lead.06.text: The east stair only goes to one door, into the service tunnel. And the lift went down empty.

c7_swap.map.01.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.map.01.text: Service tunnel, east stairs. The doctor has the real President.

c7_swap.map.03.speaker: saren
c7_swap.map.03.text: Mr. Mercer, the sound desk is a very small room.

c7_swap.map.find.speaker: steve
c7_swap.map.find.text: The woman at the lectern has a bare wrist, so she was made from the old scan. The real Ward, with this morning’s bandage, went down the east stair with the physician into the service tunnel. June and Iris are going after her.

c7_swap.bus.lead.02.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.bus.lead.02.text: Three sends. Amber reaches the lectern and the press van. Green reaches the back fence and the service steps.

c7_swap.bus.lead.03.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.bus.lead.03.text: Blue reaches the lectern, the back fence and the service steps.

c7_swap.bus.lead.04.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.bus.lead.04.text: The press van feeds the national broadcast. Keep your tone off it, or every copy watching at home hears it too.

c7_swap.bus.lead.05.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.bus.lead.05.text: For June’s reply, three returns. Copper goes to you, Stephen and the lectern speaker.

c7_swap.bus.lead.06.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.bus.lead.06.text: Slate goes to you and Stephen. Pearl goes to you alone.

c7_swap.bus.lead.07.speaker: steve
c7_swap.bus.lead.07.text: June’s reply is for Stephen and me. Nobody else.

c7_swap.bus.01.speaker: steve
c7_swap.bus.01.text: All-call. Enough level to reach the back fence. Leave the microphone clear.

c7_swap.bus.find.speaker: steve
c7_swap.bus.find.text: The tone goes out on Blue: the lectern, the back fence and the service steps, but not the press van. June’s reply comes back on Slate, to Stephen and me alone.

c7_swap.tone.lead.01.speaker: calder
c7_swap.tone.lead.01.text: Service tunnel. We see them. Give us a few seconds.

c7_swap.tone.lead.02.speaker: calder
c7_swap.tone.lead.02.text: The team gets to the patient at 11:58 and fourteen seconds. Not one second sooner.

c7_swap.tone.lead.03.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.tone.lead.03.text: The speakers switch to the anthem at eighteen seconds past. Your tone runs two seconds. It has to finish before then.

c7_swap.tone.03.speaker: steve
c7_swap.tone.03.text: Fourteen people stopped in the fog and turned toward the sea.

c7_swap.tone.01.speaker: steve
c7_swap.tone.01.text: Fourteen. Rook. The physician. The woman at the microphone.

c7_swap.tone.04.speaker: calder
c7_swap.tone.04.text: She has my letter. She read it by flashlight in the tunnel, and she believes us. She wants to meet the man at the sound desk.

c7_swap.tone.find.speaker: steve
c7_swap.tone.find.text: At 11:58:15 Dad’s tone went out on every site speaker. Fourteen people stopped and turned toward the sea, the woman at the microphone among them. June and Iris had the real President.

c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: steve
c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.01.text: What did the press ask you?

c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.02.text: My favorite food. I said Sunday dinner at La Marea. Then I wasn’t sure whose memory that was.

c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: steve
c7_swap.talk.stephen.1.03.text: It belongs to both of us. It was a good answer.

c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.01.text: My hands are shaking. Are yours shaking too?

c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.02.text: They’ve been shaking since six this morning.

c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen
c7_swap.talk.stephen.2.03.text: Good. I was worried it was only me.

c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.01.text: The last time I sat at a desk out here, four generals stood behind me.

c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.02.text: Were they as nervous as I am?

c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.talk.shaw.1.03.text: Less. Breathe, Mercer. The tape won’t play any faster if you hold your breath.

c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.01.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.01.text: Your father’s tape is in good shape. Who stored it?

c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.02.text: He did. Cool and dry, and labeled in pencil. He labeled everything.

c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.03.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.talk.shaw.2.03.text: Then I would have hired him in a heartbeat.

c7_swap.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder
c7_swap.talk.calder.1.01.text: Iris is right beside me. She’s counting her steps out loud.

c7_swap.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.talk.calder.1.02.text: Is she all right down there?

c7_swap.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c7_swap.talk.calder.1.03.text: She says she’s fine. She says it the way you always do.

c7_swap.recap.01.speaker: steve
c7_swap.recap.01.text: Fourteen copies turned toward the sea at once, in front of everyone who mattered. The real President was in a service tunnel, with a bandaged wrist and June Calder.

c7_swap.recap.02.speaker: steve
c7_swap.recap.02.text: Iris told me later that the tone pulled at her too. She held on to June’s sleeve and counted Sunday dinners until it passed.

c7_swap.recap.03.speaker: steve
c7_swap.recap.03.text: Rook’s copy slipped away into the fog. Before he went, he asked me one thing.

c7_swap.out.01.speaker: rook_copy
c7_swap.out.01.text: Is he awake? The other one?

c7_swap.out.04.speaker: steve
c7_swap.out.04.text: An hour later, in a locked room under the array, the President of the United States thanked me.

c7_swap.out.02.speaker: ward
c7_swap.out.02.text: Thank you, Mr. Mercer. Their Prefect wants one thing from us by the ninth night. Our space-fold engine.

c7_gate.out.01.speaker: wen
c7_gate.out.01.text: Lin Wen. I was the other side’s engineer at Sentinel Point, nine years ago. Helen wrote this? Where is she?
c7_gate.out.01.direction: seeing the notebook in Steve’s hand

c7_gate.out.02.speaker: steve
c7_gate.out.02.text: Asleep under the bay. Can you read it?

c7_gate.out.03.speaker: wen
c7_gate.out.03.text: This page... Madam President. He should hear it from us.

c7_swap.out.05.speaker: ward
c7_swap.out.05.text: Now we owe you an explanation.

c7_swap.out.03.speaker: shaw
c7_swap.out.03.text: There is no engine. There never was.

p_meeting.ctx.01.speaker: wen
p_meeting.ctx.01.text: Your mother’s shorthand. Sentinel Point, nine years ago. I was in that room.

p_meeting.in.01.speaker: general_us
p_meeting.in.01.text: We are prepared to discuss the practical status of our demonstration.

p_meeting.in.02.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.in.02.text: After you explain the difference between practical and actual.

p_meeting.terms.lead.02.speaker: helen
