p_meeting.terms.lead.02.text: My card had two words he might use. One meant a technical demonstration. The other meant a performance, as on a stage.

p_meeting.terms.lead.03.speaker: helen
p_meeting.terms.lead.03.text: My rule never changes. An interpreter adds nothing and removes nothing.

p_meeting.terms.03.speaker: general_us
p_meeting.terms.03.text: Performances. Yes. That is... a fair word.

p_meeting.terms.02.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.terms.02.text: That would be a useful place to begin.

p_meeting.terms.find.speaker: helen
p_meeting.terms.find.text: He said biaoyan, a performance, as on a stage. I translated it exactly and noted that he chose it. The American heard the word and did not argue.

p_meeting.confess.lead.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.confess.lead.01.text: Both men were waiting for the other to blink. Somebody had to ask the first question, and it had to be me.

p_meeting.confess.lead.02.speaker: general_us
p_meeting.confess.lead.02.text: Our observers saw a ring of light on your screen. We were never allowed inside your room.

p_meeting.confess.lead.03.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.confess.lead.03.text: Our observers saw a ring of light on yours. We never went inside your room either.

p_meeting.confess.lead.04.speaker: helen
p_meeting.confess.lead.04.text: Each man could only speak for his own machine. And the joint minutes would be read by the whole world.

p_meeting.confess.02.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.confess.02.text: There was no engine at our test either.

p_meeting.confess.03.speaker: helen
p_meeting.confess.03.text: Then we can discuss what to do next.

p_meeting.confess.find.speaker: helen
p_meeting.confess.find.text: Each delegate described his own machine, and neither had an engine. In the joint minutes we wrote only what both sides saw: a ring of light.

p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.01.text: Coffee, General? It comes from the machine in the hall.

p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.02.speaker: general_us
p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.02.text: Is it any good, Mrs. Mercer?

p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.03.speaker: helen
p_meeting.talk.general_us.1.03.text: No. But it is hot, and it doesn’t pretend to be anything else.

p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.01.speaker: general_us
p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.01.text: We put our test out on open radio. Every ham in three states heard it.

p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.02.speaker: helen
p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.02.text: My husband is a ham. He talked about it at dinner for a week.

p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.03.speaker: general_us
p_meeting.talk.general_us.2.03.text: Then I hope your husband enjoyed the show.

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.01.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.01.text: Your building has no windows, Mrs. Mercer. And no tea.

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.02.speaker: helen
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.02.text: I brought my own. Jasmine. There is enough for two.

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.03.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.1.03.text: Then this meeting has already gone better than I expected.

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.01.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.01.text: You choose your words very carefully. Who taught you?

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.02.speaker: helen
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.02.text: My mother. Now my son corrects me. He records everything, even the kettle.

p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.03.speaker: general_cn
p_meeting.talk.general_cn.2.03.text: A family of listeners. That is rare these days.

p_meeting.recap.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.recap.01.text: Both demonstrations were staged. Both sides admitted it, in this room, to each other. Then they agreed to keep lying, together.

p_meeting.record.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.record.01.text: Dates. Names. What each person actually said. Someone may need the truth one day.

p_meeting.out.02.speaker: helen
p_meeting.out.02.text: When they understood that they had bluffed each other, the whole room laughed. Tired laughter. The kind that lets you breathe.

p_meeting.out.01.speaker: helen
p_meeting.out.01.text: Everyone agreed to keep lying. It may be the most honest thing I have seen.

c8_lab.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c8_lab.ctx.01.text: Shaw took us into the Meridian laboratory. It was a film set. The doors were painted on the walls.

c8_lab.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c8_lab.ctx.02.text: The reactor was a stack of washing-machine drums, theater lights and a fog machine.

c8_lab.in.01.speaker: wen
c8_lab.in.01.text: Your mother wrote ‘heard this before’ beside a drum beat that isn’t there. I want to know where she heard it.

c8_lab.in.05.speaker: wen
c8_lab.in.05.text: Mine fooled six. And a premier.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.01.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.01.text: Help me put her pages back in order.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.02.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.02.text: This scrap is the American test. Two drum strikes, a missing beat, then a lamp flare.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.03.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.03.text: This one is our test. Before we built it, we were sent a copy of the American test to study.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.text: Both tests went out over open radio. Anyone with a receiver could hear them.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.text: And the minutes of the meeting at one table quote both tests. Your mother was in that room.

c8_lab.notebook.01.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.01.text: They heard the demonstrations nine years ago. They came here three years ago. We called them without knowing anyone was listening.

c8_lab.notebook.02.speaker: steve
c8_lab.notebook.02.text: Heard this before. Mom heard that missing beat in the bay. In Dad’s reels.

c8_lab.notebook.find.speaker: steve
c8_lab.notebook.find.text: America staged its test first, and China built its own from a copy, missing beat and all. Both went out over open radio, and something out there recorded them. Mom heard that same missing beat again, in the bay. The fleet came because of a show.

c8_lab.props.lead.01.speaker: shaw
c8_lab.props.lead.01.text: Film log’s on the clipboard. Tell me what you see.

c8_lab.props.lead.02.speaker: shaw
c8_lab.props.lead.02.text: Drums, lamps and fog. If two effects hit on the very same frames, one cue can drive them both.

c8_lab.props.lead.03.speaker: shaw
c8_lab.props.lead.03.text: Ignore anything marked rehearsal. That was me testing bulbs.

c8_lab.props.01.speaker: shaw
c8_lab.props.01.text: Those drums survived six films and a congressional visit. They can manage one more show.

c8_lab.props.02.speaker: steve
c8_lab.props.02.text: They fell for a show once. So we put on another one. Live, this time.

c8_lab.props.find.speaker: steve
c8_lab.props.find.text: The drums and lamps hit together on frames 120, 128 and 136; the fog just drifts. One cue drives the whole effect. Shaw’s reactor can play again, and this time we play it live.

c8_lab.lastpage.lead.01.speaker: wen
c8_lab.lastpage.lead.01.text: Beside it she wrote: “From Frank’s tapes. I cannot read it, but I know a language when I hear one.”

c8_lab.lastpage.lead.02.speaker: wen
c8_lab.lastpage.lead.02.text: Three strokes. The second joins the first and climbs higher. Then a gap. Then a long stroke, lower than both.

c8_lab.lastpage.lead.03.speaker: steve
c8_lab.lastpage.lead.03.text: Dad wrote the pitch on every reel. A higher number means a higher note.

c8_lab.lastpage.01.speaker: wen
c8_lab.lastpage.01.text: I can read Helen’s shorthand. This is something else.

c8_lab.lastpage.find.speaker: steve
c8_lab.lastpage.find.text: Mom’s last page is Dad’s Reel 11: two joined tones rising, 220 to 330, a half-second gap, then a long 165, lower than both. Her margin says it repeats after the low note. It’s a language, and nobody on Earth can read it.

c8_lab.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: steve
c8_lab.talk.wen.1.01.text: You knew my mother nine years ago. What was she like in that room?

c8_lab.talk.wen.1.02.speaker: wen
c8_lab.talk.wen.1.02.text: Tired, like all of us. But she brought a tin of lemon cookies and shared them with both sides.

c8_lab.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen
c8_lab.talk.wen.1.03.text: Nobody refuses a cookie from the interpreter. It was very clever of her.

c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.speaker: wen
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.text: I walked here from the hotel. An old woman with a dog said good morning to me in Mandarin.

c8_lab.talk.wen.2.02.speaker: steve
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.02.text: In Mandarin? Out here in Bellwether?

c8_lab.talk.wen.2.03.speaker: wen
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.03.text: Perfect Mandarin. Then she asked me if I needed any bait.

c8_lab.talk.wen.3.01.speaker: steve
c8_lab.talk.wen.3.01.text: How long have you two known each other?

c8_lab.talk.wen.3.02.speaker: wen
c8_lab.talk.wen.3.02.text: Nine years. We were enemies for one week and friends ever since.

c8_lab.talk.wen.3.03.speaker: wen
c8_lab.talk.wen.3.03.text: She still owes me a dinner. She lost a bet about the fog machine.

c8_lab.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: shaw
c8_lab.talk.shaw.1.02.text: Six of them, from a laundromat in Reno. The owner thought I was starting a business.

c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.01.speaker: shaw
c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.01.text: Thirty years of explosions, and I can still hear a mouse cough in the next room.

c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.02.speaker: steve
c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.02.text: So can I. It makes the cinema very hard.

c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.03.speaker: shaw
c8_lab.talk.shaw.2.03.text: Sit in the back row. Nobody coughs in the back row.

c8_lab.recap.01.speaker: steve
c8_lab.recap.01.text: Two countries faked two tests and broadcast them on open radio. Something out there was listening, and it came. Mom heard the proof in the bay.

c8_lab.recap.02.speaker: steve
c8_lab.recap.02.text: Shaw’s reactor still works, if one cue drives the drums and lamps. And Mom’s last page is a language from Dad’s tapes that nobody can read.

c8_lab.out.03.speaker: steve
c8_lab.out.03.text: Mrs. Penhallow was standing by the reactor. Nobody had seen her come in.

c8_lab.out.01.speaker: agnes
c8_lab.out.01.text: A lie is only shameful when it’s lazy, Steven.

c8_lab.out.05.speaker: steve
c8_lab.out.05.text: When I turned round, she was gone.

c8_lab.out.02.speaker: saren
c8_lab.out.02.text: Midnight tomorrow, Madam President. The ninth night. The engine, or the scan resumes.
c8_lab.out.02.direction: from every screen and radio in the county

c8_lab.out.06.speaker: saren
c8_lab.out.06.text: And Mr. Mercer. Come down to the beach at dawn. Alone.

c8_beach.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c8_beach.ctx.01.text: Dawn on the beach. Saren came alone, the way he said he would: taller than the doorframes on his ship, and perfectly still.

c8_beach.in.01.speaker: saren
c8_beach.in.01.text: Give me the notebook. Helen and Frank will walk out of the sea tomorrow morning.

c8_beach.in.04.speaker: saren
c8_beach.in.04.text: Your mother would like a word.

c8_beach.second.lead.01.speaker: helen
c8_beach.second.lead.01.text: Come out with us, kiddo. Tonight.
c8_beach.second.lead.01.direction: from a small device in Saren’s hand; a splice, made by editing recording.voicemail

c8_beach.second.lead.02.speaker: steve
c8_beach.second.lead.02.text: I know every breath of her voicemail. Let me play it right next to this.
c8_beach.second.lead.02.direction: taking Dad’s recorder out of his cardigan pocket

c8_beach.second.02.speaker: steve
c8_beach.second.02.text: Same breath before ‘kiddo’. And a hole where four words used to be.

c8_beach.second.find.speaker: steve
c8_beach.second.find.text: Saren’s message is Mom’s voicemail, cut and stitched: the same breath before ‘kiddo’, and a gap where ‘The bay is singing’ used to be. He has no message from her. He has my tape.

c8_beach.refuse.01.speaker: steve
c8_beach.refuse.01.text: That’s my voicemail. You cut my mother out of her own message. No. You don’t get to trade the whole town for my family.

c8_beach.refuse.find.speaker: steve
c8_beach.refuse.find.text: I kept the notebook. Saren had a promise, my mother’s voice cut to fit it, and nothing else.

c8_beach.recap.01.speaker: steve
c8_beach.recap.01.text: Saren offered me my parents for Mom’s notebook. His proof was my own voicemail, cut to say what he wanted.

c8_beach.recap.02.speaker: steve
c8_beach.recap.02.text: I said no. And for the first time I wondered how many times he’d done this before.

c8_beach.out.01.speaker: steve
c8_beach.out.01.text: How many families on Tirel got a message like that?

c8_beach.out.04.speaker: steve
c8_beach.out.04.text: He was quiet for a long time.

c8_rig.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c8_rig.ctx.01.text: Back at Sentinel Point, I told them the plan. It had a lot of holes. Shaw filled most of them with gaffer tape.

c8_rig.in.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.in.02.text: I know. That is why it has to be a show.

c8_rig.in.04.speaker: iris
c8_rig.in.04.text: Before you decide. Every sleeper you wake cuts one of us loose, and that one starts to forget. Stephen too.

c8_rig.in.05.speaker: steve
c8_rig.in.05.text: Then it isn’t my decision alone.

c8_rig.in.03.speaker: iris
c8_rig.in.03.text: Wake them. Even if we start forgetting. I vote to do it.

c8_rig.in.06.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.in.06.text: Seconded. I’ll write things on my hand.

c8_rig.in.07.speaker: steve
c8_rig.in.07.text: Here’s the show. We stage the test again, live, so nothing ever repeats. And while they’re watching it, we wake everyone.

c8_rig.source.lead.01.speaker: wen
c8_rig.source.lead.01.text: Three feeds, three jacks. Shaw, give me a cue.

c8_rig.source.lead.02.speaker: wen
c8_rig.source.lead.02.text: One jack carries my lamp tester. It flashes on beat five, every time.

c8_rig.source.lead.03.speaker: shaw
c8_rig.source.lead.03.text: One carries my rehearsal film, looping on beat four. And one is my own hand on the button.

c8_rig.source.lead.04.speaker: wen
c8_rig.source.lead.04.text: Shaw cued beat four, then beat seven. Birch flashed on five both times. Ash flashed on four both times.

c8_rig.source.lead.05.speaker: wen
c8_rig.source.lead.05.text: Elm flashed on four, then on seven. It followed her.

c8_rig.source.01.speaker: steve
c8_rig.source.01.text: Their old test failed because it repeated. Ours won’t. Every answer will be live.

c8_rig.source.find.speaker: steve
c8_rig.source.find.text: Birch is Wen’s fixed tester, stuck on beat 5. Ash is Shaw’s rehearsal loop, stuck on 4. Elm follows Shaw’s hand, live. Only Elm can answer a cue nobody has seen before.

c8_rig.path.lead.01.speaker: wen
c8_rig.path.lead.01.text: I ran a paper trial. Three receipts. Only one of them would convince me, if I were them.

c8_rig.path.lead.02.speaker: wen
c8_rig.path.lead.02.text: The dock receipt says a camera saw the lamps. The mast receipt says the ship measured them. The shore receipt says the ship got our crew’s numbers.

c8_rig.path.lead.03.speaker: wen
c8_rig.path.lead.03.text: The fleet trusts nothing that its own ship did not measure.

c8_rig.path.lead.04.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.path.lead.04.text: My crew pass still opens the antenna passage. I checked. Twice.

c8_rig.path.lead.05.speaker: steve
c8_rig.path.lead.05.text: And the sleepers are in the Gallery. Mom and Dad are in row nine.

c8_rig.path.01.speaker: wen
c8_rig.path.01.text: The ship must measure the event.

c8_rig.path.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.path.02.text: Then we take the rig to its antenna.

c8_rig.path.03.speaker: rook_copy
c8_rig.path.03.text: Prefect, they’re at the Sentinel Point workshop. All of them. They’re building something.
c8_rig.path.03.direction: on Frank’s radio, a channel he thinks is private

c8_rig.path.find.speaker: steve
c8_rig.path.find.text: The fleet only trusts what its own ship measures, so the show has to go in through the ship’s antenna. Stephen’s pass opens the antenna passage. The rest of us go to the Gallery and wake everyone.

c8_rig.rig.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.rig.lead.01.text: Three couplers, identical plugs. I’d like the one that works.

c8_rig.rig.lead.02.speaker: wen
c8_rig.rig.lead.02.text: I tested all three twice. Once to see the cue go out, and once to hear what leaks back.

c8_rig.rig.lead.03.speaker: shaw
c8_rig.rig.lead.03.text: We need a signal going out and nothing coming back. Otherwise the ship hears my theater.

c8_rig.rig.lead.04.speaker: wen
c8_rig.rig.lead.04.text: Careful. A dead coupler also lets nothing back. It looks perfect until you check the cue.

c8_rig.rig.01.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.rig.01.text: I can carry this. You get them awake.

c8_rig.rig.02.speaker: ward
c8_rig.rig.02.text: Both delegations are at your disposal, Mr. Mercer.

c8_rig.rig.find.speaker: steve
c8_rig.rig.find.text: Coupler A leaks the stage hum, B passes nothing, and C passes Shaw’s cue with a clean return. Stephen carries C to the antenna.

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.01.text: Did you water the balcony flowers before we left?

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.02.text: This morning. The irises have two new buds. I counted them.

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.03.text: Nora always forgot to water them. They nearly died twice.

c8_rig.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris
c8_rig.talk.iris.1.04.text: Then I’ll keep them alive until she’s home. That’s something I can do.

c8_rig.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris
c8_rig.talk.iris.2.01.text: Carmen called. She asked if we’re coming on Sunday. I told her yes, both of us.

c8_rig.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.iris.2.02.text: Both of us meaning you and me? Or Nora and me?

c8_rig.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris
c8_rig.talk.iris.2.03.text: Nora and you. I’ll be happy just to help set the plates.

c8_rig.talk.iris.3.01.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.iris.3.01.text: What have you lost so far?

c8_rig.talk.iris.3.02.speaker: iris
c8_rig.talk.iris.3.02.text: Small things. The name of Nora’s first goldfish. The way to her old school.

c8_rig.talk.iris.3.03.speaker: iris
c8_rig.talk.iris.3.03.text: It doesn’t hurt. It’s like a radio station drifting slowly out of range.

c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.01.text: I’m writing a list on my hand. Steve, Mom, Dad, Biscuit.

c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.02.text: Biscuit made your list before the rest of the town?

c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Biscuit is very important. Ask Pell.

c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.01.text: When this is over, I’d like to do one show at the radio station. Just one.

c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.02.text: The machine has my old chair now.

c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.talk.stephen.2.03.text: Then we take it back together. You do the sound. I’ll do the talking.

c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw
c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.01.text: I’ve used eleven rolls of gaffer tape today. That’s a personal record.

c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.02.text: Is that good news or bad news?

c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw
c8_rig.talk.shaw.1.03.text: In my business, it means the show is nearly ready.

c8_rig.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: wen
c8_rig.talk.wen.1.01.text: I called my daughter last night. She asked what I’m building this time.

c8_rig.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen
c8_rig.talk.wen.1.03.text: A very honest lie. She said that sounded exactly like me.

c8_rig.talk.ward.1.02.speaker: ward
c8_rig.talk.ward.1.02.text: Bandaged and famous. Half the country has seen it on television.

c8_rig.talk.ward.1.03.speaker: ward
c8_rig.talk.ward.1.03.text: My doctor wants to look at it. I said, not you, thank you.

c8_rig.talk.ward.2.01.speaker: ward
c8_rig.talk.ward.2.01.text: A week ago I had never heard of Bellwether. Now I won’t forget it.

c8_rig.talk.ward.2.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.talk.ward.2.02.text: Try Sunday dinner at La Marea before you leave. Carmen will feed you twice.

c8_rig.talk.ward.2.03.speaker: ward
c8_rig.talk.ward.2.03.text: If we’re all still here on Sunday, I’ll book a table.

c8_rig.recap.01.speaker: steve
c8_rig.recap.01.text: The plan: Shaw and Wen stage the Meridian test again, live, on Elm through coupler C. Stephen carries the rig into the ship’s antenna, so the ship measures the show for itself.

c8_rig.recap.02.speaker: steve
c8_rig.recap.02.text: The rest of us go to the Gallery and wake everyone, Mom and Dad included. Iris and Stephen voted for it, knowing what it costs them.

c8_rig.out.01.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.out.01.text: Dad’s name. I know it. I just...

c8_rig.out.03.speaker: stephen
c8_rig.out.03.text: Frank. I’ll write it on my hand.

c8_rig.out.04.speaker: steve
c8_rig.out.04.text: That night we went back under the bay, through the aquarium tunnel. Pell stayed behind with Biscuit. Ten minutes later he caught up with us, carrying her.

c9_gallery.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.ctx.01.text: The third ninth night. We came in through the intake tunnel, soaked to the knees.

c9_gallery.in.04.speaker: guard
c9_gallery.in.04.text: Unscheduled visitors detected. Would you like to be scanned while you wait?

c9_gallery.in.05.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.in.05.text: We’ve done this one. It ends with a flood.

c9_gallery.in.06.speaker: stephen
c9_gallery.in.06.text: I’ll take your word for it. I wasn’t conscious for the good part.

c9_gallery.in.01.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.in.01.text: Steve? They put me back under after the pump trick. Five months. And thirteen months before that, when you barely said a word.

c9_gallery.in.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.in.02.text: I’m so glad to hear you angry.

c9_gallery.in.03.speaker: iris
c9_gallery.in.03.text: I can break the link. Let me do this.

c9_gallery.link.01.speaker: iris
c9_gallery.link.01.text: These memories were borrowed. The choice is mine.

c9_gallery.link.02.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.link.02.text: I can move. I can finally move.

c9_gallery.link.find.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.link.find.text: Iris opened the release herself, watching her own memory drain. Nora can move.

c9_gallery.talk.01.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.01.text: I was afraid that if I wanted something, I would lose it too. That doesn’t excuse leaving you alone.

c9_gallery.talk.02.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.02.text: Then keep talking. We have a lot to do.

c9_gallery.talk.03.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.03.text: I laughed. I couldn’t help it. Then she laughed too.

c9_gallery.talk.find.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.find.text: I told Nora the truth about the thirteen months: I was afraid that if I wanted something, I’d lose it too. She told me to keep talking.

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.01.speaker: stephen
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.01.text: One door, one pass, one very important face. Let’s go.

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.02.speaker: calder
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.02.text: This visitor slip gets me onto the observation deck. It won’t open a single door.

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.03.speaker: stephen
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.03.text: The lamp for the inner door is round the bend. You can only see it from the deck.

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.04.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.04.text: And I stay right here by Nora’s bed. I promised her.

c9_gallery.antenna.lead.05.speaker: stephen
c9_gallery.antenna.lead.05.text: Then I don’t walk on until somebody sees that lamp light up.

c9_gallery.antenna.01.speaker: stephen
c9_gallery.antenna.01.text: Calder saw the lamp. I’m heading up to the antenna. Don’t wait for me.

c9_gallery.antenna.find.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.antenna.find.text: Stephen’s pass opened the inner pad. June saw the lamp light from the deck and called it in, and Stephen went on alone to the antenna with the rig. I stayed where I promised.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.01.text: Did my mother notice? That it wasn’t me at her table?

c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.02.text: She said you’d stopped arguing with her. That’s how she knew something was wrong.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.nora.1.03.text: Good. I’m going to argue with her all week.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.01.text: Is anybody feeding Admiral properly? He gets sulky.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.02.text: He stole my sandwich on the pier. Rye bread.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.03.text: He hates rye. He was making a point.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.04.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.nora.2.04.text: He came to my whistle, Nor. Not hers. That’s when I started to wonder.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.01.text: I know half this hall by name now. It’s like a very cold party.

c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.02.text: Who is the best company down here?

c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.nora.3.03.text: Dale Kittredge. He says he’s never been this late with the mail in thirty years.

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.01.text: You wore my favorite coat for five months.

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: iris
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.02.text: It is a good coat. I sewed the top button back on.

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.03.text: I’ve been meaning to do that for two years.

c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.04.speaker: iris
c9_gallery.talk.iris.1.04.text: I know. I remembered meaning to.

c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris
c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.01.text: I keep reaching for things she knows. Some of them are already gone.

c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.02.text: Do you want me to stop asking you things?

c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris
c9_gallery.talk.iris.2.03.text: No. Keep asking. I want to find out which answers are mine.

c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: stephen
c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.02.text: Frank. Dad. I check it every few minutes. I hate that I have to.

c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Then I’ll check it with you. Every few minutes.

c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder
c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.01.text: I took this slip from a sleeping man in a very nice suit.

c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.02.text: Is that strictly legal, Sheriff Calder?

c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c9_gallery.talk.calder.1.03.text: I’ll write myself a ticket when we get home.

c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.01.speaker: calder
c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.01.text: Adrian Rook is somewhere in this hall. The real one.

c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.02.text: We’ll find him, June. I promise.

c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.03.speaker: calder
c9_gallery.talk.calder.2.03.text: Good. He still owes me a coffee from twenty years ago.

c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.01.speaker: guard
c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.01.text: Would you like to be scanned while you wait?

c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.02.text: Still no, thank you. Very kind of you to ask again.

c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.03.speaker: guard
c9_gallery.talk.guard.1.03.text: Your answer has been noted. The offer remains open.

c9_gallery.recap.01.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.recap.01.text: Nora is free. Iris paid for it with her own memory, and chose to.

c9_gallery.recap.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.recap.02.text: Stephen is on his way to the antenna with the rig. Mom and Dad are somewhere in this hall, in row nine.

c9_gallery.out.06.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.out.06.text: I left you something. Slot B. Press play.

c9_gallery.out.03.speaker: nora
c9_gallery.out.03.text: Steve, if you ever hear this message: I am furious with you. I love you. Please stop making me do both alone.
c9_gallery.out.03.direction: from every speaker in the Gallery at once

c9_gallery.out.07.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.out.07.text: Nora and Iris looked at each other. Neither of them knew what to say.

c9_wake.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c9_wake.ctx.01.text: Row nine. Mom and Dad, side by side, the way they always slept. I’d brought every sound I had.

c9_wake.in.01.speaker: nora
c9_wake.in.01.text: We’ve kept the service route open. Tell me who to wake first.

c9_wake.in.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.in.02.text: I brought the sounds. I think they can hear us.

c9_wake.frank.lead.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.frank.lead.02.text: Nothing. He used to say a call sign is a name you can hear through static.

c9_wake.frank.lead.03.speaker: nora
c9_wake.frank.lead.03.text: There are three call cards in his tray. They all look almost the same.

c9_wake.frank.lead.04.speaker: steve
c9_wake.frank.lead.04.text: Dad’s call sign is on his old cassette, in Morse. But the tape is scratched. It always loses the very last letter.

c9_wake.frank.find.speaker: steve
c9_wake.frank.find.text: Dad’s card is K7BLW. The scratched cassette lost the last letter, the W: dot, dash, dash. I sent it again, and Dad answered his own call sign.

c9_wake.helen.lead.01.speaker: frank
c9_wake.helen.lead.01.text: Your mother. Play her the song, kiddo. I’ll write it down for you.

c9_wake.helen.lead.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.helen.lead.02.text: That’s the song in the hum. All this time, the ship was humming Mom’s lullaby.

c9_wake.helen.lead.03.speaker: frank
c9_wake.helen.lead.03.text: It starts at home. Up once, then up again. Back down to the middle note, then home, and hold it.

c9_wake.helen.01.speaker: steve
c9_wake.helen.01.text: You used to sing this when I couldn’t sleep. Now I need you to wake up.

c9_wake.helen.find.speaker: steve
c9_wake.helen.find.text: Home, up, higher, back to the middle, then home and hold. Mom’s lullaby, the one the ship’s hum kept almost playing. She woke up singing the last note.

c9_wake.rook.01.speaker: calder
c9_wake.rook.01.text: Adrian. It’s June. Come back to work.

c9_wake.rook.02.speaker: rook
c9_wake.rook.02.text: June? Why am I in pajamas?

c9_wake.rook.find.speaker: steve
c9_wake.rook.find.text: No recording this time. June talked to him, and the real Adrian Rook woke up asking about his pajamas.

c9_wake.agnes.lead.01.speaker: nora
c9_wake.agnes.lead.01.text: Mrs. Penhallow? She taught half this town. She’s squinting at me like I spelled something wrong.

c9_wake.agnes.lead.02.speaker: nora
c9_wake.agnes.lead.02.text: Her glasses case still has a price sticker from her bait shop. That one is hers.

c9_wake.agnes.lead.03.speaker: nora
c9_wake.agnes.lead.03.text: The row list says the sleeper marked OT is on her left, and MV is on her right.

c9_wake.agnes.01.speaker: agnes_original
c9_wake.agnes.01.text: My glasses. Has somebody changed the price of bait while I was gone?

c9_wake.agnes.02.speaker: agnes_original
c9_wake.agnes.02.text: Who has been minding my bait stall, Steven?

c9_wake.agnes.03.speaker: steve
c9_wake.agnes.03.text: I thought you had, Mrs. Penhallow. Every Sunday on the pier.

c9_wake.agnes.04.speaker: agnes_original
c9_wake.agnes.04.text: On Sundays? I never open on Sundays. Sunday is for church and the crossword.

c9_wake.agnes.find.speaker: steve
c9_wake.agnes.find.text: Mrs. Penhallow’s glasses, from the middle tray. Her bed tag says she’s been asleep in here for three years. So who has been selling me bait?

c9_wake.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora
c9_wake.talk.nora.1.01.text: We kept this aisle open with a mop handle and a lot of shouting.

c9_wake.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.nora.1.02.text: All that shouting? I can believe that.

c9_wake.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora
c9_wake.talk.nora.1.03.text: Mostly mine. Dale helped. He shouts like a man who has met a lot of dogs.

c9_wake.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora
c9_wake.talk.nora.2.01.text: Your mother just asked me if I’m eating enough. On a spaceship.

c9_wake.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.nora.2.02.text: That’s how she says I love you.

c9_wake.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora
c9_wake.talk.nora.2.03.text: I know. My mother does the exact same thing with soup.

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.01.speaker: frank
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.01.text: How long were we under, kiddo?

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.02.text: Eighteen months, Dad. A year and a half.

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.03.speaker: frank
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.03.text: That’s a lot of Thursdays. The club must think I quit.

c9_wake.talk.frank.1.04.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.frank.1.04.text: They don’t. I called them on your radio. Gull nearly cried.

c9_wake.talk.frank.2.01.speaker: frank
c9_wake.talk.frank.2.01.text: Did the boat make it back?

c9_wake.talk.frank.2.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.frank.2.02.text: It drifted in the next morning. Your radio was still on.

c9_wake.talk.frank.2.03.speaker: frank
c9_wake.talk.frank.2.03.text: Good radio. I told your mother it was a good radio.

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.01.text: You never told me the words, Mom.

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: helen
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.02.text: There weren’t any, Steven. I made up the tune your first night home from the hospital.

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.03.text: The ship has been humming it for months.

c9_wake.talk.helen.1.04.speaker: helen
c9_wake.talk.helen.1.04.text: Then the ship has good taste.

c9_wake.talk.helen.2.01.speaker: helen
c9_wake.talk.helen.2.01.text: Is that Nora? She looks so tired.

c9_wake.talk.helen.2.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.helen.2.02.text: She ran this whole hall while you were asleep, Mom.

c9_wake.talk.helen.2.03.speaker: helen
c9_wake.talk.helen.2.03.text: Then she has earned a proper dinner. I’ll talk to Carmen.

c9_wake.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder
c9_wake.talk.calder.1.01.text: He asked about his pajamas before he asked about me.

c9_wake.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.talk.calder.1.02.text: He’s awake, June. That’s what matters.

c9_wake.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c9_wake.talk.calder.1.03.text: I know. I’m still telling everyone at the office.

c9_wake.talk.rook.1.01.speaker: rook
c9_wake.talk.rook.1.01.text: Where are my clothes? Who has been wearing my clothes?

c9_wake.talk.rook.1.02.speaker: calder
c9_wake.talk.rook.1.02.text: A man with your face, Adrian. He had your manners too, mostly.

c9_wake.talk.rook.1.03.speaker: rook
c9_wake.talk.rook.1.03.text: Then he owes me a dry cleaning bill.

c9_wake.recap.01.speaker: steve
c9_wake.recap.01.text: Dad woke to his call sign, Mom to her lullaby, Adrian Rook to June’s voice, and Mrs. Penhallow to her reading glasses.

c9_wake.recap.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.recap.02.text: Somewhere above us, Rook’s copy was losing the man he’d been pretending to be. And he was telling Saren everything he had left.

c9_wake.out.01.speaker: rook_copy
c9_wake.out.01.text: I’m forgetting. Prefect, they’re at the antenna. They have a rig.

c9_wake.out.02.speaker: saren
c9_wake.out.02.text: Take Stephen. Break the apparatus. Bring me the original.

c9_choir.in.04.speaker: steve
c9_choir.in.04.text: They took the rig off Stephen and broke it over the rail. Then they took me.

c9_choir.in.01.speaker: saren
c9_choir.in.01.text: We will finish your scan. This time there will be no interruption.

c9_choir.in.05.speaker: steve
c9_choir.in.05.text: The chair pulled at everything I knew. My dad’s name. It was... it’s on Stephen’s hand. Why is it on his hand?
c9_choir.in.05.direction: strapped into the scan chair, frightened

c9_choir.in.03.speaker: choir
c9_choir.in.03.text: Four thousand years of unchanged records. Three hundred and twelve human lives. Show us one record that changed, and we will choose.

c9_choir.truth.lead.01.speaker: steve
c9_choir.truth.lead.01.text: You want a record that changed? I’ve been keeping a list.

c9_choir.truth.lead.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.truth.lead.02.text: Nora’s good morning, on Saturday and on Sunday. The same breath, the same pause, both days.

c9_choir.truth.lead.03.speaker: steve
c9_choir.truth.lead.03.text: Rook telling June to sit tight. The same take on her voicemail and through a door in the mountains.

c9_choir.truth.lead.04.speaker: steve
c9_choir.truth.lead.04.text: And Iris, on Monday. She said the same words twice, and the second time she paused somewhere new.

c9_choir.truth.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.truth.02.text: Same voice. In October she played back a recording. On Monday she chose her own words.

c9_choir.truth.01.speaker: choir
c9_choir.truth.01.text: We remember birthdays, quarrels, songs and the things people tried again. Open the doors. Wake them.

c9_choir.truth.find.speaker: steve
c9_choir.truth.find.text: Nora’s good morning and Rook’s line were recordings, played back. Iris chose her words twice, differently. The same voice that once replayed Nora now speaks for itself. The Choir heard a record change, and chose.

c9_choir.wick.lead.01.speaker: steve
c9_choir.wick.lead.01.text: The frost broke. Something tall sat up in Row Zero for the first time in three hundred years. It looked at Mom, and it bowed.

c9_choir.wick.lead.02.speaker: choir
c9_choir.wick.lead.02.text: Row Zero holds one who is not human. We took it from Tirel. We call it Wick. It has not stopped dreaming.

c9_choir.wick.lead.03.speaker: nora
c9_choir.wick.lead.03.text: That’s the one under the frost. It hums when you talk to it.

c9_choir.wick.lead.04.speaker: helen
c9_choir.wick.lead.04.text: That’s the phrase from your father’s tapes. Two joined notes going up, a little gap, then one long low note.

c9_choir.wick.lead.05.speaker: helen
c9_choir.wick.lead.05.text: I wrote it in my margin, Steven. After the low note, it starts all over again.

c9_choir.wick.01.speaker: helen
c9_choir.wick.01.text: I heard you in the hum. The Choir was dreaming with you.

c9_choir.wick.02.speaker: helen
c9_choir.wick.02.text: Tirel hid. All seven worlds hid. They watched you erase yourselves and were afraid you would erase them.

c9_choir.wick.find.speaker: steve
c9_choir.wick.find.text: Page 12: two joined strokes rising, a gap, one long low stroke, and then it starts again. Mom followed Wick from phrase to phrase. Tirel was never destroyed. It hid. They all hid.

c9_choir.note.01.speaker: frank
c9_choir.note.01.text: We wanted your ears, kiddo. We always liked having the rest of you along too.

c9_choir.note.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.note.02.text: I thought saying no was the worst thing I’d ever done.

c9_choir.note.find.speaker: steve
c9_choir.note.find.text: Dad’s note from the boat: they wanted my ears, and they always liked having the rest of me along too. For eighteen months I thought saying no was the worst thing I’d ever done.

c9_choir.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora
c9_choir.talk.nora.1.01.text: Three hundred people just woke up in wet pajamas.

c9_choir.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.talk.nora.1.02.text: And not one of them has shoes.

c9_choir.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora
c9_choir.talk.nora.1.03.text: I’m starting a line for blankets. Somebody has to.

c9_choir.talk.frank.1.01.speaker: frank
c9_choir.talk.frank.1.01.text: You kept a list, kiddo. Dates and everything.

c9_choir.talk.frank.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.talk.frank.1.02.text: You taught me. Put a date on everything.

c9_choir.talk.frank.1.03.speaker: frank
c9_choir.talk.frank.1.03.text: I did, didn’t I? Good. I’m glad something stuck.

c9_choir.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: helen
c9_choir.talk.helen.1.01.text: It sings in phrases, like a person thinking out loud.

c9_choir.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.talk.helen.1.02.text: Can you understand what it says?

c9_choir.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: helen
c9_choir.talk.helen.1.03.text: Not every word. But I can hear when it means something.

c9_choir.talk.calder.1.01.speaker: calder
c9_choir.talk.calder.1.01.text: Every door on this ship just opened at once.

c9_choir.talk.calder.1.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.talk.calder.1.02.text: Is everybody all right down there?

c9_choir.talk.calder.1.03.speaker: calder
c9_choir.talk.calder.1.03.text: Dale Kittredge is asking for his mailbag. So yes, I think so.

c9_choir.recap.01.speaker: steve
c9_choir.recap.01.text: The Choir chose. Every door on the ship opened, and three hundred people woke up at once in wet pajamas. The crew had no procedure for it.

c9_choir.recap.02.speaker: steve
c9_choir.recap.02.text: Tirel hid. All seven worlds hid. The Veyri have spent nine hundred years afraid of neighbors who were afraid of them.

c9_choir.out.01.speaker: frank
c9_choir.out.01.text: You’d have been the third person in the Gallery, kiddo. Then who would have come for us?

c9_choir.out.02.speaker: helen
c9_choir.out.02.text: I should have told you what we were doing.

c9_choir.out.03.speaker: steve
c9_choir.out.03.text: We’re here now. All of us.

c9_choir.out.04.speaker: calder
c9_choir.out.04.text: Something enormous just came out of the sky. We have one hour.

c9_choir.out.05.speaker: choir
c9_choir.out.05.text: The Vigil. It followed us here in silence, to check the Prefect’s word. His report goes out in one hour.

c9_choir.out.06.speaker: steve
c9_choir.out.06.text: The rig was in pieces. And all over town, the copies had begun to forget.

c10_station.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c10_station.ctx.01.text: One hour. The rig was in pieces, and all over town the copies were forgetting.

c10_station.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.ctx.02.text: Then I remembered Halcyon’s tower. Every ninth night for a year it had talked to the ship, alone.

c10_station.in.04.speaker: stephen
c10_station.in.04.text: The rig is in pieces. We need another way onto their antenna.

c10_station.in.05.speaker: steve
c10_station.in.05.text: We don’t need the rig. KBWR’s tower already talks to the ship.

c10_station.in.01.speaker: autorick
c10_station.in.01.text: Good morning! Up next, another hour of uninterrupted favorites.

c10_station.in.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.in.02.text: Rick, buddy. I need my microphone back.

c10_station.in.03.speaker: autorick
c10_station.in.03.text: Your request is important to us!

c10_station.playlist.lead.01.speaker: steve
c10_station.playlist.lead.01.text: Rick keeps a log of everything. Including the last time a human got the microphone.

c10_station.playlist.lead.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.playlist.lead.02.text: Three slips. My station ident, a traffic report and a news bulletin.

c10_station.playlist.lead.03.speaker: steve
c10_station.playlist.lead.03.text: The ident never stops the music. Traffic waits until the song ends. A bulletin puts a person on the air.

c10_station.playlist.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.playlist.02.text: Thank you, Rick. We’re live now.

c10_station.playlist.find.speaker: steve
c10_station.playlist.find.text: 06:01 was the ident, 06:03 the traffic and 06:05 the bulletin, the one that hands the air to a human. I signed the bulletin as duty host, and KBWR was mine again.

c10_station.route.lead.01.speaker: wen
c10_station.route.lead.01.text: Same labels as the rig. You remember which is which, I hope.

c10_station.route.lead.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.route.lead.02.text: Birch was your fixed tester. Ash was the old rehearsal loop. Elm followed Shaw’s hand.

c10_station.route.lead.03.speaker: wen
c10_station.route.lead.03.text: Returns: A is the booth echo, B is a shore camera, and C is measured aboard their ship.

c10_station.route.01.speaker: steve
c10_station.route.01.text: The route was here the whole time. It’s why they bought the station.

c10_station.route.find.speaker: steve
c10_station.route.find.text: Elm follows Shaw’s hand, live, the way it did at the rig. Return C is a measurement signed aboard the Long Patience, the only kind the fleet trusts. Elm into Return C.

c10_station.out.01.speaker: frank
c10_station.out.01.text: K7BLW calling the Thursday club. We’re going to need a few more operators.

c10_station.relay.lead.01.speaker: frank
c10_station.relay.lead.01.text: Yesterday I sent signal three. Today I’m sending signal four. Let’s see who keeps up.

c10_station.relay.lead.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.relay.lead.02.text: The official channel just sent back three. That’s yesterday’s cue.

c10_station.relay.lead.03.speaker: operator
c10_station.relay.lead.03.text: Gull here. Cedar and Marsh both say four. Marsh says the wind just turned west out at the Point.

c10_station.relay.lead.04.speaker: frank
c10_station.relay.lead.04.text: Ask them both about the wind again, Gull.

c10_station.relay.lead.05.speaker: operator
c10_station.relay.lead.05.text: Marsh says it’s dropping now. Cedar said the same words as last time, exactly.

c10_station.relay.01.speaker: frank
c10_station.relay.01.text: Short messages. Repeat the cue number, then pass it on.

c10_station.relay.02.speaker: operator
c10_station.relay.02.text: Understood. Sentinel Point, do you read?

c10_station.relay.find.speaker: steve
c10_station.relay.find.text: The official line sent back yesterday’s cue. Cedar can repeat a cue but can’t see the field. Marsh, out past Sentinel Point, answered with a fresh wind reading. Marsh is our eyes, and Gull carries the cues down the coast.

c10_station.talk.frank.1.01.speaker: frank
c10_station.talk.frank.1.01.text: Has anybody got dry socks? I’ll trade a perfectly good vacuum tube.

c10_station.talk.frank.1.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.talk.frank.1.02.text: There’s a lost and found behind the coffee machine.

c10_station.talk.frank.1.03.speaker: frank
c10_station.talk.frank.1.03.text: Then I’m saving the world in somebody’s bowling socks.

c10_station.talk.frank.2.01.speaker: frank
c10_station.talk.frank.2.01.text: I wired half this booth, you know. Labeled every cable.

c10_station.talk.frank.2.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.talk.frank.2.02.text: Somebody took the labels off when the new owners came.

c10_station.talk.frank.2.03.speaker: frank
c10_station.talk.frank.2.03.text: Then I’ll put them back. Every single one. After breakfast.

c10_station.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: stephen
c10_station.talk.stephen.1.01.text: Is there coffee? I remember liking coffee.

c10_station.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.talk.stephen.1.02.text: You do. Black and very strong, two cups before breakfast.

c10_station.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: stephen
c10_station.talk.stephen.1.03.text: Good. That one is still mine. I’m keeping it.

c10_station.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen
c10_station.talk.stephen.2.01.text: Do we both talk on air, or do we take turns?

c10_station.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.talk.stephen.2.02.text: Take turns. People will think the radio is broken.

c10_station.talk.stephen.2.03.speaker: stephen
c10_station.talk.stephen.2.03.text: People already think that. I listened to your replacement for a week.

c10_station.talk.autorick.1.01.speaker: steve
c10_station.talk.autorick.1.01.text: Good morning, Rick. How are you feeling today?

c10_station.talk.autorick.1.02.speaker: autorick
c10_station.talk.autorick.1.02.text: I am excellent! It is currently yesterday!

c10_station.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: wen
c10_station.talk.wen.1.01.text: When I was a girl, our village had one loudspeaker on a pole.

c10_station.talk.wen.1.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.talk.wen.1.02.text: What did the loudspeaker play all day?

c10_station.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen
c10_station.talk.wen.1.03.text: Weather, news and my aunt’s opinions. Mostly my aunt’s opinions.

c10_station.recap.01.speaker: steve
c10_station.recap.01.text: KBWR is live again, and the tower that carried the ship’s signals for a year will carry ours: Elm into Return C.

c10_station.recap.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.recap.02.text: Dad’s club is relaying the cues. Marsh at Sentinel Point, Gull down the coast, and then anyone on Earth with a radio.

c10_station.out.02.speaker: operator
c10_station.out.02.text: Coast relay ready. They’re answering from everywhere, Frank.

c10_station.out.04.speaker: frank
c10_station.out.04.text: Every continent, kiddo. Hams never really switch off.

c10_town.in.01.speaker: nora
c10_town.in.01.text: Carmen calls the restaurant list. Mateo calls the fire crews. Rafa calls everyone who owes him a favor.

c10_town.in.03.speaker: ward
c10_town.in.03.text: Listen to your local radio. Tonight, we need you to take part.

c10_town.in.04.speaker: steve
c10_town.in.04.text: Mrs. Penhallow walked into the booth with her bait bucket. Nobody had told her where we were.

c10_town.out.01.speaker: agnes
c10_town.out.01.text: I brought something in my bucket.

c10_town.in.05.speaker: agnes
c10_town.in.05.text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Original take.

c10_town.in.06.speaker: steve
c10_town.in.06.text: Mrs. Penhallow, I have never heard you say anything that wasn’t about bait.

c10_town.out.03.speaker: agnes
c10_town.out.03.text: I recorded it a long time ago, Steven. Before I had hands that smelled of herring.

c10_town.in.07.speaker: steve
c10_town.in.07.text: You’re one of them. You’re the records officer Iris told me about.

c10_town.in.08.speaker: agnes
c10_town.in.08.text: Part of her. The part that stayed for the people.

c10_town.in.09.speaker: agnes
c10_town.in.09.text: Veyr was our home, Steven. Our sun failed. That is the last wind that ever blew through our city.

c10_town.lights.lead.01.speaker: nora
c10_town.lights.lead.01.text: Two street captains, one spare phone and six thousand porch lights. Easy.

c10_town.lights.lead.02.speaker: nora
c10_town.lights.lead.02.text: Pier can see Orchard’s porch lights from the harbor. Orchard faces the hills, so they can’t see Pier at all.

c10_town.lights.lead.03.speaker: nora
c10_town.lights.lead.03.text: Both streets have the radio on. And Mateo wants one phone kept free for the fire crew.

c10_town.lights.01.speaker: nora
c10_town.lights.01.text: Listen, repeat the cue, then switch. And leave a line free for anyone who needs help.

c10_town.lights.find.speaker: steve
c10_town.lights.find.text: Nora set it up in ten minutes. Orchard starts on my cue, Pier answers what it sees, and the spare phone stays free for the fire crew.

c10_town.console.03.speaker: steve
c10_town.console.03.text: Wonderful. You can both fix it while we’re on air.

c10_town.console.find.speaker: steve
c10_town.console.find.text: Shaw calls the lamps when she sees the harbor answer, and Wen raises the grid on Shaw’s mark. Nine years of rivalry, one cue sheet.

c10_town.wind.lead.01.speaker: agnes
c10_town.wind.lead.01.text: There is a pencil mark after the last gust. I made it myself.

c10_town.wind.lead.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.wind.lead.02.text: The fleet should hear home first. Then a voice answering them, live, that nobody recorded.

c10_town.wind.01.speaker: steve
c10_town.wind.01.text: A recording can remind them of home. We’ll answer it with something happening now.

c10_town.wind.find.speaker: steve
c10_town.wind.find.text: The Veyr wind plays through to Mrs. Penhallow’s pencil mark, after the last gust. Then the Choir’s return opens, live. Home as it was, then a voice answering them now.

c10_town.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora
c10_town.talk.nora.1.01.text: My mother has called forty people already. Thirty of them owe her money.

c10_town.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.talk.nora.1.02.text: Wait. People actually owe Carmen money?

c10_town.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora
c10_town.talk.nora.1.03.text: Tabs at the restaurant. She’s calling in every single one tonight.

c10_town.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora
c10_town.talk.nora.2.01.text: Yesterday I was asleep under the bay. Today I’m running a town.

c10_town.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.talk.nora.2.02.text: You were always running the town, Nor.

c10_town.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora
c10_town.talk.nora.2.03.text: True. But now people are actually listening to me.

c10_town.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora
c10_town.talk.nora.3.01.text: Iris called my brothers before I could. She knew every number by heart.

c10_town.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.talk.nora.3.02.text: She’s had your phone for five months.

c10_town.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora
c10_town.talk.nora.3.03.text: I want that phone back. And she rearranged all my apps.

c10_town.talk.carmen.1.01.speaker: carmen
c10_town.talk.carmen.1.01.text: I have called the bakery, the church and both bars. The bars were awake.

c10_town.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.talk.carmen.1.02.text: Thank you, Carmen. I mean it.

c10_town.talk.carmen.1.03.speaker: carmen
c10_town.talk.carmen.1.03.text: Thank me by eating something. You haven’t eaten since Thursday. I can tell.

c10_town.talk.carmen.2.01.speaker: carmen
c10_town.talk.carmen.2.01.text: She argued with me twice tonight already. Twice, Steve!

c10_town.talk.carmen.2.03.speaker: carmen
c10_town.talk.carmen.2.03.text: It is the best night of my whole life.

c10_town.talk.agnes.1.01.speaker: agnes
c10_town.talk.agnes.1.01.text: You were a good student, Steven. Too loud. I liked that.

c10_town.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.talk.agnes.1.02.text: You weren’t really my teacher, were you?

c10_town.talk.agnes.1.03.speaker: agnes
c10_town.talk.agnes.1.03.text: She was. I learned her very carefully. I only kept her chair warm.

c10_town.talk.agnes.2.01.speaker: steve
c10_town.talk.agnes.2.01.text: Why a bait stall, of all things?

c10_town.talk.agnes.2.02.speaker: agnes
c10_town.talk.agnes.2.02.text: Nobody buys bait, so nobody stays long. And I could watch the water all day.

c10_town.talk.ward.1.01.speaker: ward
c10_town.talk.ward.1.01.text: My staff wanted a long speech. I told them to listen to local radio.

c10_town.talk.ward.1.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.talk.ward.1.02.text: How is your wrist, Madam President?

c10_town.talk.ward.1.03.speaker: ward
c10_town.talk.ward.1.03.text: Bandaged, and still mine. Thank you for that.

c10_town.talk.wen.1.01.speaker: wen
c10_town.talk.wen.1.01.text: Nine years ago I would have unplugged her lamps.

c10_town.talk.wen.1.02.speaker: shaw
c10_town.talk.wen.1.02.text: You tried. And my fake fooled more generals than yours.

c10_town.talk.wen.1.03.speaker: wen
c10_town.talk.wen.1.03.text: It did not. My test fooled two admirals as well.

c10_town.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw
c10_town.talk.shaw.1.01.text: I brought the fog machine. Just in case.

c10_town.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw
c10_town.talk.shaw.1.03.text: In case it needs to look impressive. It always needs to look impressive.

c10_town.recap.01.speaker: steve
c10_town.recap.01.text: Mrs. Penhallow is part of the ship’s record keeper, the part that stayed ashore with us. She brought me the last wind on Veyr in her bait bucket.

c10_town.recap.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.recap.02.text: Every porch light in Bellwether is waiting for my cue. Shaw has the lamps, Wen has the grid, and the Choir will answer live.

c10_live.in.01.speaker: steve
c10_live.in.01.text: Bellwether, this is Steve Mercer, live. I can’t do this alone, and for once I’m not going to try.

c10_live.in.04.speaker: steve
c10_live.in.04.text: I knocked over the microphone stand, caught it and kept going.

c10_live.in.02.speaker: stephen
c10_live.in.02.text: Steve. Who’s... Frank. Dad. It’s on my hand.

c10_live.in.03.speaker: steve
c10_live.in.03.text: It’s on mine too. Stay with me.

c10_live.first.lead.01.speaker: nora
c10_live.first.lead.01.text: Orchard is listening for you, Steve. The pier is watching Orchard.

c10_live.first.lead.02.speaker: nora
c10_live.first.lead.02.text: Careful. Two Pier lamps are still on from the rehearsal. Don’t count those.

c10_live.first.01.speaker: nora
c10_live.first.01.text: First street ready. Second street ready. Look at the harbor, Steve.

c10_live.first.02.speaker: shaw
c10_live.first.02.text: Field lights following. We can match that.

c10_live.first.find.speaker: steve
c10_live.first.find.text: I called Orchard. When a fresh Pier flash answered Orchard’s change, I released Shaw’s lights. A reply, made live, that nobody could have recorded.

c10_live.second.lead.01.speaker: frank
c10_live.second.lead.01.text: I logged all three faders, kiddo. One of them only looks connected.

c10_live.second.lead.02.speaker: frank
c10_live.second.lead.02.text: With the coast plugged in, Reed and Bell both answered two beats late. With the coast unplugged, Reed went quiet.

c10_live.second.lead.03.speaker: frank
c10_live.second.lead.03.text: Bell kept answering anyway. So Bell is only an echo inside the building.

c10_live.second.lead.04.speaker: steve
c10_live.second.lead.04.text: The fourth signal goes out on beat forty. Shaw goes when the coast answers. Wen needs the next two beats.

c10_live.second.lead.05.speaker: wen
c10_live.second.lead.05.text: And my power crew needs everything back by the start of beat forty-five.

c10_live.second.find.speaker: steve
c10_live.second.find.text: Reed went silent when the coast was unplugged, so Reed is the real coast return. Its reply landed at 42 for Shaw, and Wen took 43 and 44. Both grids answered, live.

c10_live.third.lead.01.speaker: steve
c10_live.third.lead.01.text: Last cue. The wind on Veyr, and then the Choir. Nobody talks over them.

c10_live.third.lead.02.speaker: steve
c10_live.third.lead.02.text: Mrs. Penhallow marked the last gust at fifty. It keeps ringing until fifty-two.

c10_live.third.lead.03.speaker: wen
c10_live.third.lead.03.text: I confirm on beat fifty-one. Give me two beats to talk.

c10_live.third.01.speaker: choir
c10_live.third.01.text: We are here. We have changed. Listen.

c10_live.third.02.speaker: steve
c10_live.third.02.text: Keep the voices clear. Let them hear every one.

c10_live.third.03.speaker: steve
c10_live.third.03.text: For the first time in nine hundred years, the fleet stopped to listen.

c10_live.third.find.speaker: steve
c10_live.third.find.text: The wind on Veyr rang out through 52. At 53, with nobody else on the line, the Choir answered. Nothing repeated, because nothing was recorded.

c10_live.recap.01.speaker: steve
c10_live.recap.01.text: Porch lights, field lamps, two national grids, a planet’s worth of radios and three hundred and twelve human voices. None of it recorded. All of it answering.

c10_live.recap.02.speaker: steve
c10_live.recap.02.text: To the Vigil’s instruments, Earth had just tested an engine that could reach the fleet in an afternoon.

c10_live.out.01.speaker: mateo
c10_live.out.01.text: Saren is on the pier. He’s going for the tower.

c10_live.out.05.speaker: saren
c10_live.out.05.text: Mr. Mercer. Turn it off, or I will come up that tower and finish your scan on air.

c10_live.out.06.speaker: steve
c10_live.out.06.text: You’re on air now, Prefect. Your whole fleet is listening. Say that again.

c10_live.out.07.speaker: steve
c10_live.out.07.text: The town stood on the pier in his way. June. The Reyes brothers. Carmen with a ladle. Pell with Biscuit. Stephen. And two hundred copies who had decided where they lived.

c10_live.out.02.speaker: carmen
c10_live.out.02.text: Then he can go through us.

c10_live.out.03.speaker: pell
c10_live.out.03.text: Biscuit and I have chosen our route.

c10_live.out.08.speaker: carmen
c10_live.out.08.text: He’s sitting down. Mateo is sitting on him.

c10_live.out.04.speaker: stephen
c10_live.out.04.text: And Admiral has stolen his command crystal. He thinks it’s a sandwich.

c10_live.out.10.speaker: saren
c10_live.out.10.text: Take me back to the ship. I will not sign anything.

c10_report.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c10_report.ctx.01.text: Mrs. Penhallow took the microphone out of my hand. Then she argued with herself, on the air, while the whole planet listened.

c10_report.in.01.speaker: saren
c10_report.in.01.text: I will not confirm this report.

c10_report.in.02.speaker: archivist
c10_report.in.02.text: To do so would violate every record we have kept.

c10_report.in.04.speaker: archivist
c10_report.in.04.text: For a year I told you the engine was in a notebook, Saren. So you would keep looking, instead of telling the fleet there was nothing here to fear.

c10_report.in.03.speaker: agnes
c10_report.in.03.text: You have spent three years selling bait to people you like. Tell them what you learned.

c10_report.echo.lead.01.speaker: agnes
c10_report.echo.lead.01.text: Last winter the boats came in empty. I let every one of them pay me in spring.

c10_report.echo.01.speaker: agnes
c10_report.echo.01.text: You can spend another nine hundred years remembering home, or let someone make a new one.

c10_report.echo.02.speaker: archivist
c10_report.echo.02.text: I remember the wind. You remember the people.

c10_report.echo.find.speaker: archivist
c10_report.echo.find.text: My echo stood behind the bait counter last winter and let the boats pay in spring. I remember the wind. She remembers the people. I will let her win.

c10_report.survey.lead.01.speaker: archivist
c10_report.survey.lead.01.text: There is a sealed survey in the Prefect’s file. He told us every world was taken.

c10_report.survey.lead.02.speaker: archivist
c10_report.survey.lead.02.text: Three slips. Reef Six has water and air, and a beacon there answers every call.

c10_report.survey.lead.03.speaker: archivist
c10_report.survey.lead.03.text: Sound Four has air, but no water at all. Reach Two has water and air, and it was visited three times.

c10_report.survey.01.speaker: archivist
c10_report.survey.01.text: He found a home. He hid it because the mission would have ended.

c10_report.survey.find.speaker: archivist
c10_report.survey.find.text: Reach 2: water, air and three separate surveys of empty ground. The Prefect found a home for the fleet and sealed it, because a home would have ended his mission.

c10_report.report.01.speaker: archivist
c10_report.report.01.text: Saren, you will remain yourself. You will have to remember being wrong.

c10_report.report.02.speaker: saren
c10_report.report.02.text: I have no procedure for that.

c10_report.report.find.speaker: archivist
c10_report.report.find.text: The danger, measured aboard our own ship. A home, surveyed empty three times. And three hundred and twelve people worth meeting. I have confirmed the report.

c10_report.recap.01.speaker: archivist
c10_report.recap.01.text: The report is confirmed. The fleet will measure an engine that does not exist, meet three hundred and twelve people, and learn of a home it was never told about.

c10_report.recap.02.speaker: archivist
c10_report.recap.02.text: I did not reconcile Saren. He will have to live with being wrong. So will I.

c10_report.out.01.speaker: archivist
c10_report.out.01.text: They are dangerous, and they sing. Go around.

c10_report.out.02.speaker: archivist
c10_report.out.02.text: Here are three hundred and twelve lives you should meet. And here is a world where we can live.

c10_report.out.03.speaker: helen
c10_report.out.03.text: Wick is adding a message for Tirel.

c10_report.out.05.speaker: autorick
c10_report.out.05.text: And now, the forecast for yesterday: sunny, with a chance of spaceships!

c10_report.out.06.speaker: steve
c10_report.out.06.text: The Vigil turned, and the fleet turned with it. At sunrise the Long Patience rose out of the bay, with Wick aboard. The whole coast watched it go. Somebody on the pier started to clap.

epilogue.in.01.speaker: choir
epilogue.in.01.text: Your memories are yours now. You need no more re-syncs.

epilogue.in.02.speaker: iris
epilogue.in.02.text: A face of my own. It will take getting used to.

epilogue.in.03.speaker: nora
epilogue.in.03.text: Thank you for helping us. I haven’t forgiven the kidnapping.

epilogue.neighbors.01.speaker: lyle
epilogue.neighbors.01.text: Two boys. Two fathers. We’ll have to learn.

epilogue.neighbors.02.speaker: pell
epilogue.neighbors.02.text: Dale has retired. Biscuit and I will maintain the route.

epilogue.neighbors.03.speaker: dale
epilogue.neighbors.03.text: Best news I’ve had in years.

epilogue.neighbors.04.speaker: gus
epilogue.neighbors.04.text: Kelp croissant. Someone wrote it in my notebook. I’m going to try it.

epilogue.neighbors.find.speaker: steve
epilogue.neighbors.find.text: Two fathers for Lyle’s boys, a new mail carrier for Biscuit, and a green croissant.

epilogue.bait.02.speaker: agnes
epilogue.bait.02.text: It is a competitive market. We are each other’s competition.

epilogue.bait.04.speaker: rook_copy
epilogue.bait.04.text: I’ll have to find out who that is.

epilogue.bait.find.speaker: steve
epilogue.bait.find.text: Two Mrs. Penhallows, one counter, and people are finally buying bait. One Adrian Rook stays. The other one leaves with the ship, to find out who he is.

epilogue.coffee.01.speaker: helen
epilogue.coffee.01.text: Steve, we’re home. There is coffee. Your father has labeled the paint.

epilogue.coffee.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.coffee.02.text: I’ll be there. Then Nora and I have somewhere to be.

epilogue.coffee.find.speaker: steve
epilogue.coffee.find.text: Mom and Dad are home. There’s a note on the table. And Nora is waiting at the door.

epilogue.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora
epilogue.talk.nora.1.01.text: I go back to the aquarium on Monday. The otter pups won’t remember me.

epilogue.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.nora.1.02.text: They’ll remember you. You’re the one who argues with the vet.

epilogue.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora
epilogue.talk.nora.1.03.text: Everybody argues with the vet. I just win.

epilogue.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora
epilogue.talk.nora.2.01.text: Somebody rearranged our kitchen. Everything is in alphabetical order.

epilogue.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.nora.2.02.text: That was Iris. She thought it looked tidy.

epilogue.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora
epilogue.talk.nora.2.03.text: The forks are under F. I’m leaving them there. It makes me laugh every morning.

epilogue.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora
epilogue.talk.nora.3.01.text: Admiral came to my whistle this morning. Straight out of the water.

epilogue.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.nora.3.02.text: Your second note went up again. I heard it from the pier.

epilogue.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora
epilogue.talk.nora.3.03.text: It always went up, Steve. Somebody else was whistling it wrong.

epilogue.talk.iris.1.01.speaker: iris
epilogue.talk.iris.1.01.text: I chose this face myself. It’s strange to be surprised by a mirror.

epilogue.talk.iris.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.iris.1.02.text: It suits you. It really does.

epilogue.talk.iris.1.03.speaker: iris
epilogue.talk.iris.1.03.text: Nora says the nose is too serious. I think that means she likes it.

epilogue.talk.iris.2.01.speaker: iris
epilogue.talk.iris.2.01.text: Carmen invited me to dinner on Sunday. Is that a trap?

epilogue.talk.iris.2.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.iris.2.02.text: With Carmen, dinner and a trap can be the same thing.

epilogue.talk.iris.2.03.speaker: iris
epilogue.talk.iris.2.03.text: Then I’ll bring bread. Nora says bread is always safe.

epilogue.talk.carmen.1.01.speaker: carmen
epilogue.talk.carmen.1.01.text: Six o’clock, Steve. Both of you. All of you.

epilogue.talk.carmen.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.carmen.1.02.text: You mean Iris is invited too?

epilogue.talk.carmen.1.03.speaker: carmen
epilogue.talk.carmen.1.03.text: Iris too. She sat at my table for five months. Now she can help with the dishes.

epilogue.talk.carmen.2.01.speaker: carmen
epilogue.talk.carmen.2.01.text: I kept your plate warm every Sunday. This Monday I am not throwing it out.

epilogue.talk.carmen.2.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.carmen.2.02.text: You never had to keep it, Carmen.

epilogue.talk.carmen.2.03.speaker: carmen
epilogue.talk.carmen.2.03.text: I know. That is why I did.

epilogue.talk.lyle.1.01.speaker: lyle
epilogue.talk.lyle.1.01.text: Ben has the school play tonight. He wants both of us in the front row.

epilogue.talk.lyle.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.lyle.1.02.text: Two Lyle Boones in one front row.

epilogue.talk.lyle.1.03.speaker: lyle
epilogue.talk.lyle.1.03.text: The other one learned the lines with him. I’m still learning mine.

epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.speaker: lyle_copy
epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.01.text: I still go to every game. Now we take turns driving.

epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.speaker: lyle
epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.02.text: He’s better at the snacks. I’m better at yelling at the umpire.

epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.speaker: lyle_copy
epilogue.talk.lyle_copy.1.03.text: We’re working on that. Both of us.

epilogue.talk.pell.1.01.speaker: pell
epilogue.talk.pell.1.01.text: Biscuit knows every porch on the route. I am still learning the gates.

epilogue.talk.pell.1.02.speaker: dale
epilogue.talk.pell.1.02.text: The blue gate on Harbor Street sticks. Kick it low.

epilogue.talk.pell.1.03.speaker: pell
epilogue.talk.pell.1.03.text: Kick it low. I have written that down.

epilogue.talk.dale.1.01.speaker: dale
epilogue.talk.dale.1.01.text: First free morning in thirty years. No mailbag, and no frozen bed.

epilogue.talk.dale.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.dale.1.02.text: What are you going to do instead, Dale?

epilogue.talk.dale.1.03.speaker: dale
epilogue.talk.dale.1.03.text: Sleep in a real bed. A warm one. Then go fishing.

epilogue.talk.gus.1.01.speaker: gus
epilogue.talk.gus.1.01.text: Try it, Steve. It’s green, but it’s honest.

epilogue.talk.gus.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.gus.1.02.text: Gus, this is actually really good.

epilogue.talk.gus.1.03.speaker: gus
epilogue.talk.gus.1.03.text: Don’t tell anyone. I have a reputation for plain bread.

epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.01.speaker: agnes_original
epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.01.text: She charges ten cents less than me for worms. On purpose.

epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.02.speaker: agnes
epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.02.text: Somebody kept this stall open for three years, Agnes.

epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.03.speaker: agnes_original
epilogue.talk.agnes_original.1.03.text: And in three years, nobody bought a single worm.

epilogue.talk.agnes.1.01.speaker: agnes
epilogue.talk.agnes.1.01.text: The ship left without me, Steven. I asked it to.

epilogue.talk.agnes.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.agnes.1.02.text: Won’t you miss the wind back home?

epilogue.talk.agnes.1.03.speaker: agnes
epilogue.talk.agnes.1.03.text: I have the wind on a spool. I would miss the people more.

epilogue.talk.rook.1.01.speaker: rook
epilogue.talk.rook.1.01.text: I have a lot of reports to write. Nobody is going to believe them.

epilogue.talk.rook.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.rook.1.02.text: Write them anyway, Adrian. Every word.

epilogue.talk.rook.1.03.speaker: rook
epilogue.talk.rook.1.03.text: That’s what June said. Word for word.

epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.01.speaker: rook_copy
epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.01.text: I’m going with the ship. I want to find out who I am when nobody is watching.

epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.02.text: Good luck out there. I mean it.

epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.03.speaker: rook_copy
epilogue.talk.rook_copy.1.03.text: Tell June I’m sorry about the voicemail.

epilogue.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: helen
epilogue.talk.helen.1.01.text: Your father leaves me a note every morning now. Today’s note says the kettle is labeled.

epilogue.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: steve
epilogue.talk.helen.1.02.text: Is the kettle actually labeled now?

epilogue.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: helen
epilogue.talk.helen.1.03.text: Kettle. In capital letters. I married a very thorough man.

epilogue.talk.helen.2.01.speaker: helen
epilogue.talk.helen.2.01.text: I keep hearing Wick’s phrase when I do the dishes.

epilogue.talk.helen.2.03.speaker: helen
epilogue.talk.helen.2.03.text: I never stopped, Steven. For a while I just had nobody to translate for.

epilogue.recap.01.speaker: steve
epilogue.recap.01.text: Bellwether kept its new neighbors. And on every ninth night now, the town puts lanterns on the water.

epilogue.out.01.speaker: steve
epilogue.out.01.text: The ring is in my pocket. We can start with coffee.

one_year.in.01.speaker: tomas
one_year.in.01.text: Welcome to I Told You So. This week, a respectful review of everyone who owes me an apology.

one_year.in.02.speaker: stephen
one_year.in.02.text: We should do a segment about who is the upgrade.

one_year.in.04.speaker: nora
one_year.in.04.text: Coffee for the morning hosts. Black, too strong, one for each of you.

one_year.newwind.01.speaker: stephen
one_year.newwind.01.text: Sounds like home. A new one.

one_year.talk.nora.1.01.speaker: nora
one_year.talk.nora.1.01.text: One year since the ninth night. Do you want to do something special?

one_year.talk.nora.1.02.speaker: steve
one_year.talk.nora.1.02.text: Coffee, and a real conversation. Same as every other day.

one_year.talk.nora.1.03.speaker: nora
one_year.talk.nora.1.03.text: Good answer. I was testing you.

one_year.talk.nora.2.01.speaker: nora
one_year.talk.nora.2.01.text: People keep asking about my ring. I tell them it’s a long story with a spaceship in it.

one_year.talk.nora.2.02.speaker: steve
one_year.talk.nora.2.02.text: It is a long story with a spaceship in it.

one_year.talk.nora.2.03.speaker: nora
one_year.talk.nora.2.03.text: I know. That’s why I love telling it.

one_year.talk.nora.3.01.speaker: nora
one_year.talk.nora.3.01.text: Admiral has a girlfriend now. She’s very loud, and she argues with everybody.

one_year.talk.nora.3.02.speaker: steve
one_year.talk.nora.3.02.text: That sounds like someone I know.

one_year.talk.nora.3.03.speaker: nora
one_year.talk.nora.3.03.text: Careful, Mercer. I still argue with everybody too.

one_year.talk.tomas.1.01.speaker: tomas
one_year.talk.tomas.1.01.text: Episode one. I already have three apologies lined up.

one_year.talk.tomas.1.02.speaker: steve
one_year.talk.tomas.1.02.text: Who is apologizing to you, Tomás?

one_year.talk.tomas.1.03.speaker: tomas
one_year.talk.tomas.1.03.text: The Sheriff, the mayor and my mother. My mother is still thinking about it.

one_year.talk.tomas.2.01.speaker: tomas
one_year.talk.tomas.2.01.text: I said it was nine nights. On my podcast. Every week. Everybody laughed.

one_year.talk.tomas.2.02.speaker: stephen
one_year.talk.tomas.2.02.text: You’re the one laughing now. Constantly. In our booth.

one_year.talk.stephen.1.01.speaker: stephen
one_year.talk.stephen.1.01.text: People still ask which of us is the original. I tell them I’m the morning one.

one_year.talk.stephen.1.02.speaker: steve
one_year.talk.stephen.1.02.text: I’m the morning one. You came in at noon yesterday.

one_year.talk.stephen.1.03.speaker: stephen
one_year.talk.stephen.1.03.text: You see? This is why we need a segment.

one_year.talk.stephen.2.01.speaker: stephen
one_year.talk.stephen.2.01.text: Dad wants both of us on the club radio this Thursday.

one_year.talk.stephen.2.02.speaker: steve
one_year.talk.stephen.2.02.text: He made us matching mugs for it, too.

postcredits.in.01.speaker: shaw
postcredits.in.01.text: Madam President. This time I didn’t build it.

postcredits.in.02.speaker: ward
postcredits.in.02.text: Evelyn, it is three in the morning.

postcredits.in.03.speaker: shaw
postcredits.in.03.text: You’re going to want to hear this.

postcredits.answer.01.speaker: helen
postcredits.answer.01.text: I know this language now. Give me a moment.

postcredits.talk.ward.1.01.speaker: ward
postcredits.talk.ward.1.01.text: Do you know how many people I had to wake up to get here?

postcredits.talk.ward.1.02.speaker: shaw
postcredits.talk.ward.1.02.text: All of them, I hope. They’ll want to hear this.

postcredits.talk.shaw.1.01.speaker: shaw
postcredits.talk.shaw.1.01.text: I run this listening station now. No fog machines. Real antennas.

postcredits.talk.shaw.1.02.speaker: ward
postcredits.talk.shaw.1.02.text: I signed that budget. I still don’t fully understand it.

postcredits.talk.shaw.1.03.speaker: shaw
postcredits.talk.shaw.1.03.text: Nobody does. That’s how you know it’s real science.

postcredits.talk.helen.1.01.speaker: helen
postcredits.talk.helen.1.01.text: I kept page twelve by my bed for a year. Just in case.

postcredits.talk.helen.1.02.speaker: shaw
postcredits.talk.helen.1.02.text: Lucky for us that you did.

postcredits.talk.helen.1.03.speaker: helen
postcredits.talk.helen.1.03.text: Not luck. An interpreter always keeps the last page.

lines: Bellwether. A fishing town on the Pacific coast.
Six thousand people, one radio station, and a lot of fog.
I’m Steve Mercer. For twelve years I ran the night shift at KBWR, the town radio station.
Nobody hears the night engineer. The night engineer hears everything.
My dad, Frank, taught me how to listen. Every sound has a source, he used to say. Go and find it.
Ham radio, every night. Strangers from all over the world, all of them his friends.
My mom, Helen, was an interpreter. Government work, rooms with no windows. She never talked about it.
She could hear what people meant, even when they said something else.
Eighteen months ago, they rowed out into the bay after dark. They said the water was making a sound.
They asked me to come along.
I said no. I had a shift.
In the morning, their boat drifted back to shore. Empty.
Nobody found them. That was eighteen months ago.
Mom called me from the boat that night. I kept her voicemail on a cassette. Most nights I play it at three in the morning. I don’t know what I’m listening for.
A year ago a company called Halcyon Media bought KBWR.
Three weeks ago they replaced me with a machine called DJ AutoRick. It reads yesterday’s weather.
And then there’s Nora. Nora Reyes runs the animals at the aquarium and argues with everybody, me included.
After the boat I went quiet. She pushed, then shouted, then stopped. Lately she’s been endlessly patient with me. I figured I’d worn her out.
So now I’m home in the mornings, with Dad’s old tape recorder and nothing left to fix.
This is the story of how I started counting nights.
Before the ship left, the Choir gave the copies one last gift. They don’t need the ninth night anymore.
More than two hundred of them stayed. Bellwether has a lot of new neighbors with familiar faces.
Iris chose a face of her own. People still say hello to the wrong Steve sometimes. We both say hello back.
Mom and Dad came home. Dad is back on the radio every Thursday.
Dad labels everything now. The paint, the radios, me.
I don’t play the old voicemail anymore.
The ring isn’t in the sock drawer anymore. Ask Nora where it is.
Nora argues with me again. About everything. I missed it more than I can say.
KBWR has live hosts again. Two of them.
Stephen and I still argue about which one of us is the upgrade.
One year after the ninth night, a package arrived at the station.
